examQuestions.questionText: What does a Q in video resolution names, such as QXGA, refer to?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Although the Q stands for quad, the pixel count for each axis is only doubled, resulting in four times as many total pixels.

answers.textAnswer: Both the horizontal and vertical components of the resolution have been quadrupled.
The resolution is cut to one-fourth.
Both the horizontal and vertical components of the resolution have been doubled.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding a monitor’s refresh rate?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The maximum allowable refresh rate does tend to be affected by the resolution you choose in the operating system. The refresh rate is most often expressed in cycles per second (Hz), not millions of cycles per second (MHz). You must usually select the refresh rate that you want from the display settings dialogs, not through the monitor’s built-in menu system, although the monitor can often tell you the refresh rate that you’re using. Finally, both the monitor and adapter must agree on the refresh rate you select. If either device does not support a particular refresh rate, such a rate cannot be used.

answers.textAnswer: As long as the graphics adapter can refresh the image at a particular rate, the attached monitor can accommodate that refresh rate.
The refresh rate is normally expressed in MHz.
The refresh rate is normally selected by using the controls on the front panel of the monitor.
As you lower the resolution, the maximum refresh rate allowed tends to increase.

examQuestions.questionText: If you are unable to display a given resolution on a monitor, which of the following might explain why?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.

The amount of memory installed on a graphics adapter is directly related to how many pixels can be displayed at one time and how many colors the pixels can be set to. Monitors don’t have memory installed in them. LCDs, not CRTs, have a single, fixed resolution called the native resolution. You might be limited to a particular refresh rate because the resolution is too high, but the refresh rate is automatically adjusted down, if necessary, when you select a resolution.

answers.textAnswer: The graphics adapter does not have enough memory installed.
The video display unit does not have enough memory installed.
You are using an LCD with a single, fixed resolution.
You have the refresh rate set too high.

examQuestions.questionText: When approaching an older LCD panel from the side, you don’t realize there is actually an image displayed on it until you are almost in front of it. Which options might explain why you could not detect the image from the side? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3},{answer-5}.
Older LCD panels might have employed a passive-matrix addressing for their pixels, resulting in a poorer viewing angle than that created by active-matrix LCD panels. Additionally, privacy filters intentionally limit the angle of screen visibility by changing the light’s polarization when viewed from the side. Antiglare filters might unintentionally do the same thing.

answers.textAnswer: Older LCDs were equipped with a motion sensor.
Multiple monitors are in use, and the LCD is the secondary monitor, resulting in its poor oblique visibility.
The user has a privacy filter in place.
The monitor employs active-matrix pixel addressing.
It is a passive-matrix LCD panel.

examQuestions.questionText: What might cause your display to appear in a resolution of 640 x 480?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.

Safe Mode disables as many nonessential drivers and services as possible. One of the nonessential drivers it disables is the driver for the graphics adapter. Windows uses its standard VGA driver to control the graphics adapter while you are in Safe Mode. Another reason for defaulting back to standard VGA is that you might have a corrupt or incorrect driver for your adapter.

answers.textAnswer: You have your resolution set to SVGA
You added memory to your graphics adapter but have not informed the BIOS of the new memory.
You have your resolution set to XGA.
You have booted into Safe Mode.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following would be the best choice as a personal display technology if a user wants to save desk space and not have to deal with interference from nearby speakers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
LCDs do not have electron guns that are aimed by magnets as CRTs do. This difference makes LCDs more compatible with nearby speaker magnets. Additionally, the cathode ray tube for which CRT monitors are named is a rather bulky component, requiring more desk space to accommodate the CRT’s cabinet. Projectors are not common personal display devices; they are used more in group environments. HDMI is a standard for connecting display devices, not a type of display device.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following have been common methods to backlight an LCD monitor? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-5}.
Early LCD monitors featured one or more fluorescent bulbs that were used to produce light that shone through the LCD panel. Modern LCD monitors have LED panels to generate the light, the advantage being that there is now a separate LED for each picture element instead of a common light source for the entire monitor.

examQuestions.questionText: Which statement about LCD monitors is most accurate?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
TN-based LCDs are less expensive and offer better response times for the money. TN, not IPS, technology suffers from color shifts when viewed at wide angles.

answers.textAnswer: The concept of refresh rate has no meaning with regard to LCDs.
Those based on IPS technology suffer from color shifts when viewed from the edges.
Those based on TN technology are preferred by gamers.
The electric fields generate a magnetic field that eventually must be removed.

examQuestions.questionText: Which video technology has a resolution of 1280&#215;1024?
examQuestions.explanation: SXGA has a resolution of 1280&#215;1024. Consult Table 4.2 for the resolutions that characterize other technologies.

examQuestions.questionText: What is contrast ratio?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Contrast ratio is a selling point for LCDs. Higher contrast ratios mean darker blacks and brighter whites. The measure of luminance between adjacent pixels is known as contrast, not contrast ratio.

answers.textAnswer: The ratio of luminance between the darkest and lightest colors that can be displayed
A term that was used with CRTs but has no meaning with LCDs
The ratio of luminance between two adjacent pixels
Something that can be corrected through degaussing

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following display types physically creates the image displayed in a manner most similar to OLED displays?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Both OLED and plasma displays use electrodes to excite the material in a sealed chamber to produce light. Each in its own way uses that light to create red, green, or blue light within individual subpixels. All LCD panels form images that require an external light source to view.

examQuestions.questionText: On which properties tab do you select the refresh rate to use between the graphics adapter and monitor in Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Although it’s true that you must start with the Display Settings dialog box, which ironically shows a single tab labeled Monitor, and that you subsequently click the Advanced Settings button, the Monitor properties tab is where you select the refresh rate. The Adapter tab in those same properties pages has no selection for refresh rate.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following results can occur with improper display settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If your monitor allows you to change the resolution, it might not actually allow you to change the resolution. As confusing as that sounds, your monitor might maintain its optimal hardware resolution, such as an LCD’s native resolution, and force you to scroll to see any pixels created by the chosen software resolution that it cannot fit on the hardware screen at that particular moment.

answers.textAnswer: The graphics adapter automatically chooses to use the highest supported resolution.
You might have to scroll to see parts of the Desktop.
The mouse cursor changes or permanently disappears.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the single, fixed resolution of an LCD called?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
An LCD’s native resolution is the single, fixed resolution that provides optimal clarity.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is possible to do with multimonitor settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The multimonitor feature allows two monitors to display exactly the same thing (clone) or to extend your Desktop onto the second monitor. There is no need to use one adapter to achieve this result. In fact, the two adapters don’t even have to use the same expansion-bus architecture. The two cards must, however, use the same graphics-adapter driver.

answers.textAnswer: Connect multiple monitors to your computer only by using a graphics adapter with two video interfaces.
Cause two different Desktops to merge onto the same monitor.
Connect two laptops together so they display the same Desktop.
Display different parts of your Desktop on different monitors.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following types of LCD has the best performance characteristics?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Active matrix is a superior technology to passive matrix. Dual scan is merely an enhanced form of passive matrix, but it is not on par with active matrix. Dual matrix isn’t an LCD type.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following resolutions is an example of a 16:10 aspect ratio?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Dividing 16 by 10 produces a value of 1.6. Dividing the first number of a 16:10 resolution by the second number always results in 1.6. Resolutions with a 4:3 aspect ratio produce the value 1.333, while 5:4 resolutions such as 1280 x 1024 produce the value 1.25.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is true with regard to the difference between refresh rate and frame rate?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Regardless of how high the refresh rate, which measures the total number of all screens of information that is displayed per second, is on a monitor, only the number of unique frames in the content being played back during each second is considered when computing frame rate. Each frame represents a complete screen of information.

answers.textAnswer: Monitors are rated only in refresh rate or frame rate, but never both.
Content is recorded at a specific refresh rate, and output on a monitor at a specific frame rate.
Refresh rate can be higher than frame rate, in terms of screens of information displayed per second, when considered for any given video output.
The frame rate of a monitor is adjustable, while the refresh rate is fixed.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the unit of measure used by manufacturers of projectors to indicate the brightness of their product?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A lumen is a unit of measure for the total amount of visible light that the projector gives off, based solely on what the human eye can perceive.

examQuestions.questionText: Which video technology has a resolution of 1280 x 1024?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
SXGA has a resolution of 1280 x 1024. Consult Table 4.2 for the resolutions that characterize other technologies.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to plug a keyboard into the back of a computer. You know that you need to plug the keyboard cable into a PS/2 port. Which style of port is the PS/2?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A PS/2 port is also known as a mini-DIN 6 connector.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum speed of USB 2.0 in Mbps?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The USB 2.0 spec provides for a maximum speed of 480 megabits per second (Mbps—not megabytes per second, or MBps).

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is both an input and an output device?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Touchscreens are used as standard displays, making them output devices, but they are also used as input devices because they translate the user’s touch to a point on a two-dimensional plane, which is then transferred to the software interface to replace such stimuli as the combination of a mouse movement and click. Webcams, motion sensors, and touchpads are used only for input.

examQuestions.questionText: What peripheral port type was originally developed by Apple and is currently regarded as the optimal interface for digital video transfers?
examQuestions.explanation:
C
The IEEE 1394 standard provides for greater data transfer speeds, increased power, and the ability to send memory addresses as well as data through a serial port. USB 3.0 proves to threaten more competition in these areas, but USB 2.0 could not compare to the overall performance of IEEE 1394.

examQuestions.questionText: What peripheral port type is expandable using a hub, operates at 1.5MBps, and is used to connect various devices (from printers to cameras) to PCs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
USB hubs are used to connect multiple peripherals to one computer through a single port. They support data transfer rates as high as 12Mbps, or 1.5MBps (for USB 1.1, which is the option listed here).

examQuestions.questionText: Which peripheral port type was designed to transfer data at higher speeds over a D-sub interface?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The IEEE 1284 standard specifies that the ECP parallel port use a DMA channel and that the buffer be able to transfer data at higher speeds to printers.

examQuestions.questionText: The surround sound mode known as 5.1 employs how many speakers when only one is used for each channel?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The description 5.1 refers to six channels of audio. The 5 in the name refers collectively to the single center channel, the right and left front channels, and the right and left rear channels. The 1 in the name refers to the single LFE channel connected to the subwoofer.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following display interfaces is equivalent to DisplayPort with PCIe added in?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Intel and Apple collaborated on Thunderbolt to add PCIe to VESA’s DisplayPort and to make the resulting interface smaller and less expensive to connect.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following interfaces allows audio to be sent out over the same cabling infrastructure as video?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
HDMI is a digital interface and cabling specification that allows digital audio to be carried over the same cable as video.

examQuestions.questionText: How do you connect a DVI-A interface on a peripheral to a DVI-D interface on the computer?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Such a connection should not be made. DVI-I cables act like universal cables; they can connect two DVI-A interfaces or two DVI-D interfaces with adapters. Natively, they are used to connect two DVI-I interfaces, both of which are configured as either analog or digital. They are unable to convert the analog signal to a digital one, however. Analog and digital DVI interfaces are too disparate to interconnect.

answers.textAnswer: With a cable that is terminated on one end with a DVI-A connector and on the other end with a DVI-D connector.
You wouldn’t interconnect those two interfaces.

examQuestions.questionText: What kind of device uses unique physical traits of the user to authenticate their access to a secure system or location?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Biometric input devices scan a physical trait of the user, such as voice, fingerprint, and retina, for authentication purposes when the user attempts to access computer systems and other property.

examQuestions.questionText: Why might you use a KVM switch?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
KVM switches are ideal when you have multiple computers situated near one another and do not want to commit the extra desk space to each computer having its own keyboard, mouse, and monitor.

answers.textAnswer: You have multiple Ethernet devices that need to communicate with one another.
You need to be able to switch the voltage supplied to a particular device.
You have a printer that is not attached to the network but you want multiple computers to be able to print to it.
You have more than one server and don’t want to buy certain external peripherals separately for each.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of input device employs roughly the same connector as the original AT keyboard?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
MIDI devices use a 5-pin DIN connector similar to the one used with the original AT keyboard.

examQuestions.questionText: What can you use to convert video to a format that can be uploaded to the Internet, among other things?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A video capture card is used to convert raw video input to a format that can be shared electronically. Although many TV tuner cards provide this functionality, it is their video-capture component that gives them this capability. Any adapter that is strictly a TV tuner cannot capture video.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not an example of a connector for a standard peripheral input device?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Multimedia input devices, not standard input devices, use 1/8" jacks. Standard input devices include human interface devices, such as keyboards and mice. The other three options can be used for such devices.

examQuestions.questionText: What category of adapter would you need to install to equip a system with one or more USB ports?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Interfaces such as USB ports are considered input/output ports. If you have to add USB capability to a computer, an I/O adapter with USB ports on it would meet the need.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of adapter has an RJ-11 jack built in?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Modems have RJ-11 jacks to provide an interface to the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN). The modular jacks that Ethernet NICs have are known as RJ-45 jacks.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of pointing device features a ball and buttons on the top and a flat, steady surface on the bottom?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A trackball is a sort of stationary upside-down mouse that has the ball for movement detection on the top of the device along with the keys. The ball is actuated by the thumb or fingers, not by moving the device along a flat surface or mouse pad. Trackballs are ideal where desk space is limited. Touchpads feature a touch-sensing surface with no ball for movement, while trackpad is a rarer term meaning the same.

examQuestions.questionText: VGA-based video technologies use what type of signal between the adapter and monitor?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
VGA signals are analog, uncompressed, component signals that carry all of the video information for all three components of the original RGB signal.

examQuestions.questionText: Which category of adapters includes NICs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Network interface cards are considered to be a form of communications adapter.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following uses would not require a custom configuration for a PC?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Windows 7 computer can be built as a normal system with a 2TB or 3TB drive. WHS 2011 needs a home server PC. A type of CAD/CAM workstation capable of CNC crafts the rims. A home theater PC is an ideal choice to take the place of both the BD player and DVR.

answers.textAnswer: A computer running Windows 7 Ultimate with 1TB of data and 250GB of applications installed
A design computer used to drive a lathe that makes automotive rims
A computer to replace a BD player and DVR

examQuestions.questionText: All of the following systems benefit from increased RAM except ___________________. (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-4}.
Virtualization and graphic design workstations benefit from as much RAM as can be installed. Home theater PCs and gaming PCs do not require a large amount of temporary storage of instructions and data. They are more about the rapid movement of graphical data toward an output device.

examQuestions.questionText: Marcus, a network technician, has been asked to build an HTPC for his manager. Which of the following is not a common requirement that Marcus should consider for this custom configuration?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Home theater PCs are based on the mini-ITX motherboard and have their own form factor, HTPC, a more compact form factor than chassis made for micro-ATX boards.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to set up a workstation for a new graphic designer at your company. Which of the following is not a requirement for a graphic design workstation?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Graphics design and CAD/CAM design workstations do not require a fast hard drive because the artist works with static images that do not stream from the drive. However, RAM is needed to hold the highly detailed, sometimes 3D, artwork before saving, and a powerful processor is required for implementing complex algorithms on a small amount of information during rendering. High-end video is necessary for assisting in the rendering and display of the images.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following system types does not require a CPU enhancement of any sort?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A/V editing workstations require video enhancements and a hard drive capable of storing a large quantity of data and accessing it quickly. The other system types require faster or more plentiful processors.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following system types does not benefit from video enhancements?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The clients of the home server PC that use the server for streaming video content might benefit from enhanced video, but the server will not.

examQuestions.questionText: Danielle has been asked to configure virtualization at her company. She recommends that her manager buy multicore processors. What justification should she give as to why virtualization workstations require as many CPU cores as possible?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Virtual machines do not imply virtual processing. The data storage, processing cycles, and RAM usage are all real. The separate hard drive and chassis for each operating system are virtual. The other answers all have at least one fundamental problem with their logic. CPU cores are not installed in virtual machines but in CPU packages within physical machines. CPU cores do not take over for each other. There is no fault tolerance among them. Storing data is the job of RAM, which should also be maximized for virtualization workstations.

answers.textAnswer: Each virtual machine has one or more cores installed directly in it.
Each virtual machine makes use of actual CPU resources for processing instructions and data.
Fault tolerance dictates that if one CPU core fails, there should be one or more in line to take its place.
Because each guest operating system runs in its own space, multiple cores are required to store the collective data.

examQuestions.questionText: Your friend Joe plays video game tournaments online, and he read in an online forum that he should overclock his CPU for better speed. You tell him that if he does that, he needs better cooling. Why is high-end cooling a requirement for gaming PCs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The processors found in a gaming PC are many, and the CPU is often overclocked. Such a configuration generates too much heat for conventional cooling to dissipate before the system is damaged. These machines don’t have unusual hard-drive requirements. The cooling has no effect on external controllers, and sound cards don’t generate much heat, but analog would certainly generate more than digital.

answers.textAnswer: Gaming PCs tend to overclock their CPUs and run multiple high-performance GPUs.
Gaming controllers have components for tactile realism that generate copious amounts of heat.
Digital sound cards generate more heat than analog sound cards.
Placing that many hard drives in such a small space generates too much heat.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of system simply needs to run standard versions of Windows and desktop applications?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Thick clients are standard desktop PCs. They stand in contrast to systems with specialized requirements, such as the remaining options.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following descriptions most closely matches that of a thin client?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Although not all thin clients are devoid of local processing capability, some are. High-resolution graphics are not a requirement, but thin clients do require a system unit with a NIC.

answers.textAnswer: A high-resolution monitor, keyboard, and mouse
A computer with a low-profile case
A dumb terminal with a NIC

examQuestions.questionText: You have recently installed a home server PC in your home so that all of your family members can share media. You have a router and network cabling that supports Gigabit Ethernet. Why should you equip a home server PC with a gigabit NIC?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Optimally, the server should communicate across a link that is the aggregate of all client links, but at the very least, the server’s link should be a faster one to alleviate the potential bottleneck when all clients try to access the server simultaneously.

answers.textAnswer: All systems, including the server, should communicate at the same speed.
The server should not be allowed to communicate at the higher speeds of the rest of the network or it will be overused.
The server should exceed the communication speed of the clients to avoid a bottleneck.
The operating system that home servers run is not compatible with Gigabit Ethernet.

examQuestions.questionText: An engineer on your network is complaining that his CAD workstation is slow and he wants a processor upgrade. Which of the following reasons is justification for having a powerful processor in a CAD/CAM workstation?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Quite simply, the rendering of 2D and 3D graphics makes use of complex algorithms that need all of the processing power they can get to remain usable. CAD workstations deal with static images, not streaming video. Manufacturing equipment is generally slower than computers used for the design phase. CAD workstations call for high-end video, which includes graphics adapters with GPUs often more powerful than the system’s CPU.

answers.textAnswer: Only powerful processors can stream graphical information efficiently.
Manufacturing equipment is generally faster than design equipment, which needs faster processors to keep up.
Graphics adapters used in CAD/CAM do not have their own processors, so the CPU performs this job as well.
The algorithms used in rendering graphics can be processor intensive.

examQuestions.questionText: A video editor at your company wants a second monitor, claiming that only having one monitor limits her ability to work. Why do A/V editing workstations benefit from more than one monitor?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Editors of this type of media have numerous controls and timelines to track. These constructs often lie along the bottom of the application and run horizontally. Subsequent monitors allow the editor to spread out without shrinking the view excessively.

answers.textAnswer: Their software often has enough controls across their width that one monitor seems cramped.
While one graphics adapter works on one rendering project, the other can simply display a normal desktop.
Once the editing is complete, the second monitor is used to present the results to others on the team.
Additional monitors are used for remote collaboration among other editors.

examQuestions.questionText: You are configuring a virtualization workstation for your home use. Which of the following is required for your new system?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Maximum RAM and CPU cores are the primary requirements for such systems. Although there are multiple guest operating systems, generally there is but one host to those guests. File sharing may be a service the administrator decides to offer, and multiple NICs might prove advantageous with virtual machines that are popular among the clients, but these workstations do not require either.

examQuestions.questionText: Robin has been asked to lead training for new technicians at a local PC distributor specializing in gaming PCs. For which one of the following should she not recommend upgraded parts?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Gaming PCs are not known for requiring fault tolerance or data persistence. RAID arrays, therefore, are generally not included. The other components are a benefit for gaming PCs, however.

examQuestions.questionText: Maria is setting up an HTPC and wants to know which type of video cables to purchase. Which of the following is the recommended video output technology for home theater PCs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Because of its exceptional capabilities of digital video and audio output as well as its potential for support of future standards, HDMI is the home-theater video output technology of choice. Neither DVI nor component video (YCbCr and YPbPr) can make the same claims. WUXGA is a resolution of 1920 x 1200 and not a video output technology.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a common feature of a standard thick client?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
These standard systems do not have any special requirements, only that they can run Windows and desktop applications.

answers.textAnswer: Has as much RAM installed as is possible
Can run a full version of Windows

examQuestions.questionText: Your network uses thin clients. A new technician is amazed that the computers have no hard drives and asks, "If the operating system is not resident on the client, where is it found?"
examQuestions.explanation: Clients request services of servers. Thin clients can request software services from their servers, whether in the form of running the software and passing the results to the client or passing the code of the software to the client to be executed by its processor and kept only in RAM.

answers.textAnswer: On a DVD inserted at bootup
On the server for session-by-session client use
Embedded in a flash module on the motherboard

examQuestions.questionText: Peter is configuring a home server PC. Which of the following should be his least-important priority to include in his home server PC?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Additional RAM in the home server PC offers no advantage for the performance of the server past a certain point. The tasks the server is asked to perform do not require high performance.

examQuestions.questionText: Which connector type is used for a modem connection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
While RJ-45 is for data, the RJ-11 connector is for a phone or modem connection.

examQuestions.questionText: Which wiring combination creates a crossover cable?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
When the same standard is used on both ends it is a straight through cable and when different standards are used on each end it is a crossover cable

examQuestions.questionText: Which fiber standard will operate up to 550 meters?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
1000BaseLX operates at 1 Gb and will go up to 550 meters.

examQuestions.questionText: Which the following is NOT a fiber connector?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A BNC connector is used with coaxial cabling not fiber.

examQuestions.questionText: Which signaling method uses a single channel in the coaxial cable?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Coax supports both baseband and broadband signaling. Baseband signaling means that a single channel is carried through the coax, and broadband refers to multiple channels on the coax

examQuestions.questionText: What type of coaxial cable is used is the type traditionally used in Thin Ethernet networks?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
RG-58 is the type traditionally used in Thin Ethernet networks (10Base2). Thick coax (10Base5) utilized RG-8, was used primarily for backbone cable.

examQuestions.questionText: Which if the following is a Class B address?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
IP addresses with a first octet value between 128-191 are Class B addresses

examQuestions.questionText: Which twisted pair cable category will has a maximum speed of 100 Mbps?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
CAT5 transmits data at speeds up to 100 Mbps and was used with Fast Ethernet (operating at 100 Mbps) with a transmission range of 100 meters.

examQuestions.questionText: Which cabling type offers no protection against EMI or RFI?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Unshielded twisted Pair (UTP) lacks the shielding required. YTH either types either have the shielding or are impervious to EMI and RFI.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following network devices receives network traffic and makes a decision on whether to send it on based on the destination hardware address?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Because bridges work at the Data Link layer, they are aware of only hardware (MAC) addresses. They are not aware of and do not deal with IP addresses. Bridges are more intelligent than repeaters, but they are unable to move data across multiple networks simultaneously.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician installed a UTP splitter on one of your network segments that has CAT6e cable. What is the maximum speed supported by this connection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
An Ethernet splitter will take the incoming signal on two pairs and then split it, so on the output end it produces two sets of signals using two pairs each. Because of this, Ethernet splitters are limited to 100Mbps connections. It is not recommended that you use Ethernet splitters on a network. If you need to connect multiple computers using UTP, use a hub or a switch.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing a fiber-optic cable between two buildings. To install the cable, you must run it through a conduit between the buildings, and access to the conduit is not easy. Before you run the cable, you want to ensure it’s working properly. Which tool should you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Cable testers are indispensable tools for any network technician. Usually you would use a cable tester before you install a cable to make sure it works. Of course, you can test them after they’ve been run as well.

examQuestions.questionText: You are using your laptop on the company network. In your web browser, you type in www.google.com and press Enter. The computer will not find Google. You open the browser on your phone, and using your cellular connection, you can open Google without a problem. Your laptop finds internal servers and can print without any issues. What is the most likely reason you can’t open Google?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Domain Name System (DNS) server is responsible for resolving host names, such as www.google.com, to IP addresses to enable communication. If it’s not working properly or you can’t connect to it, you won’t be able to browse the Internet using friendly website names.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician needs to run a network cable to a remote building, which is approximately 15 kilometers from his base station. He’s not sure if any cable will span that distance. What is the maximum distance of SMF cable?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Single-mode fiber (SMF) can provide data throughput rates of 10Gbps at a distance of 40 kilometers.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to install a run of RG-59 cable from one end of a building to the other. What is the maximum distance for this type of cable run?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
RG-59 network cable can run for about 228 meters (750 feet). The slightly thicker RG-6 can run for about 304 meters (1,000 feet).

examQuestions.questionText: Which one of the following TCP/IP protocols was designed as a replacement for Telnet?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Secure Shell (SSH) can be used to set up a secure Telnet session for remote logins or for remotely executing programs and transferring files. Because it’s secure, it was originally designed to be a replacement for the unsecure telnet command.

examQuestions.questionText: In IPv4, what is the function of the subnet mask?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Computers are able to differentiate where the network ID ends and the host address begins through the use of a subnet mask.

answers.textAnswer: It tells hosts where to route packets.
It differentiates between the network ID and host ID.
It determines which subnet the host is on.
It masks external networks from the host.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol allows a user to log into a remote computer and manage files as if they were logged in locally?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Telnet lets users log into another machine and “see” the remote computer in a window on their screen. Although this vision is text only, the user can manage files on that remote machine just as if they were logged in locally.

examQuestions.questionText: You are given a network configuration of 155.100.63.0/26 from your ISP. When you configure your network hosts, what subnet mask should you assign them?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A CIDR shorthand notation of /26 corresponds to the subnet mask 255.255.255.192.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Wi-Fi standard specifies a maximum of 54Mbps transmissions in the 2.4GHz frequency range?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
802.11g specifies a maximum of 54Mbps transmissions in the 2.4GHz frequency range.

examQuestions.questionText: You have just installed a wireless 802.11ac network for a client. The IT manager is concerned about competitors intercepting the wireless signal from outside the building. Which tool is designed to test how far your wireless signal travels?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A wireless locator or a Wi-Fi analyzer can be either a handheld hardware device or specialized software that is installed on a laptop and whose purpose is to detect and analyze Wi-Fi signals. It can detect where signals are strong or weak to determine whether there are potential security issues.

examQuestions.questionText: Some of your network users are concerned about submitting confidential information to an online website. What should you tell them?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Internet traffic is not encrypted by default. Websites that are secure and encrypt their transmissions will start with HTTPS://rather than HTTP://. These sites can be trusted to encrypt the data, and their identity is verified.

answers.textAnswer: It’s fine, because all Internet traffic is encrypted.
If the website address starts with TLS://, it should be OK to submit confidential information to a trusted site.
If the website address starts with HTTPS://, it should be OK to submit confidential information to a trusted site.
Don’t ever submit confidential information to any online website.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP Internet layer protocol is responsible for delivering error messages if communication between two computers fails?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The main Internet layer protocol is Internet Protocol (IP), and it’s the workhorse of TCP/IP. Another key protocol at this layer is Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP), which is responsible for delivering error messages. If you’re familiar with the ping utility, you’ll know that it utilizes ICMP to send and receive packets.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of IPv6 address identifies a single node on the network?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
There are three types of addresses in IPv6: unicast, anycast, and multicast. A unicast address identifies a single node on the network. An anycast address refers to one that has been assigned to multiple nodes. A multicast address is one used by multiple hosts.

examQuestions.questionText: You are configuring a wireless 802.11n router for a small network. When setting it up, which security option should you choose?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Of the wireless encryption methods listed, WPA2 is the newest and most secure. Some routers offer WPA2 Enterprise, which is a great choice as well.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol, developed by Microsoft, allows users to connect to remote computers and run programs on them?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Developed by Microsoft, the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) allows users to connect to remote computers and run programs on them. When you use RDP, you see the desktop of the computer you’ve signed into on your screen. It’s like you’re really there, even though you’re not.

examQuestions.questionText: What port number does the SSH protocol use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Secure Shell (SSH) can be used to set up a secure Telnet session for remote logins or for remotely executing programs and transferring files. SSH uses port 22.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following IP addresses is not routable on the Internet?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Private IP addresses are not routable on the Internet. The private IP address range for class A networks is 10.0.0.0/8.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a desktop computer that is behaving erratically on the network. The wired connection will often disconnect without warning. Which tool should you use to troubleshoot the network adapter?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A loopback plug is for testing the ability of a network adapter to send and receive. The plug gets plugged into the NIC, and then a loopback test is performed using troubleshooting software. You can then tell whether the card is working properly.

examQuestions.questionText: Your company just expanded and is leasing additional space in an adjacent office building. You need to extend the network to the new building. Fortunately, there is a conduit between the two. You estimate that the cable you need to run will be about 300 meters long. What type of cable should you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
UTP cables are limited to 100 meters, so CAT5 and CAT7 will not work. You need fiber, and multimode fiber (MMF) can span distances of 300 meters.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing network cabling in a highly secure facility. The cables need to be immune to electronic eavesdropping. What type of cable should you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Fiber-optic cabling uses pulses of light instead of electric voltages to transmit data, so it is immune to electrical interference and to wiretapping.

examQuestions.questionText: Which network device is designed to be a security guard, blocking malicious data from entering your network?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A firewall is a hardware or software solution that serves as your network’s security guard. Firewalls can protect you in two ways: they protect your network resources from hackers lurking in the dark corners of the Internet, and they can simultaneously prevent computers on your network from accessing undesirable content on the Internet.

examQuestions.questionText: You are manually configuring TCP/IP hosts on the network. What configuration parameter specifies the address of the router that enables Internet access?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The default gateway is the address to the network’s router, which will allow the host to communicate with hosts not on the local network.

examQuestions.questionText: A senior administrator calls you and tells you that she is working from home and trying to use RDP, but it won’t let her. What port do you need to ensure is open on the firewall to grant her access?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) allows users to connect to remote computers and run programs on them. It uses port 3389.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to configure a wireless router for an office network. The office manager wants new devices to be able to automatically join the network and announce their presence to other networked devices. Which service should you enable to allow this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) is a standard designed to simplify the process of connecting devices to a network and to enable those devices to automatically announce their presence to other devices on the network.

examQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a computer with an IPv6 address that is in the FE80::/10 range. Which of the following statements are true? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
Addresses in the FE80::/10 range are link local unicast addresses. A link local address is assigned to each IPv6 interface but is not routable on the Internet. If this is the only address the host has, it will not be able to get on the Internet.

answers.textAnswer: The computer will not be able to get on the Internet.
The computer will be able to get on the Internet.
The computer is configured with a link local unicast address.
The computer is configured with a global unicast address.

examQuestions.questionText: You have set up your web server to function as an FTP server as well. Users on the Internet complain that they are not able to access the server using FTP clients. What port number are they trying to access the server on?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is optimized for downloading files from servers. It uses port 21.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol allows you to access data such as employee phone numbers and email addresses that are stored within an information directory?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is a directory services protocol based on the X.500 standard. LDAP is designed to access information stored in an information directory typically known as an LDAP directory or LDAP database. This often includes employee phone numbers and email addresses.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing a new network and working in a wiring closet. You need to attach several network cables to a 110 block. Which tool should you use to perform this task?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you’re working on a larger network installation, you might use a punchdown tool. It’s not a testing tool but one that allows you to connect (that is, punch down) the exposed ends of a wire into wiring harnesses, such as a 110 block.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following Internet connection types offers the fastest download speeds?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Fiber-optic broadband Internet offers fast speeds (often in the 1Gbps range) but is also the most expensive.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to create several UTP cables from a roll of bulk cable. Your company uses the T568B standard. What is the correct order for wires in the connectors?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The correct order for a T568B cable is white/orange, orange, white/green, blue, white/blue, green, white/brown, brown.

answers.textAnswer: White/orange, orange, white/green, blue, white/blue, green, white/brown, brown
White/orange, orange, white/green, green, white/blue, blue, white/brown, brown
White/orange, green, white/green, blue, white/blue, orange, white/brown, brown
Orange, white/orange, white/green, blue, white/blue, green, white/brown, brown

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing network cable that will support digital cable television signals. What type of cable should you install?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Cable television installations typically use either RG-6 or RG-59 cable. RG-6 is slightly thicker, can run longer distances, and supports digital signals. RG-59 is suited only for analog TV signals.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol uses TCP ports 137–139 and 445 by default?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Server Message Block (SMB) is a protocol used to provide shared access to files, printers, and other network resources. It uses TCP ports 137–139 and 445.

examQuestions.questionText: For IPv6, which of the following statements are not true? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
Each IPv6 interface can and often does have multiple addresses assigned to it. IPv6 is backward compatible with IPv4.

answers.textAnswer: Each IPv6 interface can have only one address.
Each IPv6 interface is required to have a link local address.
IPv6 addresses are incompatible with IPv4 networks.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following network architecture devices operate at Layer 1 of the OSI model? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
A hub is a device used to link several computers together. Hubs are simple devices that possess no real intelligence, and they work at Layer 1 of the OSI model. Extenders simply allow a signal to propagate for a longer distance, and they also work at Layer 1. Switches are Layer 2 devices, and routers work at Layer 3.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to replace a faulty 250-foot section of RG-6 cable, but all you have available is RG-59. Which of the following statements is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
RG-6 and RG-59 can, in many cases, be used interchangeably. RG-6 is a better choice because it supports digital signals and has a longer range (304 meters or 1,000 feet). RG-59 can run up to 228 meters (750 feet). Both have impedance of 75 ohms, and both use BNC connectors or F-connectors.

answers.textAnswer: The replacement cable will not work because the distance exceeds RG-59 specifications.
The replacement cable will not work because RG-6 and RG-59 use different connectors.
The replacement cable will not work because RG-6 and RG-59 have different impedance.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to design a new network that requires 10Gbps transmission speeds. Which cable types will meet the minimum specifications? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-4}.
Multimode fiber and UTP CAT6 and newer support 10Gbps transmission speeds.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol was developed by Apple and used to transfer files between computers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Apple Filing Protocol (AFP) was developed by Apple as a file transfer protocol similar to FTP and Server Message Block (SMB). It was the default file transfer protocol on Mac OS until Apple changed to SMB2 in 2013.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following IPv6 addresses is equivalent to 127.0.0.1 in IPv4?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
127.0.0.7 is the loopback address, used to ping the local network interface. The IPv6 equivalent is ::1.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is configuring a wireless 802.11ac router for a home network. For security purposes, he enables the firewall. He wants to configure it so that if a computer makes an outbound request on a specific port, subsequent inbound traffic on that port would be allowed through the firewall. Which option does he need to configure to manage these settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Port triggering allows traffic to enter the network on a specific port after a computer makes an outbound request on that specific port. For example, if a computer on your internal network makes an outbound Telnet request (port 23), subsequent inbound traffic destined for the originating computer on port 23 would be allowed through.

examQuestions.questionText: You are asked to perform consulting work for a medium-sized company that is having network connectivity issues. When you examine the patch panel, you notice that none of the dozens of UTP cables are labeled. Which tool can you use to identify which cable goes to which workstation?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you need to trace a wire in a wall from one location to another, a tone generator and probe is the right tool to use. It consists of two pieces: a tone generator and a probe. To use it, attach one end to one end of the cable, such as the end at the computer. Then go to the patch panel with the other end of the probe to locate the cable. These are lifesavers when the cables are not properly labeled.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol is responsible for dynamically assigning IP addresses to client computers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) dynamically assigns IP addresses and other IP configuration information to network clients.

examQuestions.questionText: What characteristic differentiates STP from UTP?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Shielded twisted pair (STP) cabling has a foil shield surrounding the wire pairs to decrease electrical interference. Some STP cables also shield individual wire pairs. Unshielded twisted pair (UTP) does not have the shielding. Both types use RJ-45 connectors, can follow the T568A wiring standard, and can be produced as plenum-rated cable that does not produce poisonous gas when burned.

answers.textAnswer: It uses RJ-45s connectors instead of RJ-45.
It follows the T568A wiring standard.
It does not produce poisonous gas when burned.
It has a layer of foil shielding.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP port number will an email client use to push email to its email server?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Email is pushed from clients to servers using the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP). SMTP uses port 25.

examQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting an intermittently failing CAT7 network connection. You suspect that there is a short in the connection. Which tool can you use to determine this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Multimeters are versatile electronic measuring tools. A multimeter can measure voltage, current, and resistance on a wire.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol gathers and manages network performance information using devices called agents?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) gathers and manages network performance information. A management device called an SNMP server can be set up to collect data from these devices (called agents) and ensure that your network is operating properly.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Internet connection type, popular for home use, offers asymmetrical download and upload speeds and is implemented over common phone lines?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
One of the two most popular broadband choices for home use is Digital Subscriber Line (DSL). It utilizes existing phone lines and provides fairly reliable high-speed access. Most DSL subscriptions are asymmetrical, meaning they offer faster download speeds than upload speeds.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Wi-Fi encryption standard was the first to include the use of a 128-bit dynamic per-packet encryption key?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) was the first Wi-Fi encryption standard to implement the use of the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP). Whereas WEP used a static 40- or 128-bit key, TKIP uses a 128-bit dynamic per-packet key. It generates a new key for each packet sent.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing an 802.11n Wi-Fi network with five wireless access points. The access points are set up so their ranges overlap each other. To avoid communications issues, what principle should you follow when configuring them?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
When setting up wireless access points, it’s good practice to have their ranges overlap to ensure there is no loss of communication when roaming in the network’s area. However, to avoid problems, it’s best to set up the access points with nonoverlapping channels.

answers.textAnswer: Configure all access points to use the same channel.
Configure all access points to use adjacent channels.
Configure all access points to use non-overlapping channels.
Channel configuration will not cause communications issues.

examQuestions.questionText: You are setting up a small network in your neighbor’s house. She is concerned about wireless security, so she doesn’t want to use wireless networking at all. She needs to connect two computers to each other, but it will be impossible to run a network cable between them. Which technology can help her network these computers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Ethernet over power can make Ethernet connections by using electrical outlets. For it to work, both devices must be on the same electrical circuit.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to install a Wi-Fi network in a building that is approximately 100 meters long and 25 meters wide. Because of cost considerations, you will need to use 802.11g. At a minimum, how many wireless access points will you need?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The 802.11g standard has an indoor range of approximately 40 meters. At a minimum, you will need three access points. Depending on coverage and indoor interference, such as thick walls, you might need more, though.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing network cabling in a drop ceiling of an office space. The ceiling area is used to circulate breathable air. What type of cable do you need to install?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The cable can be any of the three major types, coaxial, twisted pair, or fiber, but it needs to be plenum rated. Normal cables have a PVC coating, which produces a poisonous gas when burned. Plenum-rated cables have a Teflon coating, which is not toxic when burned.

examQuestions.questionText: You are configuring a wireless 802.11n router. The office manager insists that you configure the router such that traffic from her computer receives higher priority on the network than other users’ traffic. Which setting do you need to configure to enable this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Quality of Service (QoS) is a strategy that allows an administrator to control resources to maintain a certain service level. By using QoS, an administrator can set different priorities for one or more types of network traffic based on different applications, data flows, or users.

examQuestions.questionText: If you are connecting to a website that encrypts its connection using TLS, what port number does that traffic travel on?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
To encrypt traffic between a web server and client securely, Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) can be used. HTTPS connections are secured using either Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) or Transport Layer Security (TLS). HTTPS uses port 443.

examQuestions.questionText: Your network is currently running a mix of 802.11b and 802.11g devices. At the end of the year, you have extra budget to upgrade some, but not all, of the wireless infrastructure. You want to upgrade to the newest technology but still maintain backward compatibility. Which standard should you choose?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
802.11b/g transmit in the 2.4GHz frequency, as does 802.11n, so they are compatible. The newer 802.11ac is a 5GHz standard and therefore is not backward compatible with 802.11b/g. 802.11r is not a standard related to Wi-Fi speed and is not in the A+ test objectives.

examQuestions.questionText: You are consulting with a small field office that needs a dedicated, digital point-to-point network connection to its parent office. Which Internet connection type will meet this requirement?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) is a digital, point-to-point network capable of maximum transmission speeds of about 2Mbps, although speeds of 128Kbps are more common.

examQuestions.questionText: While cleaning out a storage room, a technician finds several rolls of CAT5e network cable. He thinks that he might be able to use it to create replacement cables for his network. What is the maximum speed that this cable will support?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
CAT5e cable can support speeds of 1Gbps. CAT5 has a maximum of 100Mbps. CAT6 and newer can support 10Gbps, but no UTP cabling can currently support 20Gbps.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following shorthand notations corresponds to the CIDR subnet mask 255.255.224.0?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A subnet mask of 255.255.224.0 has eight bits in each of the first two octets set to on, and it has three bits in the third octet on. Therefore, it corresponds to /19 in shorthand.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol was developed by Microsoft and has been the default file and print sharing protocol on Windows-based computers since Windows 2000?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Common Internet File System (CIFS) is a Microsoft-developed enhancement of the SMB protocol, which was also developed by Microsoft. The intent behind CIFS is that it can be used to share files and printers between computers, regardless of the operating system that they run. It’s been the default file and print sharing protocol on Windows-based computers since Windows 2000.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Wi-Fi encryption standard uses a static key, which is commonly 10, 26, or 58 characters long?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) was one of the first security standards for wireless devices. It uses a static key; the keys are commonly 10, 26, or 58 hexadecimal characters long.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP port number does SNMP use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a noncritical service, so it uses UDP. It’s assigned port 161. IMAP4 uses port 143.

examQuestions.questionText: Because of a recent security breach, your IT team shut down several ports on the external firewall. Now, users can’t get to websites by using their URLs, but they can get there by using IP addresses. What port does the IT team need to open back up to enable Internet access via URLs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Clients are unable to get to the DNS server, which resolves host names (or URLs) to IP addresses. DNS uses port 53.

examQuestions.questionText: All of your network hosts are configured to use DHCP. Which IP address would indicate that a host has been unable to locate a DHCP server?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) is a TCP/IP standard used to configure automatically IP-based hosts that are unable to reach a DHCP server. APIPA addresses are in the 169.254.0.0/16 range. If you see a computer that has an IP address beginning with 169.254, you know that it has configured itself.

examQuestions.questionText: Your network uses UTP cabling. Which of the following types of network connections require the use of a crossover cable? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
If you are going to make a connection from hub to hub, switch to switch, hub to switch, or a computer directly to a router, you need a crossover cable. Otherwise, you need a regular patch cable.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is trying to establish a dial-up network connection using a legacy modem. What is the fastest data throughput for a modem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The fastest modems produced had a data rate of 56Kbps. At the time, they were considered fast. Today, not so much.

examQuestions.questionText: You are replacing a connector at the end of coaxial cable. What type of connector is threaded and screws into place?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
F-connectors are threaded and screw into place. The BNC connector locks by twisting one-quarter turn. SC and ST connectors are for fiber-optic cable.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing UTP network cabling. The network has a mixture of network cards, but the minimum required speed is 100Mbps. What is the minimum grade of cable you can install to meet this requirement?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Cat 5 UTP can transmit data at speeds up to 100Mbps, for a distance of 100 meters.

examQuestions.questionText: You have reason to believe that several network users are actively browsing prohibited content on unsecured sites on the Internet. Which port can you disable on the firewall to immediately stop access to these web sites?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Normal (unsecured) websites are accessed on port 80, which is the port that Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) uses. Shut it down, and no one will be able to access web sites, except secure sites that use HTTPS, which is on port 443.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing UTP network cable for a client. The client’s policies require that network cables do not produce poisonous gas when burned. What type of cable do you need to install?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Most network cables are coated with a plastic PVC coating, which produces toxic gas when burned. Plenum-rated cables are coated with a Teflon-like material that is not poisonous when burned.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to create a UTP crossover cable. Which pins need to be crossed over to make the cable work properly?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In a crossover cable, pin 1 to pin 3 and pin 2 to pin 6 are crossed on one side of the cable only. This is to get the “send” pins matched up with the “receive” pins on the other side, and vice versa.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol is designed to help resolve host names to IP addresses?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Domain Name System (DNS) is responsible for resolving host names to IP addresses. This is used millions of times daily on the Internet; when someone types in a website name, such as www.sybex.com, DNS will resolve that to an IP address to enable communication.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to install an Internet connection for a forest ranger outlook tower, located far away from electrical lines. Which option would be best for broadband Internet access?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Satellite Internet is not much like any other type of broadband connection. Instead of a cabled connection, it uses a satellite dish to receive data from an orbiting satellite and relay station that is connected to the Internet. Because it requires a clear line of sight between the transmitter and receiver, it can be referred to as “line of sight” wireless. For an installation far from civilization, it may be the only option.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP host-to-host protocol makes its best effort to deliver data but does not guarantee it?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The two host-to-host layer protocols are Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP). TCP guarantees packet delivery through the use of a virtual circuit and data acknowledgments, and UDP does not. Because of this, TCP is often referred to as connection oriented, whereas UDP is connectionless.

examQuestions.questionText: Which port number is AFP capable of using?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Apple Filing Protocol (AFP) is a file transfer protocol developed by Apple. It uses port 548.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing a wireless network for a small company. They want to have 100Mbps or better wireless transmission rates. Which of the following standards will allow you to provide this? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
The only two Wi-Fi standards that provide greater than 100Mbps throughput are 802.11n and 802.11ac. The 802.11g standard has a maximum throughput of 54Mbps, and 802.11i is an encryption standard.

examQuestions.questionText: Which twisted pair cable category uses a longitudinal separator, which separates each of the four pairs of wires from each other and reduces the amount of crosstalk possible?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Category 6 cable typically is made up of four twisted pairs of copper wire, but its capabilities far exceed those of other cable types. Category 6 twisted pair uses a longitudinal separator, which separates each of the four pairs of wires from each other and reduces the amount of crosstalk possible.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of network spans multiple buildings or offices but is confined to a relatively small geographical area?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Networks that are larger than a LAN but confined to a relatively small geographical area are metropolitan area networks (MANs). A MAN is generally defined as a network that spans a city or a large campus.

examQuestions.questionText: You are configuring hosts on a network running IPv4. Which elements are required for the computer to connect to the network?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
To communicate on an IPv4 network, a host must be configured with a valid IP address and a subnet mask. A default gateway is needed only if the host will connect to a remote network. DNS servers are optional but useful, because they resolve host names to IP addresses.

answers.textAnswer: IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway
IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS server address

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol is used to provide shared access to files and printers on the network?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Server Message Block (SMB) is a protocol used to provide shared access to files, printers, and other network resources. In a way, it functions a bit like FTP only with a few more options, such as the ability to connect to printers, and more management commands.

examQuestions.questionText: Which networking device is capable of reading IP addresses and forwarding packets based on the destination IP address?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Routers operate at the Network layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model. Because of this, they make their decisions on what to do with traffic based on logical addresses, such as an IP address.

examQuestions.questionText: Which network connectivity device does not forward broadcast messages, thereby creating multiple broadcast domains?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
One of the key features of routers is that they break up broadcast domains. Broadcast traffic on one side of the router will not get passed to the other side, which greatly reduces network traffic.

examQuestions.questionText: What port number does the Telnet protocol use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Telnet lets users log into another machine and “see” the remote computer in a window on their screen. Although this vision is text only, the user can manage files on that remote machine just as if they were logged in locally. Telnet uses port 23.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol, designed to download email, allows for multiple clients to be simultaneously connected to the same mailbox?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) is a secure protocol designed to download email. It has several advantages over the older Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3). First, IMAP4 works in connected and disconnected modes. Second, it lets you store the email on the server, as opposed to POP3, which requires you to download it. Third, IMAP4 allows multiple clients to be simultaneously connected to the same inbox.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP Internet layer protocol is responsible for resolving physical MAC addresses to logical IP addresses?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
At the Internet layer of TCP/IP, Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) resolves logical IP addresses to physical MAC addresses built into network cards. Reverse ARP (RARP) resolves MAC addresses to IP addresses.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of network is typically defined as being contained within a single office or building?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A local area network (LAN) is often defined as being contained in a single building, office, or home.

examQuestions.questionText: You are configuring network hosts with static IP addresses. You have chosen to use a class B network address. What is the default subnet mask that you should configure on the hosts?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The default subnet mask for class B networks is 255.255.0.0, or written in shorthand, /16.

examQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP protocol is designed to send email from clients to mail servers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3), and Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) are all email protocols. SMTP is for sending email. POP3 and IMAP are for downloading email.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is going to set up a Wi-Fi network using standard omnidirectional antennae. Because of the building configuration, transmitting signals for the greatest distance is his primary criterion. Which standard should he choose?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Of the Wi-Fi standards, 802.11n has the longest range by default, at roughly 70 meters indoors and 250 meters outdoors. 802.11ac is newer and faster than 802.11n, but it transmits exclusively in the 5GHz range, which restricts its functional distance.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to ensure that client computers can download email from external email servers, regardless of the protocol their email client uses. Which ports do you open on the firewall to enable this? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP, port 25), Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3, port 110), and Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP, port 143) are all email protocols. SMTP is for sending email. POP3 and IMAP are for downloading email.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following IPv6 addresses is equivalent to an address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range in IPv4?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The 169.254.0.0/16 range in IPv4 is the APIPA range, used for automatic configuration if the host can’t locate a DHCP server. The same task in IPv6 is accomplished with a link local address in the FE80::/10 range.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of coaxial cable connector locks by twisting the connector one-quarter turn?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The BNC connector locks by twisting one-quarter turn. F-connectors are threaded and screw into place. SC and ST connectors are for fiber-optic cable.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following TCP/IP protocols is connection oriented and attempts to guarantee packet delivery?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) guarantees packet delivery through the use of a virtual circuit and data acknowledgments, and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) does not. Because of this, TCP is often referred to as connection oriented, whereas UDP is connectionless.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of network covers large geographical areas and often supports thousands of users?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A wide area network (WAN) covers large geographical areas and often supports thousands of users.

examQuestions.questionText: The system is not keeping the time correctly. What should you do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If you find that you are continually resetting the system time, it could be that the CMOS battery is dying

examQuestions.questionText: What is the most common reason for an unexpected reboot?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
One common reason for shutdowns is overheating. Often when that is the case, however, the system reboots itself rather than just shutting down

examQuestions.questionText: What should the ambient temperature be inside the case?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Take care to keep the ambient air within normal ranges (approximately 60–90 degrees Fahrenheit) and at a constant temperature.

examQuestions.questionText: The system is rebooting unexpectedly and the system is NOT overheating. What other component could it be?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Power supply problems can cause reboots as well. The power supply continually sends a Power_Good signal to the motherboard and if this signal is not present momentarily the system will reset.

examQuestions.questionText: When procuring a replacement capacitor, which of the following need not match?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If the other variable match, it need not be from the same manufacturer.

examQuestions.questionText: A user calls saying that his laptop won’t power on. He charged it all night, so he knows that the battery is fine. What should you have him do first?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If a laptop won’t power up on battery, always try to use AC power. You never know when a battery could have failed. If the user had a spare and didn’t have an AC power cord, trying a spare might work, but trying AC power is the best bet. There is no battery power switch on laptops.

answers.textAnswer: Plug the laptop in using an AC adapter and try to power it on.
Replace the battery with a spare and try to power it on.
Toggle the battery power switch on the front of the laptop, and then try to power it on.
Send the laptop in for service.

examQuestions.questionText: Which operating system use the pin wheel of death as a proprietary screen crash?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
While Microsoft users have the BSOD to deal with Apple users have also come to have the same negative feelings about the “Pin Wheel” of death. This is a multicolored pinwheel mouse pointer

examQuestions.questionText: Which tool can be used to test a port?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Loopback plugs are used to test the functionality of various types of ports, but their most common use is to test a network card

examQuestions.questionText: You turn a computer on and it doesn’t boot up properly. From inside the case, you hear a rhythmic ticking sound. What is most likely the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The only components that typically make noise are the ones that have moving parts, such as fans and hard drives. In most cases, a rhythmic ticking sound will be something that’s generated by the hard drive.

examQuestions.questionText: What process may generate beep cores during reboot?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
During the boot-up of the system, a power-on self-test (POST) occurs and each device is checked for functionality.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the proprietary screen crashes called in Windows?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Once a regular occurrence when working with Windows, blue screens (also known as the Blue Screen of Death) have become much less frequent.
