Hybrid drives are named for their inclusion of traditional hard drive technology as well as newer solid-state technology. Hybrid systems can be all in one or comprise one drive of each technology. Special software is needed to optimize the hybrid drive’s usage and performance.

answers.textAnswer: A drive that has a SATA interface as well as one other
A drive that has both HDD and SSD components
A drive that can be used with Windows or Mac OS
A drive that is partially internal and partially external

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a concept that applies only to conventional magnetic hard disk drives and not newer solid-state drives?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Each concept applies to both HDDs and SSDs except for platter spin rates. Revolutions per minute (rpm) measurements refer to drives with moving parts. SSDs have none.

examQuestions.questionText: When replacing a power supply, which of the following tends to vary among power supplies and must be chosen properly to support all connected devices?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Power supplies are rated in watts. When you purchase a power supply, you should make sure the devices inside the computer do not require more wattage than the chosen power supply can offer. The voltage is fairly standard among power supplies, and it has nothing to do with the devices connected to the power supply. Amperage and resistance are not selling points for power supplies.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following wireless IEEE standards operate on the 2.4GHz radio frequency and are directly compatible with each other? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-4}.
Both 802.11b and 802.11g operate in the 2.4GHz range and use similar transmission standards. Many devices on the market are listed as 802.11b/g, meaning they will work with either system. Alternatively, 802.11a and 802.11ac operate in the 5GHz range.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the primary function of the SSID?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A service-set identifier (SSID) is the unique name given to the wireless network. All hardware that is to participate on the network must be configured to use the same SSID. Essentially, it is the network name. When you are using Windows to connect to a wireless network, all available wireless networks will be listed by their SSID.

answers.textAnswer: Secure communication between a web server and browser
Secure communication between a server and remote host
A parameter used to identify a network and configure a wireless connection
A type of password used to secure a wireless connection

examQuestions.questionText: Which two of the following are features that allow 802.11ac to achieve higher data throughput? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-3}.
The two technologies that 802.11ac employs to achieve high throughput are channel bonding and MIMO. Channel bonding is the combination of multiple smaller channels into one large channel for greater bandwidth. MIMO is enhanced over 802.11n to allow for more multiple inputs and outputs. 802.11ac also uses beamforming, but that helps the range, not the throughput.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the most secure wireless encryption standard for 802.11 networks?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
WEP was the original encryption standard developed for Wi-Fi networks, but it is easily hacked. WPA is an upgrade, but WPA2 is more secure and incorporates the entire 802.11i standard. SAFER+ is used to encrypt Bluetooth communications.

examQuestions.questionText: What level of QoS is designated for interactive voice and video?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
QoS level 5 is designated for interactive voice and video, with less than 100ms delay. Level 1 is for background applications and is low priority. Level 4 is known as controlled load, which is lower priority than interactive voice and video. Level 6 only has 10ms latency but is reserved for control traffic.

examQuestions.questionText: You have just installed a wireless router on your home network. Which of the following should you do to make it highly secure? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2}.
You should always change the default administrator name and password as well as the default SSID when installing a new wireless router. Enabling encryption is also a good idea, but WPA and WPA2 are better options than WEP. The channel has nothing to do with security.

answers.textAnswer: Change the default administrator name and password.

examQuestions.questionText: You are setting up a small office network for a client. Which Internet service would you recommend to provide the best speed?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Of the options listed, DSL provides the fastest speed. DSL can easily provide 12Mbps downloads. Dial-up is limited to 56Kbps, and BRI ISDN (128Kbps) and PRI (about 1.5Mbps) don’t even come close. Satellite is also much slower than DSL.

examQuestions.questionText: Which service allows users with private IP addresses to access the Internet using a public IP address?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Network Address Translation (NAT) allows users to have a private IP address and still access the Internet with a public IP address. NAT is installed on a router and translates the private IP address into a public one for the user to access the Internet. DHCP assigns IP configuration information to clients. DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses. A DMZ is an area on a network between an external router and an internal router.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing a single 802.11g wireless network. The office space is large enough that you need three WAPs. What channels should you configure the WAPs on to avoid communication issues?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
There are 14 communication channels in the 2.4GHz range, but only the first 11 are configurable. The three non-overlapping channels are 1, 6, and 11.

examQuestions.questionText: You are setting up a wireless network. Which wireless standards would give the users over 40Mbps throughput? (Choose three.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-3},{answer-4}.
Three standards listed—802.11ac (1300Mbps), 802.11g (54Mbps), and 802.11n (600Mbps)—give users the required throughput.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to configure a network for a small office. The wireless router is installed, and now you need to connect the client computers. What do you enter on the client computers to connect to the router?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
To join the network, client computers need to find the SSID, ensure that the security settings are correct (to match the router), and enter the security passphrase. As an administrator, you should have configured this passphrase to be different than the router’s administrator password.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following wireless communication methods has an operational range of 1 meter with a viewing angle of 30 degrees?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Infrared is limited to about 1 meter, with a viewing angle of about 30 degrees. Most Bluetooth devices can transmit up to 10 meters. WiMAX has a maximum range of about 5 miles. Satellite signals can travel from the surface of the Earth to a small metal can orbiting the planet.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are advantages to using dial-up Internet service? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-3}.
Dial-up Internet is archaic by today’s standards, but it is widely available (anywhere there is phone service) and it’s generally lower in cost than other Internet access methods. It’s definitely not high speed, and its security is really no different than that of broadband Internet access methods.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following security standards was the first to introduce a dynamic 128-bit per-packet security key?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
WEP could use a 64-bit or 128-bit security key, but it was a static key. TKIP introduced a dynamic per-packet key. AES and CCMP came after TKIP.

examQuestions.questionText: You are running an 802.11g wireless router in mixed mode. You have three 802.11g wireless NICs using the router. A new user connects using an 802.11b wireless NIC. What will happen?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The good news is that 802.11g is backward compatible with 802.11b. The bad news is if you run in a mixed environment, all devices that communicate with the WAP (or router) will be forced to slow down to accommodate the older technology.

answers.textAnswer: The user with 802.11b will access the network at 11Mbps while the users with 802.11g will access the network at 54Mbps.
The user with 802.11b will not be able to communicate on the network.
The user with 802.11b will access the network at 11Mbps. The users with 802.11g will access the network at 54Mbps unless they are communicating with the 802.11b device, which will be at 11Mbps.
All users will access the network at 11Mbps.

examQuestions.questionText: When enabled, which feature of a wireless router allows only specified computers to access the network?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
MAC filtering is a security option that can specify that only computers with specific MAC (hardware) addresses can access the network. Port forwarding is a feature of firewalls. WPS is an easy setup mechanism for wireless networks. SSID is the wireless network name.

examQuestions.questionText: A firewall operates by using a set of rules known as what?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The set of rules for access on a firewall is called an access control list (ACL). An SLA is an agreement on service level for QoS. Default deny is a good policy for firewalls because it doesn’t let any traffic through. A DMZ is a subnet located between an external network router and an internal router.

examQuestions.questionText: Besides 802.11 standards, which wireless communication method works in the 2.4GHz range?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Bluetooth also operates in the 2.4GHz range.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following broadband technologies provides two dedicated, digital data channels that can be combined for greater throughput?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Basic rate interface ISDN (BRI ISDN) provides two separate 64Kbps B channels for data transmissions. These channels can be combined to increase throughput. A PRI ISDN uses 23 B channels. DSL, cable, and satellite do not offer multiple dedicated digital channels.

examQuestions.questionText: You have set up a wireless router on your network and configured it to use AES. What configuration option do you need to choose on the client computers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If your router is using AES, the clients will need to use WPA2. TKIP is a protocol utilized by WPA. WEP is the weakest of the encryption options.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a benefit of laptop design?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
By and large, compromises always must be made when comparing laptops to desktops. Although laptops can be used as desktop replacements, their performance is almost always lower than comparably priced desktops.

examQuestions.questionText: What should you do for a Li-ion battery that appears to charge fully but does not last as long as the battery’s meter indicates that it will last?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Battery calibration for Li-ion batteries allows the powered device to drain the battery’s power before recharging. Battery exercising is the initial charging and discharging of nickel-based batteries so that they will function as expected. You should never short a battery’s terminals, and replacement is a last resort, used when any battery has reached the end of its life.

answers.textAnswer: Short the terminals to discharge the battery.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to replace a failed AC adapter for a client’s laptop. When replacing the adapter, which of the following purchases is acceptable to obtain the same or better results?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Think of wattage as a “bucket” of power that the attached device can draw on. A bigger bucket simply holds more power but does not force the power on the device. Less wattage is not advised, however. Voltage can be thought of as the pressure behind the power to the device. Anything but the proper voltage is dangerous for the device. When you replace a laptop’s AC adapter, you should match the voltage ratings of the original adapter. This also means that you should use an adapter with a fixed voltage if that matches the characteristics of the original; otherwise, obtain one that automatically switches voltages at the levels needed.

answers.textAnswer: An AC adapter with a higher voltage rating than the original
An AC adapter with a higher wattage rating than the original
A DC adapter with the same voltage rating as the original
An AC adapter with a lower voltage and wattage rating than the original

examQuestions.questionText: A client has a laptop with which you are unfamiliar. You are asked to perform a memory upgrade. How can you obtain the service manual for this laptop computer?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Laptop service manuals can be obtained from the manufacturer’s website. It’s very rare that paper service manuals are shipped with the laptop. Pressing F1 while in Windows will open Windows Help, and pressing F2 on many laptops during the system boot will take you into the BIOS.

answers.textAnswer: By pressing F1 while in Windows
By pressing F2 while the system is booting up
By reading the paper copy that comes with the laptop

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are components of an LCD? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1} and {answer-2}.
The components of an LCD screen are the inverter, screen, and backlight. The video card is also a key component of the LCD system. A CRT is a different technology than LCD.

examQuestions.questionText: Which laptop input device was released with the IBM ThinkPad (now distributed by Lenovo) series of laptops?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Touchpoint point stick was released with the IBM ThinkPad series of laptops.

examQuestions.questionText: One of the users on your network needs to travel, and she wants to work on the airplane. Which laptop accessory will allow her to power her laptop from the airplane?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A DC adapter converts the DC output from a car or airplane accessory power plug into the DC voltages required by your laptop.

examQuestions.questionText: How many pins does a DDR2 MicroDIMM memory module have?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
DDR2 MicroDIMMs can have 172 or 214 pins.

examQuestions.questionText: __________ is the fastest and most modern interface used as an expansion method for external peripherals, such as mice, webcams, scanners, and printers It is popular on laptops and desktops alike.
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
USB is used most often in laptops as an expansion bus for external peripherals. Although parallel and PS/2 ports allow for connection of external peripherals, they are not as flexible or widely used for expansion as USB.

examQuestions.questionText: You are sitting in a coffee shop and using the public wireless network. You suddenly notice suspicious activity on your laptop. Which laptop feature should you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Your best bet is to turn off your wireless connection immediately in order to sever the tie between your laptop and the public network. This is done using the Wi-Fi toggle.

examQuestions.questionText: There has recently been a string of hardware thefts in your office building. What should you recommend that your users implement to help avoid this problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Sometimes the only way to ensure that equipment doesn’t walk away is to lock it down physically. Laptops come equipped with holes for cable locks that can be used to secure them to a desk or other workstation.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a user who needs to upgrade his laptop. Due to how often he collaborates with others, he wants to be sure that the viewing angle is as wide as possible. Which technology should you look for?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The backlight won’t really affect the viewing angle of the laptop. What you should look for is a laptop that uses LCD IPS technology, which offers a wider viewing angle than does TN.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following expansion buses uses serial communications and is capable of operating in USB and PCIe modes?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The ExpressCard bus brings USB 2.0, USB 3.0, and PCIe to the small-form-factor computing industry. CardBus is an older technology that supports USB 1.1 and PCI only. Mini PCI is PCI, not PCIe.

examQuestions.questionText: A user on your network wants to be able to draw images on his screen and have the laptop capture them. What type of device does he need?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The user needs a digitizer, which takes input from the device, such as drawn images, and converts them into electronic images on the computer.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following technologies allows for data transfers of up to 20Gbps?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Thunderbolt 2 provides for speeds up to 20Gbps. USB 3.1 only supports speeds up to 10Gbps.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a user who needs to keep desktop devices such as keyboard, monitor, and mouse permanently connected so that they can be used by an attached laptop. What type of device do you recommend that they use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A docking station made specifically for its associated brand and model of laptop can host desktop components permanently, regardless of whether the laptop is attached to the docking station. When the laptop’s portability is not required, but instead use of the desktop components is the priority, attaching the laptop to the docking station makes such components available to the laptop without separately attaching each component.

examQuestions.questionText: The process by which the processor slows down to conserve power is officially called _________.
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The processor can reduce how fast it’s working, which is called throttling, to help conserve battery life.

examQuestions.questionText: How do laptop hard drives differ from desktop hard drives?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Laptop hard drives commonly have a 2½ form factor. The most common form factor for desktop hard drives is 3½. Laptop hard drives use the same drive technologies as their desktop counterparts, such as serial and parallel ATA. As with desktop hard drives, laptop hard drives are available in both solid-state and conventional varieties. Unlike desktop hard drives, laptop hard drives do not have separate power connectors.

answers.textAnswer: Laptop hard drives use completely different standards from those used by desktop hard drives for communication with the host.
Laptop hard drives are solid state; desktop hard drives have spinning platters.
Laptop hard drives require a separate power connection; desktop hard drives are powered through the drive interface.
The most common form factor of a laptop hard drive is about an inch smaller than that of a desktop hard drive.

examQuestions.questionText: One of your network users has an older laptop with no Bluetooth support. He recently received a Bluetooth headset that he needs to use with his laptop. What is the least expensive way to make the headset compatible with his laptop?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A USB Bluetooth adapter should do the trick. Replacing the laptop is a much more expensive proposition.

answers.textAnswer: Buy a Mini PCIe Bluetooth adapter.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following memory types has the smallest form factor?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
SODIMM and MicroDIMM are the common laptop small-form-factor memory standards. Of the two, MicroDIMM is smaller.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not an advantage of a Universal Serial Bus (USB) printer interface?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The rate of transfer and the ability to recognize new devices automatically are two of the major advantages that currently makes USB the most popular type of printer interface. However, it is the network printer interface that allows the printer to communicate with networks, servers, and workstations.

answers.textAnswer: It has a higher transfer rate than a serial connection.
It has a higher transfer rate than a parallel connection.
It allows the printer to communicate with networks, servers, and workstations.

examQuestions.questionText: Which voltage is applied to the paper to transfer the toner to the paper in an EP process laser printer?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Because the toner on the drum has a slight negative charge (–100VDC), it requires a positive charge to transfer it to the paper; +600VDC is the voltage used in an EP process laser printer.

examQuestions.questionText: Which types of printers are referred to as page printers because they receive their print job instructions one page at a time? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3},{answer-4}.
A page printer is a type of computer printer that prints a page at a time. Common types of page printers are the laser printer and the inkjet printer.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of printers can be used with multipart forms?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Dot-matrix printers are impact printers and therefore can be used with multipart forms. Daisy-wheel printers can be used with multipart forms as well.

examQuestions.questionText: Which step in the EP print process uses a laser to discharge selected areas of the photosensitive drum, thus forming an image on the drum?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The writing step uses a laser to discharge selected areas of the photosensitive drum, thus forming an image on the drum.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are page-description languages? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-4}.
Of those listed, only PostScript and PCL are page-description languages. There is no PDL or PageScript.

examQuestions.questionText: What voltage does the corona wire or corona roller hold?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
For the toner (which has a charge of –600VDC) to be transferred from the print drum (which has a charge of –600VDC) to the paper, there must be a positive, or opposite, charge of greater difference to break the –600VDC charge from the drum.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the correct order of the steps in the EP print process?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The correct sequence in the EP print process is processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning.

answers.textAnswer: Developing, exposing, transferring, fusing, charging, cleaning, processing
Charging, processing, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning
Processing, transferring, exposing, developing, charging, cleaning, fusing
Processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning

examQuestions.questionText: Most printers that use the electrophotographic process contain how many standard assemblies?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
There are nine standard assemblies in an electrophotographic process printer. Early laser printers using the electrographic process contained the nine standard assemblies. Newer laser printers do not require an ozone filter and contain only eight standard assemblies.

examQuestions.questionText: What happens during the developing stage of laser printing?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
After a laser has created an image of the page, the developing roller uses a magnet and electrostatic charges to attract toner to itself and then transfers the toner to the areas on the drum that have been exposed to the laser. The toner is melted during the fusing stage. The laser creates an image of the page on the drum in the writing stage. An electrostatic charge is applied to the paper to attract toner in the transferring stage, which happens immediately after the developing stage.

answers.textAnswer: An electrostatic charge is applied to the drum to attract toner particles.
Heat is applied to the paper to melt the toner.
The laser creates an image of the page on the drum.
An electrostatic charge is applied to the paper to attract toner particles.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are possible interfaces for printers? (Choose three.)
examQuestions.explanation: {answer-1},{answer-3},{answer-4}.Printers can communicate via parallel, serial, USB, infrared, wireless, and network connections.

examQuestions.questionText: Which printer contains a wheel that looks like a flower with raised letters and symbols on each petal?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The daisy-wheel printer gets its name because it contains a wheel with raised letters and symbols on each “petal.”

examQuestions.questionText: What part of a laser printer supplies the voltages for charging and transferring corona assemblies?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The high-voltage power supply is the part of the laser printer that supplies the voltages for charging and transferring corona assemblies.

examQuestions.questionText: Which printer part gets the toner from the photosensitive drum onto the paper?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The transfer corona assembly gets the toner from the photosensitive drum onto the paper. For some printers, this is a transfer corona wire, and for others, it is a transfer corona roller.

examQuestions.questionText: Which step in the laser printer printing process occurs immediately after the exposing phase?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Developing happens after exposing. The correct order is processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning.

examQuestions.questionText: Which laser printer component permanently presses the toner into the paper?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The fuser assembly presses and melts the toner into the paper. The transfer corona transfers the toner from the drum to the paper. The printer controller circuitry converts signals from the PC into signals for the various printer assemblies. The paper transport assembly controls the movement of the paper through the printer.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following most accurately describes how to obtain a firmware upgrade for your laser printer?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Firmware upgrades for laser printers are downloaded for free from the manufacturer’s website. A technician does not need to install a new chip because firmware is upgraded via software. It’s unlikely that the manufacturer will send you the upgrade on a CD; it will refer you to its website to download it.

answers.textAnswer: Download the firmware upgrade for free from the manufacturer’s website.
Pay to download the firmware upgrade from the manufacturer’s website.
Have a certified laser printer technician come to your site and install a new firmware chip.
Contact the manufacturer of the printer, and they will send you the firmware upgrade on a CD.

examQuestions.questionText: What is typically included in the EP laser printer toner cartridge? (Choose three.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2},{answer-4}.
An electrophotographic (EP) laser printer toner cartridge includes the toner, print drum, and cleaning blade. The laser is usually contained within the printer, not within the toner cartridge.

examQuestions.questionText: Which OSI layer signals “all clear” by making sure that the data segments are error free?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
It is the responsibility of the Transport layer to signal an “all clear” by making sure that the data segments are error free. It also controls the data flow and troubleshoots any problems with transmitting or receiving data frames.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of device will block unwanted traffic from your network using a set of rules called an ACL?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.

The job of a firewall is to block unwanted network traffic. Firewalls do this by using a list of rules called an access control list (ACL). Routers connect networks to each other. Internet appliances give the user Internet access. A network attached storage (NAS) device is like a dedicated file server.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following statements are not associated with a star network? (Choose all that apply.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-3},{answer-4}.
In a star network, all systems are connected using a central device such as a hub or a switch. The network is not disrupted for other users when more systems are added or removed. The star network design is used with today’s UTP-based networks.

answers.textAnswer: A single cable break can cause complete network disruption.
All devices connect to a central device.
It uses a single backbone computer to connect all network devices.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following wireless communication standards is often described in terms of a wireless personal area network?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.

Bluetooth networks are often called wireless personal area networks (WPANs).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which protocol provides a mechanism to access and query directory services systems?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) provides a mechanism to access and query directory services systems.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the first step in the laser printing process?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
In the first part of the laser print process, a rubber blade inside the EP cartridge scrapes any toner left on the drum into a used-toner receptacle inside the EP cartridge, and a fluorescent lamp discharges any remaining charge on the photosensitive drum (remember that the drum, being photosensitive, loses its charge when exposed to light).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum distance that you can run thinnet coaxial cable?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Thinnet coaxial can run up to 185 meters. UTP can run up to 100 meters, and multimode fiber can run up to 400 meters. Thicknet coaxial can run up to 500 meters.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: On your impact printer, the characters are not coming out clean. Which of the following should you attempt?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
On an impact printer, the print head should never be lubricated, but you can clean off debris with a cotton swab and denatured alcohol. A ribbon is used instead of an ink tank, and there is no drum.

answers.textAnswer: Clean the print head with denatured alcohol
Clean the drum with a moist cloth

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which statement is true about laptops and smaller mobile devices?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Most laptops use mechanical drives. Mobile device parts are not usually field serviceable, most mobile devices use solid-state drives, and laptops do not typically use multitouch and touchflow technology.

answers.textAnswer: Mobile device parts are usually field serviceable.
Most mobile devices use mechanical drives.
Laptops use multitouch and touchflow technology.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which custom configuration features surround sound audio?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Of the options listed, only the home theater PC benefits the user by featuring surround sound audio.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have a laptop that doesn’t have any video. Its power lights are on. You plug in a known working external monitor and toggle the LCD cutoff switch and there is no video on the external monitor either. What most likely needs to happen?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you’re not getting video on the external monitor or the LCD screen, it’s likely a problem with the video card. You can’t reinstall the video driver because you can’t see. Replacing the screen or trying another monitor won’t likely help. It looks like the video card needs to be replaced, and in most cases this will mean replacing the entire motherboard.

answers.textAnswer: You need to reinstall the video driver.
You need to replace the LCD screen.
You need to try a second external monitor.
You need to service the laptop’s video card.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which switch can be used with PING to specify a packet size?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The –l switch can be used with PING to specify a packet size.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which function enables a mobile device to be located?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Geotracking, which can be done through both cell towers and through 802.11 APs, can be used to locate a mobile device.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You want to add a printer to a network but not add a host computer. Which of the following is an appropriate solution?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A print server is a popular option for adding a printer to the network and not adding a host computer. To be a print server, the network interface card (NIC) in the printer differs from a NIC in a computer in that it has a processor on it to perform the management of the NIC interface and it is made by the same manufacturer as the printer.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Your laser printer is reporting that it needs a maintenance kit installed. Which of the following is not usually included in a maintenance kit?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Maintenance kits are marketed by the manufacturer. Each kit varies in contents based on the printer in question but typically consists of a fuser, a transfer roller, and the feed/separation rollers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Fire code regulations in your area require that you use network cables that are fire retardant. What type of cables will you need to use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
For areas where a cable must be fire retardant, such as in a drop ceiling, you must run plenum-grade cable. Plenum refers to the fact that this cable is safe to run in a plenum area because the coating on the sleeve of the cable does not produce poisonous gas when burned. PVC is the other type of coating typically found on network cables, but it produces poisonous gas when burned.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following display connections provides the best picture?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
While both DVI and HDMI provide a high-quality digital picture, the HDMI connection will be the best.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which class of the following is a radio frequency technology that can connect a printer to a computer at a short range?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Bluetooth is a radio frequency technology that can connect a printer to a computer at a short range; its absolute maximum range is 100 meters (330 feet), and most devices are specified to work within 10 meters (33 feet).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: BitLocker is an example of wha
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Many operating systems provide the ability to encrypt an entire volume or drive, protecting a mobile device’s data in the event of theft. A good example of this is BitLocker, which is available in Windows Vista, Windows 7, and Windows 8.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Under normal circumstances, the GPS receiver must be in contact with how many GPS satellites to calculate horizontal position?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.

To calculate the horizontal position, the GPS receiver normally needs signals from three satellites. It can also calculate elevation or vertical position with four satellite signals.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Ghosting is occurring on paper coming from your laser printer. Which of the following would likely be causing this?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Ghosting means you can see light images of previously printed pages on the current page. This is caused by one of two things: bad erasure lamps or a broken cleaning blade.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the term that describes running a processor faster than its rating for increased performance?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.

Overclocking is the practice of increasing the clock frequency of the frontside bus to increase performance. Overclocking usually requires better than standard cooling efforts to avoid damage to the processor.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following laptop states leaves programs running but requires the user’s password to be entered again before the session can continue?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Lock state leaves programs running, but locks the computer and requires the user’s password to be entered again before the session can continue.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the process of updating the BIOS called?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The process is referred to as flashing the BIOS. It simply means the old instructions are deleted from the EEPROM chip and the new instructions are written to the chip.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the most effective security feature to protect sensitive data on a mobile device?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Remote wipes are instructions sent remotely to a mobile device that erases all the data in cases where the device is stolen.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following connectors does not use a bar-and-slot configuration but rather pins and sockets?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
USB interfaces use a reciprocal flat, almost interlocking, pair of plastic bars, having pins on the inside of each, which do not qualify as bar-and-slot, the latter being characteristically more central to the connector. The other interfaces use connectors where the device and cable connect by a central slot mating with a bar that has pins on both sides.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a client computer and discover it has an IP address of 169.254.10.25 with a subnet mask of 255.255.0.0. What does this indicate?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.

Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) addresses are in the 169.254.0.0 network. The fact that this client has an address in that range means that it was unable to obtain a lease from the DHCP server and that it configured itself with APIPA.

answers.textAnswer: The client’s address has been manually configured.
The client was unable to reach the DHCP server.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not an advantage of using flash memory for storage as opposed to a hard drive?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The advantages are reduced heat, lower power consumption, less noise, and better reliability since you have no moving parts. The disadvantages are higher cost and less capacity.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which RAID level is also known as disk striping?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
RAID 0 is also known as disk striping. RAID 5 is known as striping with parity.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The system board’s underlying circuitry is called the __________.
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The computer’s bus moves information into and out of the processor and other devices.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following laptop states keeps the session in memory and puts the computer in a low-power state that you can quickly resume from?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The sleep option keeps the session in memory and puts the computer in a low-power state that you can quickly resume from.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following takes the DC power the laptop is providing and boosts it up to AC to run the backlight?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The inverter takes the DC power the laptop is providing and boosts it up to AC to run the backlight.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which type of networking utilizes POTS?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
With dial-up, you simply add a modem to your computer and connect to an Internet service provider (ISP) over the existing phone lines—also known as the Plain Old Telephone System (POTS) or the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user calls complaining that every time he turns his desktop computer on, it beeps at him once. He’s afraid that there is something wrong and that the computer is going to crash. What is wrong with the computer?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
It doesn’t sound like anything is wrong with the system. Most BIOSs beep once to indicate that everything checked out okay. If you get more than one beep, called a beep code, that can indicate a problem.

answers.textAnswer: The system BIOS has detected an error.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the diagnostics process that occurs during every startup called?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Every computer has a diagnostic program built into its BIOS called the power-on self-test (POST). When you turn on the computer, it executes this set of diagnostics.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have counted the number of chips on a SIMM stick and are convinced that it’s parity RAM. How many chips should be there?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
You can identify parity SIMM by counting the number of chips on the stick. If there are nine, it’s parity RAM. If there are eight, it’s nonparity.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following take the signal going out and echo it back, allowing you to test ports?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Also called wrap plugs, loopback plugs take the signal going out and essentially echo it back. This allows you to test ports to make certain they’re working correctly.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the term that describes when packets meet the criteria of a firewall’s ACL and are passed through?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Port forwarding is when a packet meets the ACL criteria and is passed through the firewall. Port triggering is an automated form of port forwarding.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is used to identify each host by its unique number and determine specifically which addresses are allowed to access the network?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
When MAC filtering is implemented, you identify each host by this number and determine specifically which addresses are allowed to access the network.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: When a system keeps losing the proper date and time, what is usually the problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
When the PC is not keeping the correct time or date when turned off, it is usually a CMOS battery issue and a warning that the battery is going to die soon.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following cellular technologies is also referred to as 4G?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
4G or Long-Term Evolution (LTE) offers potential data rates competitive with 802.11 standards.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: If Automatic Private IP Addressing is being used, what will the host’s subnet mask be?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If a DHCP server cannot be found, the clients automatically assign themselves an IP address, somewhat randomly, with a subnet mask of 255.255.0.0.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is similar to an inkjet printer with the exception that there is a small heater used to heat the ink?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Bubble jet printers are similar to inkjet with the exception that there is a small heater used to heat the ink.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What technology allows for memory and CPU to be dynamically allocated to the VMs as required?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The benefit derived from the virtualization product (also called a hypervisor) using hardware-assisted virtualization is that it allows the hypervisor to dynamically allocate memory and CPU to the VMs as required.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a reason that 2.5² hard drives are used in laptops instead of 3.5² hard drives?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
2.5² hard drives are smaller, produce less heat, and use less power, but in comparison to 3.5² hard drives they have less capacity and cache and operate at a lower speed.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: On an ATX, there is a single power connector consisting of a block of how many holes (in two rows)?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
On an ATX, there is a single power connector consisting of a block of 24 holes (in two rows).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a tape-cartridge format?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Exabyte tapes are 8-millimeter cartridges, but there are no 9mm tapes.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a high-speed type of RAM memory?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Rambus dynamic RAM (RDRAM) is a high-speed type of RAM.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A client has recently purchased an LCD monitor that has an uncharacteristically shiny finish on the screen. The client complains about the glare from surrounding lights. Which of the following is the best solution to the client’s problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Antiglare filters actually exist. You would prefer to use one instead of a privacy filter if glare is the only complaint. Although some privacy filters might solve some of, or the entire, glare problem, they also limit the viewing angle of the monitor. The brightness of the image is not the problem, and you cannot adjust the fixed contrast ratio, only contrast.

answers.textAnswer: Increase the contrast ratio of the display.
Turn down the brightness on the display.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following services leases IP addresses to hosts?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The DHCP service leases IP addresses to hosts and automatically configures them to use the TCP/IP network.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: ATA-7 supports transfers of up to what speed?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
ATA-7 supports UltraDMA/133, with transfer modes of up to 150 MBps.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: ______________ is a user interface feature used by dragging your finger up and down or left and right to access common tasks on the screen. This movement is akin to scrolling the screen left and right or scrolling the screen up and down.
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Touchflow or TouchFLO is a user interface feature designed by HTC. It is used by dragging your finger up and down or left and right to access common tasks on the screen. This movement is akin to scrolling the screen left and right or scrolling the screen up and down.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You suspect that there is a problem with a customer’s serial ports. Which of the following devices is used to test a serial port?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Various versions of loopback connectors are used to test ports, such as serial and network interfaces and are often used as part of the troubleshooting process. A print driver is software that enables the printer to communicate with the operating system. A multimeter measures voltage, among other things, and a cable tester certifies cables for their intended purpose.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding the refresh rate of a monitor?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If the monitor does not support a given refresh rate, setting the adapter to such a rate will result in no image or a flickering image being displayed. The monitor might also display an “out of range” error until the rate is adjusted to a supported one. The refresh rate is adjusted through the display adapter’s properties in Windows 8 and through the Display Settings dialog in Windows Vista and Windows 7.

answers.textAnswer: Adjusting the refresh rate does not affect the quality of the displayed image.
As long as the graphics adapter supports a given refresh rate, the monitor will support it.
The refresh rate is adjusted through Device Manager.
Both the monitor and graphics adapter must be correctly identifiable in the operating system by using the correct drivers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What are two methods of recovering a forgotten BIOS password?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-4}.
To reset a forgotten password, you can remove the CMOS battery to reset everything. There also may be a Reset jumper on the motherboard.

answers.textAnswer: Using the reset jumper in the motherboard

unsortedQuestions.questionText: If Automatic Private IP Addressing is being used with IPv4, in what ip address range will a host’s IP address be?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If a DHCP server cannot be found, the clients automatically assign themselves an IPv4 address, somewhat randomly, in the 169.254.x.x range.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum capacity for a standard SD card?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The maximum capacity for a standard SD card is 4 GB.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a term relating to CPUs?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The communication between a CPU and the rest of the system is considered I/O from the perspective of the CPU, but an I/O port is not used for this purpose. I/O ports, such as USB or sound ports, are not directly related to the CPU.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What type of laptop memory has 144 pins?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
SODIMMs have 144 pins, and MicroDIMMs have 172 pins. MiniDIMM and SlotDIMM are not valid standards

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the top upload speed possible with SDSL?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
With SDSL (symmetric DSL), the top upload speed is 1.5 Mbps. The top download speed is also 1.5 Mbps.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which bus connects the RAM to the CPU?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The address bus connects the RAM to the CPU.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following cannot be monitored in the BIOS?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
NIC traffic rates cannot be monitored in the BIOS.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the width of the USB bus?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Because USB is a serial interface, its width is 1 bit.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Laptops often allow you to switch the display to an external monitor. This is accomplished through what type of key combination?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
This is accomplished through an Fn key combination (for example, Fn+F8 on most Dells, Fn+F4 on many HPs, and so on).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Laptop memory comes in a small form factor and is known as:
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Laptop memory comes in small form factors known as small outline DIMMs (SODIMMs).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What type of PC card is used for memory?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Type I is used mostly for memory. These are rarely used in today’s systems since the new laptops have other means of increasing memory, such as SODIMMs.

answers.textAnswer: PCMCIA cards cannot be used for memory.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following communication technologies is designed for use with peripheral devices such as keyboards, mice, and wireless headsets?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.

Bluetooth was made to work as a wireless personal area network (WPAN). As such, it’s perfect for computer peripherals such as keyboards, mice, and wireless headsets.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Your mobile device is not changing the screen position when you move it. What component is malfunctioning?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The accelerometer changes the screen orientation from landscape to portrait based on the position of the device. If it is not working correctly, this behavior will occur.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which twisted pair wiring standard specifies the pin arrangements for the RJ-45 connectors on UTP or STP cables?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The pin arrangements for the RJ-45 connectors on UTP or STP cables are specified by wiring standards T568A (older) and T568B (newer).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Replacing which of the following items usually requires soldering?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Replacing a bad DC jack usually requires soldering. If this is not a skill you possess, just replace the motherboard.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a laser printer that keeps jamming. When you talk to the printer manufacturer’s support reps, they ask what caliper of paper you are using. What are they referring to?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Caliper refers to the thickness of the paper.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: At what port does Telnet run?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Telnet runs at port 23.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: How many bits are included in IPv4 binary addresses?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
IP addresses are 32-bit binary numbers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following items cannot be set through CMOS setup?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The most common settings to adjust in CMOS include port settings (parallel, serial, USB), drive types, boot sequence, date and time, and virus/security protections, but they do not include IP address.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not an example of a memory-card format?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
There is no micro version of CompactFlash modules. The other options represent legitimate memory-card formats.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which type of network cable is a specific type rated for use in heating and air-conditioning systems?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Plenum cable is a specific type of cable that is rated for use in plenum spaces. Plenum spaces are areas in a building used for heating and air-conditioning systems.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are installing a printer for a medical firm. They will print carbonless three-part forms on this printer. One form will go in the patient’s file, one will go to the insurance company, and one will be mailed to the patient. Which type of printer would you recommend they use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In a situation where someone is using a multi-part form, a printer that makes an impact on the paper is required. Of the choices listed, only dot-matrix printers are impact printers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The built-in network card on a user’s laptop isn’t working. What things should you have her check first? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2}.
The first two things to check would be to see if there are any lights and to ensure that the card didn’t get turned off by accident. Those are the easy ones. If the card appears to be on, then you can try to plug it in and see if it works, if she has a cable.

answers.textAnswer: See if there are any connectivity lights.
Make sure that the network card switch didn’t get turned off accidentally.
Plug the network card into a cable and see if it works.
Check her TCP/IP settings to make sure she’s getting an IP address from a DHCP server.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Up to how many USB devices can share a single set of system resources?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Some of the advantages of USB include hot-plugging and the capability for up to 127 USB devices to share a single set of system resources.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following devices go into a DIMM slot?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The listed devices would be placed in the following slot types:
  • Video card: Advanced Graphics Processor (AGP) slots were made to provide better support for video card.
  • Memory: This will go into either a SIMM or DIMM slot.
  • CPU: This will fit into a slot called a socket such as LGA 775.
  • Sound card: This most likely will use a PCI slot.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following display technologies should not be used at high altitudes?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Plasma subpixels are created by filling tiny chambers with a gas that reacts to changes in external pressure, which is affected by changes in altitude. Visual quality can suffer, but the real problem comes from the noises that can be emitted by the display.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the aspect ratio of 1080p? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
B,{answer-3}.
The resolution known as 1080p is actually 1920 x 1080, which is the same resolution denoted as 1080i; the only difference being that i stands for interlaced, which means that every other line is drawn during each cycle, which does not affect the aspect ratio. Dividing 1920 by 1080 produces the same value as dividing 16 by 9: 1.778, which means that 1080p has a 16:9 aspect ratio.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not held in CMOS memory while the system power is off?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The CMOS memory only stores hardware-level settings, not those related to operating systems. Those settings are kept in files maintained by the operating systems.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A BIOS intrusion detection notification informs you of what?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
This may also be referred to as chassis intrusion detection or possibly a case open warning.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following could an administrator use to manage the amount of bandwidth provided to applications that don’t function well with lags—voice and video, for example?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Quality of service (QoS) describes the strategies used to manage the flow of network traffic. A network administrator can use QoS to manage the amount of bandwidth provided to applications that are latency sensitive.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the default subnet mask for a Class B address in IPv4?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The default subnet mask for a Class B address is 255.255.0.0.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not an item you can sync between a mobile device and another device or location?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Items that can be synced include contacts, email, pictures, music, and video, but not updates.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: By default, what port (or ports) does the FTP service use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
By default, the FTP service uses ports 20 and 21.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which type of cache holds data that is waiting to enter the CPU?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Level 1 cache, also known as the L1 or front-side cache, holds data that is waiting to enter the CPU.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum number of devices that can be supported by USB?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Though it is unlikely that it would ever be necessary, a single USB chain can theoretically support 127 different peripheral devices. This includes scanners, cameras, MP3 players, printers, keyboards, and so on.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: At what speed does USB 1.1 run?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
USB 1.1 runs at 12 Mbps, and USB 2.0 runs at 480 Mbps.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following would not be a reason to use a KVM switch?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If multiple systems need to be accessed directly at the same time, a KVM switch is not an acceptable solution because it allows access to only one system at a time.

answers.textAnswer: There is only one administrator employed by the company.
Most server access is done remotely.
Four coworkers with their own computer systems and working on the same project are seated in four cubicles that form a square.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following would most likely be the cause of vertical white lines running down a page coming from a laser printer?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The vertical white lines are caused by foreign matter (more than likely toner) caught on the transfer corona wire.

answers.textAnswer: A scratch in the EP drum
Foreign matter on the transfer corona wire

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the firmware called that contains settings that can be manipulated and diagnostic utilities that can be used to monitor the device?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2} .
This firmware called the Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) contains settings that can be manipulated and diagnostic utilities that can be used to monitor the device.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A _________________ once activated stays in contact with a monitoring center, allowing you to send the commands to lock the device and delete data via the center if the device is stolen.
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
LoJack is a product made by Absolute Software that allows you to remotely locate and lock the device and delete the data on a mobile device when it is stolen.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is an area where you can place a public server for access by people you might not trust otherwise?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A demilitarized zone (DMZ) is an area where you can place a public server for access by people you might not trust otherwise. By isolating a server in a DMZ, you can hide or remove access to other areas of your network. You can still access the server using your network, but others aren’t able to access further network resources.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following networking terms is used to signify delays?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Latency is the networking term used for delays

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is any machine or interface that participates in a TCP/IP network?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A host is any machine or interface that participates in a TCP/IP network, whether as a client or as a server. Every interface on a TCP/IP network that must be issued an IP address is considered a host.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the most common reason for moving the DVD drive to the top of the boot order?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Although it is possible to boot to an operating system on a DVD, that is not the most common reason for moving the DVD to the top of the list. You might set the DVD drive first to boot from a Windows 7 Setup disk on a system that already contains an operating system.

answers.textAnswer: To listen to music on the DVD
To copy data off the DVD
To boot to an operating system on the DVD

unsortedQuestions.questionText: On an inkjet printer, calibration is more commonly known as which of the following?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
On an inkjet printer, calibration is more commonly known as head alignment.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the capacity of data that a single-sided, single-density DVD normally holds?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A single-sided, single-density DVD normally holds 4.7 GB of data. In a double-sided, double-layered configuration, this can stretch to as much as 17 GB.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following slot types used for video is being replaced by PCI Express?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
As systems got faster, PC game players wanted games that had better graphics, more realism, and more speed. However, as the computers got faster, the video technology couldn’t seem to keep up, even with the PCI bus. The AGP bus was developed to meet this need. Since 2004 this has been increasingly replaced by PCI Express.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not an advantage of the daisy-wheel printer?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The daisy-wheel printer is much slower when compared to the dot-matrix printer, and therefore speed is a disadvantage.

answers.textAnswer: Print quality that’s comparable to a typewriter

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following options describes video resolution?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Resolution is most often represented numerically as columns x rows.

answers.textAnswer: The number of colors that a pixel can display at any one time
Whether each pixel is controlled by one or two transistors
The difference in brightness between adjacent pixels
The number of pixels displayed represented in column and row measurements

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the most common expansion slot found in PCs?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The PCIe or PCI Express is the most common slot found in today’s computers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the speed at which IEEE 1394a transfers data?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
IEEE 1394 transfers data at 400 Mbps and supports up to 63 chained devices on a single set of resources.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: ________________ is a measurement of the rate at which the clock signal oscillates and is expressed in millions of cycles per second or megahertz.
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The clock speed, or external speed, is the speed at which the motherboard communicates with the CPU. It’s determined by the motherboard, and its cadence is set by a quartz crystal (the system crystal) that generates regular electrical pulses.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are common types of Mini PCIe card devices? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-4}.
Hard drive controllers, network cards, and sound cards can all be found in Mini PCIe forms. Hard drives and processors are not made in Mini PCI form.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is considered the IPv4 loopback address?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
On all TCP/IP IPv4 implementations, 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the autoconfigured address range in IPv6?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The autoconfigured address range in IPv6 is FE80::. In IPv4, it is 169.254.0.0.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What motor is used by an impact printer to move the print head back and forth?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A stepper motor is a motor that can move in small increments. Printers use stepper motors to move the print head back and forth as well as to advance the paper.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: WPA increased security by using what to scramble encryption keys?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
WPA was able to increase security by using Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) to scramble encryption keys using a hashing algorithm. The keys are issued an integrity check to verify they have not been modified or tampered with during transit.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which connectors are used to connect a DSL modem to a network card and to a phone line? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
The network card connects to the DSL modem using a standard RJ-45 connector, and the DSL modem connects to the phone jack using a phone cord that has RJ-11 connectors.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The size and shape of a motherboard is called its _______________.
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
There are a number of different sizes, or form factors, of motherboards.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the distance limitation of 1000BaseLX fiber in multimode?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
In a multimode format, the distance limitation is 550 meters (in single-mode, it is 5 km).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following communication methods is point-to-point, limited to a distance of about 1 meter?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.

Infrared communications are point-to-point only and are limited to about 1 meter. Bluetooth can work up to 100 meters, depending on the version. Wireless Ethernet network signals can travel for several hundred meters, and cellular communications can span several kilometers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: True or False: Mobile devices do not require antivirus software.
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
False: Mobile devices can suffer from viruses and malware just like laptops and desktops. Major antivirus vendors such as McAfee and Kaspersky make antivirus products for mobile devices that provide the same real-time protection that the products do for desktops. The same guidelines apply for these mobile devices: keep them up to date by setting the device to check for updates whenever connected to the Internet.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following supports both digital and analog and can be obtained in both a single and dual link format?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
DVI-D connectors supply digital signals only. These can also come in a single- or dual-link format. A dual-link format allows provision for a second data link. DVI-A has pins that can provide analog and digital. This type comes in a single-link format only. DVI-I provides analog and digital. These can also come in a single- or dual-link format. There is no DVI-B.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Printer drivers vary based on which of the following?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The printer drivers vary based on the operating system being used on the client computer. If a printer is attached to more than one operating system, you have to make sure you have the appropriate driver for each operating system in use.

answers.textAnswer: The operating system being used on the file server
The operating system being used on the printer host
The operating system being used on the client computer

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following form factors is normally used for set-top boxes, media centers, and car computers?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Nano-ITX is even smaller than the Mini-ITX and is used for set-top boxes, media centers, and car computers.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a chip found in the motherboard that can enhance drive encryption security?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When the device has a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) chip present on the motherboard, additional security and options become available for drive encryption.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a potential disadvantage to dual-rail power supplies?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Although they supply more power overall, when compared to single-rail power supplies, dual-rail power supplies split their 12VDC power between their rails. If any one component requires more power than is available on its specific rail, it may be underpowered and not work.

answers.textAnswer: Overall, they supply less power than single-rail power supplies.
One of the rails is 12VDC, while the other is only 5VDC.
The output is split between AC and DC, but internal components require only DC.
The higher collective power is split into two lesser groups.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is another term for a cluster?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Clusters and allocation units are the same. During the formatting of a partition, individual sectors are collected in configurable, fixed-sized sets. The operating system uses a unique numerical cluster identifier to reference each set of sectors.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You need to install a network segment that can run several kilometers without any signal regeneration. Which of the following would you select?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Fiber-optic cable can span distances of several kilometers because it has much lower crosstalk and interference when compared to standard copper cables.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following supplies both an I/O path for peripherals and 45W of power per interface for those peripherals?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
FireWire, or IEEE 1394, supplies a pathway for peripherals to communicate at high speeds with the host system. FireWire also supplies 45W of DC power to peripherals, powering devices such as security cameras and wireless access points. USB is similar, but supplies a mere fraction of the power available with FireWire, less than 5W when not specifically used for charging external devices.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What laser printer component applies &#8211;600V to the drum?
unsortedQuestions.explanation: The primary corona wire applies &#8211;600V. The primary corona wire charges the drum with &#8211;600V before the image is written on it.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which component is responsible for managing POST?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The BIOS begins and manages the execution of the power-on self-test (POST) when the computer performs a cold boot.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following can help to improve the sharpness of display quality?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Increasing the refresh rate serves to sharpen a display’s image, as long as the monitor supports the selected rate.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What type of power adapter would a laptop use when plugged in to a power receptacle in an automobile?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Automobiles provide direct current (DC) power. Wall outlets provide alternating current (AC) power. NiCd and NiMH are types of laptop batteries.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What technology allows for network devices to be placed in locations where there are no electrical outlets?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Power over Ethernet (PoE) allows electrical power to be supplied via network cables.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following benefit A/V editors most when a custom workstation is used?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A/V editors benefit from the use of multiple monitors to extend the size of the desktop. Fast drives are ideal, but not at the expense of size. SSDs can have very fast access rates, but are not as large as conventional drives yet.

answers.textAnswer: Two monitors with an extended Desktop

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which device in an inkjet printer contains the print head?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In an inkjet printer, the ink cartridge is the actual print head. This is where the ink is expelled to form letters or graphics. Toner cartridges are used by laser printers to store toner. A daisy wheel is the device that impacts the letters on the paper in a daisy-wheel printer. Paper trays are the storage bins in laser printers and inkjet printers that allow the pickup rollers to feed the paper into the printer.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: How many pins does a MicroDIMM memory module have?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A MicroDIMM chip has 172 pins. SODIMM memory chips have 144, 200, or 204 pins.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which motherboard slots feature varieties that have 168 pins, 184 pins, and 240 pins?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The pin counts listed are for SDR SDRAM, DDR SDRAM, and DDR2/DDR3 SDRAM, respectively.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have just installed and networked six computers together. One of the users shares a printer from his computer, and all other users share various files from their computers. This network is an example of which network design?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In a peer-to-peer network, the computers act as both service providers and service requestors. Peer-to-peer networks are great for small, simple, inexpensive networks. This model can be set up almost immediately, with little extra hardware required.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following refers to a laptop backlight?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Many laptops use a cold cathode fluorescent lamp (CCFL) as a backlight.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which elements are required to communicate on a TCP/IP network? (Choose all that apply.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2}.
To communicate on a TCP/IP network, you need to have a unique IP address and a valid subnet mask. A default gateway and DNS server are optional.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You need to leave your laptop in an unsecured office. What should you use to keep it from being stolen?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A cable lock can be used to secure your laptop to a desk to prevent its theft.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which protocol within TCP/IP is responsible for network addressing?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Internet Protocol is responsible for network addressing as part of TCP/IP. IPX is not part of the TCP/IP suite. UDP and TCP provide connectionless and connection-oriented delivery, respectively.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Who manages GPS?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Global Positioning System (GPS) is a satellite-based navigation system managed by the United States Department of Defense. It is free for commercial use.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is a virtualization workstation?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A virtualization workstation is a host system and operating system that runs one or more guest operating systems in virtual machines.

answers.textAnswer: A workstation running within a virtual machine
A centralized workstation that manages the virtual machines of an enterprise running on other devices
An operating system running in RAM on a thin client that has no hard drive
A workstation that runs virtual machines

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting an older laser printer. Which of these is not one of the seven stages of the electrophotographic (EP) print process?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The seven stages in the EP print process are processing, conditioning, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which video technology supports both analog and digital signals, each requiring a cable with different connectors from the other?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
DVI cables and interfaces are available in analog and digital varieties. The two are not compatible or convertible.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are administering a system that has been locked down for security reasons. You notice that among all of the other ports, port 21 has been disabled. What service is associated with port 21?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
FTP uses ports 20 and 21. HTTP uses 80, Telnet uses 23, and HTTPS uses 443.
