The monitor has a resolution of 16:9. You can determine this by dividing the first number in the resolution by 16 and multiplying the result by 9. It should equal the second number. (Or, you can just multiply the second number by 1.778, and it should equal the first number. For 16:10 you would multiply the second number by 1.6, and it should equal the first.) 16:9 is the aspect ratio for high-definition television.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A laser printer you are working on is producing images that have vertical black streaks running the length of the page. Which of the following could be causing this? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-4}.
A groove or scratch in the EP drum can cause the problem of vertical black lines running down all or part of the page. Because a scratch is lower than the surface, it doesn’t receive as much (if any) of a charge as the other areas. The result is that toner sticks to it as though it were discharged. The groove may go around the circumference of the drum, so the line may go all the way down the page. Another possible cause of vertical black lines is a dirty charging corona wire. A dirty charging corona wire prevents a sufficient charge from being placed on the EP drum. Because the charge on the EP drum is almost zero, toner sticks to the areas that correspond to the dirty areas on the charging corona.

answers.textAnswer: Fusing assembly not heating up properly

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have installed an 802.11g Wi-Fi network. The network has three overlapping wireless access points. What channels should you set the access points to in order to avoid communications problems?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
To avoid communications problems, you need to set the wireless access points to have nonoverlapping channels. In 802.11g, the three non-overlapping channels are 1, 6, and 11.

answers.textAnswer: Any three different channels will work fine.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are installing an ATX power supply. Which of the following is not a voltage provided by the power supply?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
ATX power supplies provide the following voltages for the computer: +3.3VDC, +5VDC, –5VDC (on older systems), +12VDC, and –12VDC. The 12v connectors have either four or eight pins.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user complains that his desktop computer randomly reboots. He does not see any error messages before it happens, and there is not a specific program that triggers the reboot. Which of the following components is most likely to be causing this problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Memory problems can cause system lockups, unexpected shutdowns or reboots, or errors such as Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) in Windows or the rotating pinwheel in MacOS. CPUs problems can also cause intermittent rebooting.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user calls the help desk to report that she has no network connectivity. She had connectivity yesterday, but when she booted up her desktop computer this morning, she could not connect. She does not use the wireless network. No other users have reported issues. What is the first thing you should do?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Rule #1 of troubleshooting is to always check your connections first. The most common issue that prevents network connectivity on a wired network is a bad or unplugged patch cable.

answers.textAnswer: Check to see whether the network card driver is responding.
Run IPCONFIG to see what her IP address is.
Use a loopback plug to test the network card.
Check to ensure that the network cable is plugged in.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following wireless connection types generally has a functional communication distance of 10 meters?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The vast majority of consumer Bluetooth mobile devices are Class 2 devices, which have a maximum communication distance of 10 meters.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The Southbridge on a motherboard is responsible for managing which type of communications?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Northbridge is responsible for managing high-speed peripheral communications. The Southbridge manages slower onboard peripherals.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In your company’s lobby, there is a desktop computer with an LCD monitor that plays a continuous loop of a welcome video. The monitor is enclosed in a cabinet. Recently, the monitor will shut itself down near the end of the day, for no apparent reason. What is likely causing this problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Monitors have their own internal power supply, and they can overheat. Overheating was more common with CRT displays than LCDs, but it still happens. Make sure the air vents on the back of the monitor are dust and debris free. In this case, removing the monitor from the cabinet might help. If the problem persists, it’s best to replace the monitor.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: One of your network users develops software for multiple operating systems. He asks for a specialized computer that will allow him to run multiple operating systems at the same time in virtualized environments. Which two components should you optimize in his computer? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-2}.
This user needs a virtualization workstation. To ensure that the operating systems have the most resources possible, optimize the processors (the more cores, the better) and memory.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The design of the micro-ATX motherboard makes which of the following statements true?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The micro-ATX form factor is designed to work in standard ATX cases, as well as its own smaller cases.

answers.textAnswer: It will fit in standard ATX cases.
It will fit in standard ATX cases when used with a mounting adapter kit.
It will fit in standard ATX cases but can’t support full-length expansion cards.
It will not fit in standard ATX cases.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A 32-bit PCI expansion bus will operate at one of which of the following two data rates? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
PCI expansion buses operate at 33MHz or 66MHz (version 2.1) over a 32-bit (4-byte) channel, resulting in data rates of 133MBps and 266MBps, respectively, with 133MBps being the most common, server architectures excluded.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which two TCP/IP protocols are designed to download email from mail servers? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3), and Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) are all email protocols. SMTP is for sending email. POP3 and IMAP are for downloading email.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are testing the power levels provided to the paper transport motor inside a laser printer. What voltage does this motor require?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The DC power supply (DCPS) converts house current into three voltages: +5VDC and –5VDC for the logic circuitry and +24VDC for the paper-transport motors.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are examining an existing coaxial cable installation and notice that the previous technician installed a splitter. Which of the following statements is true?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Splitters generally have two effects on a network cable: they degrade the signal and limit the distance the signal will travel. Use them judiciously.

answers.textAnswer: The splitter will degrade the quality of the network signal.
The splitter will cause the network connection to fail.
The splitter will increase the distance the network signal will travel.
The splitter will have no effect on the network signal.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Users on your network complain of poor wireless network access in a certain part of your building. They say that the connection is slow and disconnects frequently. You are using 802.11n wireless routers and access points. What tool should you use to troubleshoot the situation?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A wireless locator or a Wi-Fi analyzer can be either a handheld hardware device or specialized software that is installed on a laptop, and its purpose is to detect and analyze Wi-Fi signals.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A desktop computer will not retain the system time or date. The user always needs to reset them after their system is powered off. What should you do to fix the problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A fairly common issue with the BIOS is it fails to retain your computer’s settings, such as time and date and hard drive configuration. The BIOS uses a small battery (much like a watch battery) on the motherboard to help it retain settings when the system power is off. If this battery fails, the BIOS won’t retain its settings. Simply replace the battery to solve the problem.

answers.textAnswer: Use the jumper on the motherboard to set the BIOS back to factory specifications.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have just installed a new printer on a client’s workstation. When you attempt to print, nothing but garbled characters appear on the paper. Which two things are most likely to cause a problem like this? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
The correct printer driver needs to be installed for the printer and operating system. For example, if you have an HP LaserJet III and a Windows 7 computer, then you need to install an HP LaserJet III driver made for Windows 7. If this is not done, you will get garbage out of the printer. The other cause of several pages of garbage being printed is a bad formatter board. This circuit board takes the information the printer receives from the computer and turns it into commands for the various components in the printer. Usually, problems with the formatter board produce wavy lines of print or random patterns of dots on the page.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user has turned in a tablet computer that has a swollen battery. What should you do to resolve the problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you have a swollen battery, turn the device off immediately and make sure that it’s not plugged into a charger. It may be possible to remove the battery, but swollen batteries are more prone to explosions than normal ones because the casing is already compromised. The best course of action is to purchase a new device. Take the battery or device to a proper recycling center to dispose of it. Never just throw it in the trash because it can explode and harm sanitation workers, as well as cause significant damage to the environment.

answers.textAnswer: Turn the tablet off, let it cool down, and then return it to the user.
Order a new tablet for the user, drain the excess electrolyte from the battery, and then dispose of the defective one in the trash.
Order a new tablet for the user and dispose of the defective one in the trash.
Order a new tablet for the user and take the defective one to a recycling center.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a Windows 10 desktop computer that boots into VGA mode. You have tried changing the resolution and reinstalled the video driver, but it still will only boot into VGA mode. What should you do next?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When your system refuses to boot into anything other than VGA mode, it indicates one of two problems. Either the video card is set to a resolution that it can’t handle, or the video card driver isn’t loading properly. When in VGA mode, reset the video resolution to something you know the card can handle and reboot. If that doesn’t solve it, reinstall the driver. If it still doesn’t work, replace the video card.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a laptop computer that will not boot properly. When you power it on, there is nothing on the display, and you hear beeps in a pattern of 1-3-3. What two things could you use to troubleshoot the problem? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
The beeps are a BIOS beep code produced because there is an error in the POST routine. The manufacturer’s website will likely tell you what the beep code means, and you can also troubleshoot using a USB POST card. Laptops do not have PCIe slots, and there is no specific tool called a BOOT tester.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: When creating a custom computer configuration, what type of system will most benefit from high-end video card and cooling systems?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Gaming PCs should have multicore processors, high-end video cards, high-definition sound cards, and high-end cooling systems.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which RAM modules have 240 pins? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-2}.
DIMM DDR2 and DDR3 have 240 pins. SODIMM DDR2 has 200 pins, and SODIMM DDR3 has 204 pins.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Several Bluetooth devices are connected in an ad hoc network. Which acronym best describes this type of network?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A personal area network (PAN) is a small-scale network designed around one person within a limited boundary area. The term generally refers to networks that use Bluetooth technology.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Your motherboard supports up-plugging for PCIe adapter cards. Which of the following statements is true?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The x8 card won’t completely fill the x16 slot, but it will work at x8 speeds if up-plugging is supported by the motherboard. Otherwise, the specification requires up-plugged devices to operate at only the x1 rate.

answers.textAnswer: You can’t put an x8 card into an x16 slot.
You can put an x8 card into an x16 slot, but it will run at x1 speed.
You can put an x8 card into an x16 slot, and it will run at x8 speed.
You can put an x8 card into an x16 slot, and it will run at x16 speed.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You need to create several UTP patch cables from a roll of bulk cable. Your company uses the T568A standard. What is the correct order for wires in the connectors?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The correct order for a T568A patch (straight through) cable is white/green, green, white/orange, blue, white/blue, orange, white/brown, brown.

answers.textAnswer: White/orange, orange, white/green, blue, white/blue, green, white/brown, brown
White/orange, green, white/green, blue, white/blue, orange, white/brown, brown
White/green, green, white/orange, blue, white/blue, orange, white/brown, brown
White/green, green, orange, blue, white/blue, white/orange, white/brown, brown

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which computer component is most likely to use a DB15 connector?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A DB15 connector is most often used for VGA, or analog video, connections. Therefore, a monitor is the best choice.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about the function of the laser in the exposing step of the laser printer imaging process?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
In the exposing step, the image is written to the photosensitive imaging drum. Wherever the laser beam touches, the photosensitive drum’s charge is severely reduced from –600VDC to a slight negative charge (around –100VDC). As the drum rotates, a pattern of exposed areas is formed, representing the image to be printed.

answers.textAnswer: It increases the charge from +100VDC to +600VDC.
It decreases the charge from +600VDC to +100VDC.
It increases the charge from –100VDC to –600VDC.
It decreases the charge from –600VDC to –100VDC.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Your co-worker needs to transfer files from a mobile device using a memory card reader and an SD memory card. He quickly finds out that his maximum capacity is only 4GB. Which technology does he have?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Mobile devices often make use of small form factor memory cards, such as Secure Digital (SD), miniSD, or microSD cards. Higher-capacity versions of these cards are SDHC, SDXC, miniSDHC, microSDHC, and microSDXC. The standard versions can hold up to 4GB in storage, HC up to 32GB, and XC up to 2TB.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You need to purchase new RAM for two computer systems, both of which have an FSB speed of 667MHz. The computer specifications require DDR2. Which RAM modules should you purchase?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
For DDR2, multiply the bus speed by 8 to identify the type of memory needed. In this case, 667 ´ 8 equals 5333. The PC industry rounds this off to 5300.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You need to print documents containing sensitive information, but all the printers are in a shared workspace. Which technology will allow you to hold the print job until you enter a PIN on the printer?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
To use secure printing, go into the printer preferences (or a similar place) and indicate that it’s a secure print job. The document will not print until you physically go to the printer and enter the PIN.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A guest speaker plugs an external projector into her laptop, using the VGA port on the back of the laptop. The projector is on but just shows a blue screen instead of her presentation. What is the easiest way for her to fix this issue?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Because of the much smaller space available for keys, some laptop keys are consolidated into special multifunction keys. These keys are accessed through the standard keys by using a special function (Fn) key. Nearly every laptop has a video connector on the back or the side to plug in an external monitor or a projector. You will need to use the video toggle key to get this external port to work.

answers.textAnswer: Turn the projector off and back on to synchronize it with the laptop.
Press the Fn key on her keyboard and toggle the projector backlight Function key until the image appears.
Press the Fn key on her keyboard and toggle the video output Function key until the image appears.
Press the Fn key on her keyboard and toggle the screen brightness Function key until the image appears.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A technician is troubleshooting a computer in the field and calls you to report that she is getting a S.M.A.R.T. error ID 188, Command timeout. Which component is likely to be causing this error?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Nearly every hard drive is built with Self-Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting Technology (S.M.A.R.T.) software installed on it, which monitors hard drive reliability and theoretically can warn you in the event of an imminent failure.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user reports that when he presses the L key on his laptop keyboard, the L character repeats across the screen and doesn’t stop until he presses the L key several more times. When you look at the laptop, it does not appear that the key is physically sticking. What should you tell him to do next?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If a key on the laptop keyboard is stuck, you need to determine whether the contact is having problems or whether the key itself is stuck. If the key is not physically stuck but the laptop thinks it is, rebooting generally solves the problem.

answers.textAnswer: Clean under the key with compressed air.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A technician is configuring a wireless router for use on a small office network. If he wants to assign private IP addresses to client computers but still allow them to have Internet access from the ISP, what option does he need to configure?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Network Address Translation (NAT) is a service that translates private IP addresses on your internal network to a public IP address on the Internet. He may also choose to configure DHCP to make IP address configuration easier, but DHCP does not translate addresses like NAT does.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A technician has two hard drives and wants to increase the data access speed of her computer. Which of the following is her best option?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
RAID 0 is called disk striping. Data can be written to or read from multiple devices at the same time, increasing data access speed. However, if one drive fails, all data is lost. (Back up early and often!) RAID 1 is a mirror set, which does not increase data access but provides fault tolerance. RAID 5 is disk striping with parity, which provides both speed and fault tolerance but requires three hard disks.

answers.textAnswer: Install both drives and configure them as separate volumes.
Install both drives and implement RAID 0.
Install both drives and implement RAID 1.
Install both drives and implement RAID 5.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What type of converter requires power, either from its own source or from the interface it plugs into?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
VGA devices are analog and therefore cannot be driven passively by digital HDMI ports directly. An HDMI-to-VGA adapter must be active in nature, either powered externally or through the HDMI interface itself.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: During the charging step of the laser printer printing process, what charge is applied to the imaging drum?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
During the charging step, the charging corona uses a high voltage to apply a strong, uniform negative charge (around –600VDC) to the surface of the imaging drum.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are purchasing a mobile device that requires the use of a stylus to input information; it does not respond to the touch of a finger. What type of touch screen technology does this device use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Resistive touch screens respond to pressure, and they are highly accurate in detecting the position of the touch. These types of touch screens require the use of a stylus or other hard object, such as a fingernail.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum data throughput rate of a SATA 3 hard drive?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
SATA 1 has throughput of 1.5Gbps, SATA 2 is rated at 3Gbps, and SATA 3 is rated at 6Gbps. SATA speeds can be confusing because the naming does not line up well with the data rates.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In a laptop computer, which component is responsible for providing the right kind of energy to light the display?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Fluorescent lighting, and LCD backlights in particular, require fairly high-voltage, high-frequency energy. The component that provides the right kind of energy is the inverter. The inverter is a small circuit board installed behind the LCD panel that takes DC current and inverts it to AC for the backlight.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user complains of a burning smell and smoke coming from his computer. After shutting it down, you notice that the motherboard has burn marks on it. You replace the motherboard. The next day, the user complains of more smoke, and you see this motherboard is burnt as well. What should you do next?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If you have scorch marks on a component, say a video card or a motherboard, it could be that the specific component went bad. It could also be a sign of a problem with the power supply. If you replace the component and a similar problem occurs, definitely replace the power supply as well as the damaged component.

answers.textAnswer: Replace the motherboard and power supply.
Plug the computer into a different wall outlet.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have a network installation that requires transmission speeds of 10Gbps at a distance of 85 meters. Among the UTP standards listed, which one is the oldest one that meets the requirements for this network?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
CAT7 UTP can handle 10Gbps transmissions over 100 meters. CAT6 can handle 10Gbps, but only for 55 meters. CAT5 has a maximum speed of 100Mbps, and CAT5e has a maximum of 1Gbps.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a Windows 7 computer and suspect that the hard drive has some bad sectors. Which utility should you use to scan the hard drive and attempt to fix the bad sectors?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
You can use the Windows chkdsk utility to create and display status reports for the hard disk. chkdsk can also correct file system problems (such as cross-linked files) and scan for and attempt to repair disk errors.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not verified as part of the POST routine?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The POST routine verifies the BIOS integrity as well as the presence of multiple hardware devices, including RAM, boot devices, and system buses. It does not verify the integrity of the hard drive (such as looking for bad sectors).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A UTP cable just failed, and you need to replace it. You have a spool of cable and connectors but no pre-made cables. Which tool do you need to use to make a new cable?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A crimper is a handy tool for helping you put connectors on the end of a cable. Most crimpers will be a combination tool that strips and snips wires as well as crimps the connector onto the end.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are installing and configuring DHCP on one of your servers. What port numbers are used by DHCP? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) dynamically assigns IP addresses and other IP configuration information to network clients. It’s not considered a critical service requiring guaranteed data delivery, so it uses the connectionless UDP as its host-to-host layer protocol. It uses UDP 67 and UDP 68.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are contemplating purchasing either a tablet or an e-reader to read books and magazines. What are two advantages an e-reader has over a tablet? (Choose two.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
Most e-readers use a technology called electrophoretic ink, or E Ink, which is a proprietary type of electronic paper. It’s available in color but is often used in grayscales or black and white. E Ink allows for less energy use than other LCD displays, giving longer battery life, and it’s much easier to read in bright conditions. E-readers generally have less memory than tablets do.

answers.textAnswer: Easier to read in bright conditions

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user reports having an error message pop up and tell them that Windows has detected an IP address conflict. Your network uses a DHCP server. What should you do to resolve the problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The most common cause of an IP address conflict is if someone configures a computer with a static IP address that’s part of the DHCP server’s range. The DHCP server, not knowing that the address has been statically assigned somewhere, doles out the address and now there’s a conflict. Rebooting the computer won’t help, and neither will releasing the address and getting a new lease from the DHCP server—it’s just going to hand out the same address again because it doesn’t know that there’s a problem.

answers.textAnswer: On their computer, run ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew.
On the DHCP server, exclude their IP address from the scope.
On their computer, ensure that it’s set to Obtain An IP Address Automatically.
On their computer, ensure that it’s set to Use The Following IP Address.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A technician is troubleshooting a RAID 5 array with four hard disks. Two of the disks have failed. What can he do to recover the array?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you’re using RAID 5 (disk striping with parity), a single drive failure usually means that your data will be fine, provided you replace the failed drive. If you lose multiple drives at the same time, you will need to restore from backup.

answers.textAnswer: Rebuild the failed disks and restore from backup.
Remove the failed disks and rebuild the array.
Replace the failed disks and rebuild the array.
Replace the failed disks and restore from backup.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are at a Windows server with a command prompt open. You want to share the D:\corp\acctrec directory and have users connect to it with the name receipts. Which command is correct to do this?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The net share command is used to share folders on a network. (And net use will allow users to connect to them.) The proper syntax is net share <share_name>=<drive_letter>:<path>.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: MicroSD cards, often used in mobile phones, are the smallest memory cards commonly used. What is the size of a MicroSD card?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
MicroSD cards are 15mm × 11mm. xD Picture Cards are 25mm × 20mm, and miniSD cards are 21.5mm × 20mm. There is no current standard for an 11mm × 8mm memory card. For comparison, standard SD cards measure 32mm × 24mm.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a laptop that will not power up while plugged into a wall outlet. You verified that the outlet works and have tried a second AC adapter, but it still won’t power up when plugged in. If you unplug it from the wall, it will power up from the battery. What should you do to get it to power up while plugged into the wall outlet?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The first thing to try is to remove the battery and then see whether it will power up using AC power. This usually works. Longer term, you may want to replace the battery.

answers.textAnswer: Remove the battery, power it up, and reinsert the battery.
Drain the battery completely and then power it up.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: When setting up your network, you configured your clients to obtain IP addressing information automatically from a DHCP server. Which of the following configuration items can the DHCP server provide?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The DHCP server can provide all required and optional TCP/IP configuration information to clients. This includes an IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS server address.

answers.textAnswer: IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway
IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS server address

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Your office just increased from 20 to about 40 people. Everyone uses the same laser printer. When you print, jobs are often processed very slowly. Other than get a new printer, what can you do to help eliminate the problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If print jobs are processed very slowly or if you are continually seeing “low memory” error messages, it might be a good time to upgrade the memory in the printer.

answers.textAnswer: Stop and restart the print spooler.
Implement printing priorities for the most important users.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have configured four 1TB hard drives as a RAID 10 array. After the array is configured, how much usable storage space will you have for data?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A RAID 10 array is a mirror of a striped set. You need two drives to create the striped set, and the other two will mirror the first two. Therefore, you have only 2TB worth of storage in this configuration.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A client has an older Windows 7 laptop with an integrated 802.11b network adapter. She wants faster wireless access, and the network access points all support 802.11n. What is the best way to upgrade her system?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The easiest way is to install an external NIC. Windows should detect the new card and disable the old one. If it doesn’t, you can disable it manually in Device Manager.

answers.textAnswer: Remove the old card, and replace it with an internal 802.11n NIC.
Leave the old card in the system, and add a new internal 802.11n mini-PCIe NIC. The system will automatically disable the old card.
Add a USB 802.11n NIC. If needed, disable the old card in Device Manager.
Add a USB 802.11n NIC. If needed, disable the old card in System Manager.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a Windows 7 desktop computer that does not produce video when it boots. You tried a second monitor, one that you know works, on this computer and there still is no video. What should you do to fix the problem?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Trying another monitor quickly narrowed down this problem. It’s not the monitor, so it’s the video card. Video connectors are not field replaceable, so just replace the entire video card.

answers.textAnswer: Replace the video connector on the video card.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In the laser printer printing process, which step comes immediately before the fusing step?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The order of steps is as follows: processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: On an IPv6 network, if you want to send a single message to a group of computers at the same time, what type of address class do you need to use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
There are three types of addresses in IPv6: unicast, anycast, and multicast. A unicast address identifies a single node on the network. An anycast address refers to one that has been assigned to multiple nodes. A multicast address is one used by multiple hosts. IPv6 does not use broadcasts.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which TCP/IP Internet layer protocol is responsible for resolving IP addresses to MAC addresses?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
At the Internet layer of TCP/IP, Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) resolves logical IP addresses to physical MAC addresses built into network cards. Reverse ARP (RARP) resolves MAC addresses to IP addresses.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In IPv6, which address range is the multicast range?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The FF00::/8 range in IPv6 is for multicasts. Remember that IPv6 does not use broadcasts. The closest IPv6 gets is the use of multicast addresses.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Data transfers for which wireless connection type will be interrupted if someone walks between the sending and receiving devices?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Infrared is a short-distance, line-of-sight wireless communication method. If line of sight is broken, the communication will end.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are configuring a wireless 802.11ac router for its first use. Which of the following configuration options is recommended?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
When configuring a router, you should take five steps. Change the router’s SSID, change the administrator username and password, select strong encryption such as AES or WPA2, choose a high-quality security passphrase, and connect the clients using the passphrase.

answers.textAnswer: Choose WPA as the encryption method.
Leave the administrator password as the default.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which network device comes in two types: active, which is powered, and passive, which is not?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Hubs can be either active or passive. Passive hubs connect all ports electrically but do not have their own power source. Active hubs use electronics to amplify and clean up the signal before it is broadcast to the other ports.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: How much data throughput does a PCIe 1.1 x16 slot provide when operating bidirectionally?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
There are four major versions of PCIe currently specified: 1.x, 2.x, 3.0, and 4.0. For the four versions, a single omnidirectional lane (such as in x1) operates at a data rate of 250MBps, 500MBps, approximately 1GBps, and roughly 2GBps, respectively. A bidirectional slot doubles the data rate. An x16 slot will operate 16 times as fast as x1.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are purchasing a new LCD monitor for a small conference room. It will be viewed by people sitting at wide angles to the screen. Which technology should you purchase?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The two most popular methods of manufacturing LCD panels are twisted nematic (TN) and in-plane switching (IPS). Of the two, IPS is regarded as having the best color representation in all angles, while TN is faster and less expensive. Fluorescent and LED are types of backlighting.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A technician needs to choose an optical disc technology that provides the greatest storage space possible. Which technology will best meet her needs?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Of the three optical disc technologies, Blu-ray provides the most capacity over DVD and CD-ROM. Blu-ray double-sided, dual-layer (DS, DL) provides 100GB of storage space, whereas single-sided, single-layer (SS, SL) provides 25GB.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following cellular technologies offers the best potential performance?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
4G Long Term Evolution (LTE) offers potential data rates competitive with 802.11 standards.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following devices goes into an AGP slot?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Advanced Graphics Processor (AGP) slots were made to provide better support for video cards.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Your mobile device is not responding correctly to your touch. What needs to be adjusted?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
For a touchscreen device to operate correctly—that is, for it to properly interpret your touch and react accordingly—it must be calibrated correctly. When you touch an item on the screen and nothing happens or a movement that normally results in an expected reaction does not, the calibration of the device is off.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Accelerometers and gyroscopes are used to manage what function in a mobile device?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Both accelerometers and gyroscopes can be used by mobile devices to determine the movement and tilt of the device. This means the device can tell which way the screen is being held. It uses this information to automatically adjust the display orientation appropriately with no action on the part of the user.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: By default, what port (or ports) does the IMAP service use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
By default, the IMAP service uses port 143.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which type of cache holds data that is exiting the CPU?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Level 2 cache, also known as the L2 or back-side cache, holds data that is exiting the CPU and is waiting to return to RAM.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: At what speed does USB 2.0 run?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
USB 1.1 runs at 12 Mbps, and USB 2.0 runs at 480 Mbps.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which connector is used to connect a computer to an Ethernet network?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A standard RJ-45 connector is used to connect a computer to an Ethernet network.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You are wearing a smart watch enabled with GPS and are hiking in the mountains. How many satellites must your watch communicate with for you to know your location and elevation?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
GPS systems were designed to require multiple satellites. Receivers use a process called triangulation, which they use to calculate the distance between themselves and the satellites (based on the time it takes to receive a signal) to determine their location. They require input from four satellites to provide location and elevation or from three to provide location.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The AES security algorithm was introduced with which Wi-Fi encryption standard?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) is a huge improvement over WEP and WPA. It uses Counter Mode CBC-MAC Protocol (CCMP), which is a protocol based on the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) security algorithm. CCMP-AES was created to address the shortcomings of TKIP, so consequently it’s much stronger than TKIP.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum speed of an ExpressCard 1.x card running in PCIe 1.0 x1 mode?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
ExpressCard 1.x cards running in PCIe 1.0 x1 mode have a maximum speed of 2.5Gbps. ExpressCard 1.x cards running in USB 2.0 mode have a maximum speed of 480Mbps.

examQuestions.questionText: Which editions of Windows Vista support Local Security Policy (secpol.msc)? (Choose three.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3},{answer-4},{answer-5}.
Only the Business, Enterprise, and Ultimate editions of Windows Vista support Local Security Policy (secpol.msc).

examQuestions.questionText: Which utility is the System Configuration tool in Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.

The System Configuration tool is msconfig.exe in Windows Vista.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the first file used in the boot process of Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The first file used in the Windows Vista boot process is BOOTMGR.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is an Ethernet standard implemented via a card that allows a "sleeping" machine to awaken when it receives a wakeup signal?
examQuestions.explanation: Wake on LAN is an Ethernet standard implemented via a card that allows a "sleeping" machine to awaken when it receives a wakeup signal.

examQuestions.questionText: Which editions of Windows Vista include BitLocker support? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-4}.
Only the Enterprise and Ultimate editions of Windows Vista include support for BitLocker.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Windows Vista feature allows you to recover from an accidental deletion or overwrite?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Shadow Copy is a Windows Vista feature that allows you to recover from an accidental deletion or overwrite.

examQuestions.questionText: You are migrating one stand-alone machine from Windows XP to Window Vista. Which of the following tools should you consider for transferring user state data and application files?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
For just one machine, Windows Easy Transfer should be used for transferring user state data and application files. For a mass rollout across a network, USMT can be used.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following files is at the end of the boot process and presents the user with the Logon screen?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
WINLOGON presents the Logon screen and wraps up the boot process.

examQuestions.questionText: Where is the Windows Memory Diagnostics utility found in Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Windows Memory Diagnostics utility (Start > Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Memory Diagnostics Tool) can be used to check a system for memory problems.

answers.textAnswer: In the System folder, beneath Accessories

examQuestions.questionText: After installation of the Windows Vista operating system, what is required in order to curb software piracy?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Windows Vista requires the installation to be followed by a process known as product activation to curb software piracy.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum number of physical CPUs supported by Windows Vista Business edition?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The maximum number of physical CPUs supported by Windows Vista Business edition is two. Both Home Basic and Home Premium editions support only one, while Business, Enterprise, and Ultimate support two.

examQuestions.questionText: Which feature allows you to use free space on a removable drive (usually USB) to speed up a system?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The ReadyBoost feature allows you to use free space on a removable drive (usually USB) to speed up a system.

examQuestions.questionText: Spencer has dug out from the closet a legacy machine that is running Windows XP Professional. Since it is no longer supported, he wants to upgrade it to Windows Vista. Which of the following upgrades are possible? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-4}.
Windows XP Professional can only be upgraded to Windows Vista Business and Windows Vista Ultimate.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following network locations disables network discovery in Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
When the network location is set to Public, network discovery is disabled. Network discovery is enabled for both Home and Work. There is no such location as Personal in Windows Vista.

examQuestions.questionText: Which directory on a standard Windows Vista installation holds the boot file configuration?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
On a standard, default installation, the /boot directory holds the boot file configuration for Windows Vista.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum amount of RAM supported in the 64-bit Ultimate edition of Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The 64-bit Enterprise, and Ultimate editions support 128GB. The maximum amount of RAM supported by Home Premium is 16GB. The Home Basic edition supports only 8GB.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum amount of RAM supported in the 64-bit Home Premium edition of Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The maximum amount of RAM supported by 64-bit Home Premium is 16GB. The Business, Enterprise, and Ultimate editions support 128GB. The Home Basic edition supports only 8GB.

examQuestions.questionText: Which version of Windows Vista does not include offline folder capabilities?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The two biggest modifications to offline folders in Windows Vista are the inclusion of the Sync Center and the restriction of offline file support to the Business, Enterprise, and Ultimate versions.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is an Ethernet standard implemented via a card that allows a “sleeping” machine to awaken when it receives a wakeup signal?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Wake on LAN is an Ethernet standard implemented via a card that allows a “sleeping” machine to awaken when it receives a wakeup signal.

examQuestions.questionText: When Windows 8 was initially released, what was the interface called?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Windows 8 interface was originally called Metro. It is now more commonly referred to as the Windows 8 UI.

examQuestions.questionText: For a 64-bit installation of Windows 8, how much RAM is considered the minimum requirement?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
For 64-bit installations, 2GB RAM and 20GB hard drive space represent the minimum requirements.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the online/cloud storage account (to which you can save or move files) that comes with your Microsoft account?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
OneDrive is the online/cloud storage account that comes with your Microsoft account.

examQuestions.questionText: Previous versions of Windows included Windows Explorer. What is this utility called in Windows 8?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
File Explorer is the new name for Windows Explorer.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is an online site, requiring Windows 8 or higher, where you can download apps, games, software, and so forth?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Windows Store is an online site where you can download apps, games, software, and so on. Windows 8 or higher is required to use the Windows Store.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are controls that are available on the side of the screen and consist of Search, Share, Start, Devices, and Settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Charms are controls that are available on the side of the screen. They consist of Search, Share, Start, Devices, and Settings.

examQuestions.questionText: PowerShell script files are based on which programming framework?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Within PowerShell, you can write script files based on the .NET programming framework.

examQuestions.questionText: Which tool can evaluate your current system and determine if it can be upgraded to Windows 8?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Windows Upgrade Assistant can evaluate your current system and determine if it can be upgraded to Windows 8.

examQuestions.questionText: Which tool from Microsoft simplifies the process of creating a Windows 8 image for upgrading multiple machines and reduces the time each install takes?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Microsoft Deployment Toolkit (commonly called MDT) simplifies the process and reduces the time each install takes.

examQuestions.questionText: If Windows is installed on a system with multiple hard drives, what tool can be used to verify that images are pointing to their intended drives?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If you install Windows on a system with multiple hard drives, you can use diskpart to make sure images are pointing to their intended drives.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following was created to allow Windows 8 to boot from flash drives?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Windows To Go can be used to boot Windows 8 from flash drives.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing Windows 8 on a solid-state drive (SSD). Which of the following can be used to reduce the number of write operations Windows makes and thus optimize Windows for the SSD?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Microsoft recommends that WinSAT.exe be used with the formal option to optimize Windows for the SSD. (This reduces the number of write operations Windows makes.)

examQuestions.questionText: Which partition is the one that contains the hardware-specific files needed to load Windows?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
By definition, a system partition is one that contains the hardware-specific files needed to load Windows.

examQuestions.questionText: Which versions of Windows 8 include Windows To Go? (Choose all that apply.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Only Windows 8 Enterprise includes the Windows To Go feature.

examQuestions.questionText: Which repair option keeps personal files and settings along with the default apps and those that you installed from the Windows Store?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The refresh repair option keeps personal files and settings along with the default apps and those that you installed from the Windows Store.

examQuestions.questionText: How many characters are in a Windows 8 product key?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Windows 8 product key is a 25-character code used for Windows activation.

examQuestions.questionText: In a drive path, what does the system partition usually appear as?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The system partition usually appears as 0, but the system can assign different numbers and different computers with identical hardware configurations that can have different disk numbers assigned to them.

examQuestions.questionText: Windows 7 Ultimate can be upgraded to which versions of Windows 8? (Choose all that apply.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Windows 7 Ultimate can be upgraded to Windows 8 Pro.

examQuestions.questionText: Which versions of Windows 8 support EFS? (Choose all that apply.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2}.
Only the Pro and Enterprise versions support BitLocker and EFS.

examQuestions.questionText: You have enabled Wi-Fi calling on your new mobile device. You are on a cellular call within your Wi-Fi network’s range and you lose the cellular signal. What happens to your call?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When Wi-Fi calling is enabled, calls will seamlessly switch from cellular to Wi-Fi if you are within range of a Wi-Fi network of which you are a member.

answers.textAnswer: It will seamlessly switch over to Wi-Fi.
The phone will beep at you and then switch to Wi-Fi.
The phone will beep at you, and you need to tap Confirm to switch to Wi-Fi.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a valid reason to disable cellular data networking?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Phone calls will always be sent out over the cellular network by default. In situations like that, data transfers may still be using a Wi-Fi connection. Whenever you have a reliable Wi-Fi signal available, which you do not pay for “as you go,” you should feel free to disable your cellular access to data networking. The wireless network is often faster and does not cost you anything to use. If data networking works better when you leave the cellular network available as a fallback, you can choose to disable it only for certain large downloads or disable it completely until the download is complete. Unless you are particularly sensitive to the situation or know that data is going out over your cell access, you might not need to disable the cellular data-networking feature.

answers.textAnswer: You have a limited amount of data in your monthly plan.
You have access to a reliable Wi-Fi signal.
You are about to download an update to your phone.
Your phone calls are going out over your carrier’s cellular network.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a difference between iOS and Android?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
There is no requirement of either operating system that the devices on which they are installed have cellular calling capability.

answers.textAnswer: Android is not a proprietary operating system.
You can download iOS apps from only one place.
You can make a cellular phone call from all Android devices.
It costs more to be a developer of iOS apps.

examQuestions.questionText: Bob’s iPhone 4S cannot detect when he turns his device to the left and right like it’s a steering wheel. Games and other apps that require this motion will not work correctly as a result. Which component has failed in Bob’s phone?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Three gyroscopes are used to detect roll, pitch, and yaw. The problem is with the gyroscope that detects yaw. The accelerometer would be suspect if the iPhone were not detecting flat movement to the side or forward and backward. The magnetometer can only help with compass headings, and the GPS helps with geographical positioning.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a requirement for installing iTunes on a Windows machine?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
iTunes will run on a computer with 512MB of RAM. 1GB is not required unless you want to play 720p high-definition videos.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to create an Android application. Which of the following do you need to download and use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
To develop an app, you need a software development kit (SDK). The app package will have an .apk filename extension when it’s developed.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is more likely to be associated with a resistive touchscreen versus a capacitive one?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Resistive touchscreens require pressure to actuate them, while capacitive ones do not and instead can be actuated by the fleshy part of the human finger. Body oils, moisture, and dirt are not as detrimental to the effectiveness of resistive screens as they are to capacitive screens.

answers.textAnswer: You won’t have to apply as much pressure.
You will need to recalibrate it.
You will have to clean it more often for optimal functionality.
You can use the pad of your finger instead of your fingernail.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are text-messaging services used with mobile devices? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-5}.
SMS is the most widely supported text-messaging service across all platforms and service providers. MMS is another text messaging technology.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of Bluetooth?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The range of Bluetooth connections is considered short compared to Wi-Fi connections. Bluetooth is a fully standardized protocol that supports file transfers using FTP. Rebooting, or even restarting, paired devices is not a requirement for Bluetooth connection.

answers.textAnswer: Bluetooth connections support wireless device control but not file transfers.
Bluetooth is not yet a fully standardized protocol.
Bluetooth connections do not reach as far as Wi-Fi connections.
You must reboot paired devices to complete connection establishment.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the default TCP port number for SMTP?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
SMTP sends mail to the server at TCP port 25. POP3 uses port 110. IMAP4 uses 143, and POP3 uses port 995 securely over SSL or TLS.

examQuestions.questionText: Which mail protocol commonly uses TCP port 587?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
SMTP with TLS uses port 587 by default. With SSL, SMTP uses port 465. IMAP4 with SSL/TLS uses port 993, while POP3 with SSL/TLS uses port 995.

examQuestions.questionText: Which technology built into some mobile phones allows for the user to pass the phone close to a receiver to make an electronic payment, without the phone touching the receiver?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The technology that allows a phone to pass near a receiver to make an electronic payment is near field communication (NFC).

examQuestions.questionText: Which two communications technologies can you use to create a VPN connection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-3}.
You can create virtual private network (VPN) connections on a mobile device using Wi-Fi or cellular network connections.

examQuestions.questionText: Which software component of a mobile phone is responsible for managing all wireless communications?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Each mobile phone has a separate processor that manages wireless communications, also known as radio communications or baseband communications. There is a baseband OS that manages this, and it works with the primary OS on the phone.

examQuestions.questionText: Which two of the following are examples of RTOSs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2}.
The two real-time OSs (RTOSs) that mobile phones have are the baseband OS and the SIM OS.

examQuestions.questionText: Which standard is used to encrypt and decrypt email messages on mobile devices?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
S/MIME is the public key encryption standard used for encrypting and decrypting email.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are universally common items that are synced between a mobile device and a larger computer? (Choose three.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-4},{answer-6}.
The items most often able to be synchronized are contacts, apps, email, photos, music, and videos.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following statements about configuring email access on a mobile device is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Mail access uses standard secure or insecure TCP ports, not UDP ports. Exchange access to such mail services is not unheard of, but it is exceedingly rare. Mobile devices tend to have email clients built in.

answers.textAnswer: Most Internet mail services offer an Exchange option.
The TCP ports used for configuring access are usually standard port numbers.
Most ports used for access are UDP ports.
You must download third-party apps for connecting to email services.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are disabled when airplane mode is switched on? (Choose all that apply.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2},{answer-3},{answer-4}.
Airplane mode disables all radio communications, including cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and NFC. It does not affect the opening of any other apps or the lock screen.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Verizon 4G mobile phone that you want to use as a mobile hotspot. How many connections are you allowed to support simultaneously on that device?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
4G Verizon devices functioning as mobile hotspots can support up to 10 concurrent connections. 3G devices can support only five.

examQuestions.questionText: You’re the administrator for a large bottling company. At the end of each month, you routinely view all logs and look for discrepancies. This month, your email system error log reports a large number of unsuccessful attempts to log on. It’s apparent that the email server is being targeted. Which type of attack is most likely occurring?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A software exploitation attack attempts to exploit weaknesses in software. A common attack attempts to communicate with an established port to gain unauthorized access.

examQuestions.questionText: You’re working late one night, and you notice that the hard drive on your new computer is very active even though you aren’t doing anything on the computer and it isn’t connected to the Internet. What is the most likely suspect?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A symptom of many viruses is unusual activity on the system disk. The virus spreading to other files on your system causes this.

answers.textAnswer: A virus is spreading in your system.
Your system is under a DoS attack.

examQuestions.questionText: How is a worm is different from a virus?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A worm is different from a virus in that it can reproduce itself, it’s self-contained, and it doesn’t need a host application to be transported.

answers.textAnswer: doesn’t need a host application to be transported
it is no longer a threat

examQuestions.questionText: One of the vice presidents of the company calls a meeting with the information technology department after a recent trip to competitors’ sites. She reports that many of the companies she visited granted access to their buildings only after fingerprint scans, and she wants similar technology employed at this company. Of the following, which technology relies on a physical attribute of the user for authentication?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Biometrics relies on a physical characteristic of the user to verify identity. Biometric devices typically use either a hand pattern or a retinal scan to accomplish this.

examQuestions.questionText: Your company provides medical data to doctors from a worldwide database. Because of the sensitive nature of the data you work with, it’s imperative that authentication be established on each session and be valid only for that session. Which of the following authentication methods provides credentials that are valid only during a single session?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Tokens are created when a user or system successfully authenticates. The token is destroyed when the session is over.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the process of masquerading as another user or device?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Spoofing is the process of masquerading as another user or device. It is usually done for the purpose of accessing a resource to which the hacker should not have access or to get through a security device such as a firewall that may be filtering traffic based on source IP address.

examQuestions.questionText: You’re in the process of securing the IT infrastructure by adding fingerprint scanners to your existing authentication methods. This type of security is an example of which of the following?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A fingerprint scanner, or any device that identifies a person by a physical trait, is considered a biometric security control.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of virus alters other programs and databases?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A phage virus alters other programs and databases. The virus infects all of these files.

examQuestions.questionText: Which if the following is a vulnerability discovered in a live environments before a fix or patch exists?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Vulnerabilities are often discovered in live environments before a fix or patch exists. Such vulnerabilities are referred to as zero-day vulnerabilities.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is different from a virus in that it can reproduce itself, it’s self-contained, and it doesn’t need a host application to be transported?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A worm is different from a virus in that it can reproduce itself, it’s self-contained, and it doesn’t need a host application to be transported.

examQuestions.questionText: You’ve discovered that an expired certificate is being used repeatedly to gain logon privileges. Which type of attack is this most likely to be?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A replay attack attempts to replay the results of a previously successful session to gain access.

examQuestions.questionText: Which virus type attaches itself to legitimate programs and then creates a program with a different filename extension?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A companion virus attaches itself to legitimate programs and then creates a program with a different filename extension. This file may reside in your system’s temporary directory. When a user types the name of the legitimate program, the companion virus executes instead of the real program

examQuestions.questionText: As part of your training program, you’re trying to educate users on the importance of security. You explain to them that not every attack depends on implementing advanced technological methods. Some attacks, you explain, take advantage of human shortcomings to gain access that should otherwise be denied. What term do you use to describe attacks of this type?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Social engineering uses the inherent trust in the human species, as opposed to technology, to gain access to your environment.

examQuestions.questionText: Which component of physical security addresses outer-level access control?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The first layer of access control is perimeter security. Perimeter security is intended to delay or deter entrance into a facility.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a very small network in a home-based office, and you want to limit network access to only those hosts that you physically own. What should you utilize to make this possible?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The advantage to assigning the IP addresses statically is that you can make certain which host is associated with which IP address and then utilize filtering to limit network access to only those hosts.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of attack denies authorized users access to network resources?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Although the end result of any of these attacks may be denying authorized users access to network resources, a DoS attack is specifically intended to prevent access to network resources by overwhelming or flooding a service or network.

examQuestions.questionText: As the security administrator for your organization, you must be aware of all types of attacks that can occur and plan for them. Which type of attack uses more than one computer to attack the victim?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack uses multiple computer systems to attack a server or host in the network.

examQuestions.questionText: A server in your network has a program running on it that bypasses authentication. Which type of attack has occurred?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
In a back door attack, a program or service is placed on a server to bypass normal security procedures.

examQuestions.questionText: A junior administrator comes to you in a panic. After looking at the log files, he has become convinced that an attacker is attempting to use a duplicate IP address to replace another system in the network to gain access. Which type of attack is this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
TCP/IP hijacking is an attempt to steal a valid IP address and use it to gain authorization or information from a network.

examQuestions.questionText: A smurf attack attempts to use a broadcast ping on a network; the return address of the ping may be that of a valid system in your network. Which protocol does a smurf attack use to conduct the attack?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A smurf attack attempts to use a broadcast ping (ICMP) on a network. The return address of the ping may be that of a valid system in your network. This system will be flooded with responses in a large network.

examQuestions.questionText: Your system log files report an ongoing attempt to gain access to a single account. This attempt has been unsuccessful to this point. What type of attack are you most likely experiencing?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A password-guessing attack occurs when a user account is repeatedly attacked using a variety of passwords.

examQuestions.questionText: Your help desk has informed you that they received an urgent call from the vice president last night requesting his logon ID and password. When talking with the VP today, he says he never made that call. What type of attack is this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Someone trying to con your organization into revealing account and password information is launching a social engineering attack.

examQuestions.questionText: Upper management has decreed that a firewall must be put in place immediately, before your site suffers an attack similar to one that struck a sister company. Responding to this order, your boss instructs you to implement a packet filter by the end of the week. A packet filter performs which function?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Packet filters prevent unauthorized packets from entering or leaving a network. Packet filters are a type of firewall that block specified traffic based on IP address, protocol, and many other attributes.

answers.textAnswer: Prevents unauthorized packets from entering the network
Allows all packets to leave the network
Allows all packets to enter the network

examQuestions.questionText: Which media is susceptible to viruses?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
All of these devices can store and pass viruses to uninfected systems. Make sure that all files are scanned for viruses before they’re copied to these media.

examQuestions.questionText: Your network has 20 Windows 8.1 workstations. When it comes to managing patches and updates, which of the following is the best practice?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Patches and updates should be applied, regardless of the severity of the issue. In addition, they should be applied immediately. Use Windows Update to manage the process for you.

answers.textAnswer: Apply patches and updates only after they have received good reviews on the Internet.
Apply patches and updates once per month.
Apply patches and updates immediately after they become available.
Apply patches and updates only if they fix a critical security flaw.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8.1 workstation and want to prevent a potential hacker from booting to a CD from the optical drive. What should you do to help prevent this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A strong Windows password will help protect Windows but does not protect the computer in general. If a user can get into the BIOS, then he can change the boot sequence, boot to a CD, and do some damage to the system. The way to protect against this is to implement a BIOS/UEFI password.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of security solution generally functions as a packet filter and can perform stateful inspection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Firewalls are among the first lines of defense in a network. The basic purpose of a firewall is to isolate one network from another. Firewalls function as one or more of the following: packet filter, proxy firewall, or stateful inspection firewall.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are examples of physical security methods? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
Biometrics and privacy filters are physical security methods. Multifactor authentication may require a physical device (for example, something you have) but not necessarily. Firewalls can be hardware devices but can also be software packages.

examQuestions.questionText: A user on your network reported that he got a telephone call from Diane in the IT department saying that he needed to reset his password. She offered to do it for him if he could provide her with his current one. What is this most likely an example of?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Social engineering is a process in which an attacker attempts to acquire information about your network and system by social means, such as talking to people in the organization. A social engineering attack may occur over the phone, over email, or in person. The intent is to acquire access information, such as user IDs and passwords.

answers.textAnswer: The IT department needs to reset the user’s password.

examQuestions.questionText: Your corporate IT department has decided that to enhance security, they want to configure all mobile devices to require both a passcode and fingerprint scan to unlock a mobile device for use. What is this an example of?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Any time there is more than one authentication method required, it’s multifactor authentication. In this case, it does involve using biometrics, but the passcode is not a biometric factor. Multifactor authentication usually requires two of the following three types of inputs: something you know (password), something you have (smart token), or something you are (biometrics).

examQuestions.questionText: Several employees at your company have been tailgating to gain access to secure areas. Which of the following security methods is the best choice for stopping this practice?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Tailgating refers to being so close to someone when they enter a building that you are able to come in right behind them without needing to use a key, a card, or any other security device. Using mantraps, which are devices such as small rooms that limit access to one or a few individuals, is a great way to stop tailgating.

examQuestions.questionText: Robert has joined your company as a network administrator. His user account name is RobertS. What is the recommended way to give Robert the administrative privileges he needs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Adding RobertS to the Administrators group will certainly work, but it’s not the recommended approach. Since members of the Administrators group have such power, they can inadvertently do harm (such as accidentally deleting a file that a regular user could not). To protect against this, the practice of logging in with an Administrators group account for daily interaction is strongly discouraged. Instead, system administrators should log in with a user account (lesser privileges) and change to the Administrators group account (elevated privileges) only when necessary.

answers.textAnswer: Add the RobertS user account to the Administrators group.

Create an account called AdminRobertS. Add that account to the Administrators group. Have Robert use the RobertS account unless he needs administrative rights, in which case he should use the other account.
Copy the Administrator account and rename it to RobertS.
Add the RobertS user account to the Power Users group.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 7 workstation with one volume, [code]C:[code], that is formatted with FAT32. What is the easiest way to enable this volume to have file- and folder-level security permissions?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you’re using FAT32 and want to change to NTFS, the convert utility will allow you to do so. For example, to change the E: drive to NTFS, the command is convert e: /FS:NTFS.

answers.textAnswer: Reformat the volume with NTFS and restore all of the data from backup.
Enable file and folder permissions in System Properties.
At a command prompt, type [code]reformat c: /fs:ntfs[code].
At a command prompt, type [code]convert c: /fs:ntfs[code].

examQuestions.questionText: Luana is a member of the Dev group and the HR group. She is trying to access a local resource on an NTFS volume. The HR group has Allow Full Control permission for the payroll folder, and the Dev group has Deny Read permission for the same folder. What is Luana’s effective access to the payroll folder?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
When there are conflicting NTFS permissions, generally they are combined, and the most liberal is granted. The exception to that is when there is an explicit Deny. That overrides any allowed permissions.

examQuestions.questionText: Which default Windows group was designed to have more power than normal users but not as much power as administrators?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Microsoft wanted to create a group in Windows that was not as powerful as the Administrators group, which is how the Power Users group came into being. The idea was that membership in this group would be given read/write permission to the system, allowing members to install most software but keeping them from changing key operating system files.

examQuestions.questionText: You have just transformed a Windows workgroup into a small domain and are configuring user accounts. Which of the following is considered a best practice for managing user account security?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
When assigning user permissions, follow the principle of least privilege; give users only the bare minimum that they need to do their job. Assign permissions to groups rather than users, and make users member of groups (or remove them from groups) as they change roles or positions.

answers.textAnswer: Require every user to log on as a Guest user.
Allow all users Read and Write access to all server files.
Follow the principle of least privilege.
Place all user accounts in the Power Users group.

examQuestions.questionText: Someone has placed an unauthorized wireless router on your network and configured it with the same SSID as your network. Users can access the network through that router, even though it’s not supposed to be there. What type of security threat could this lead to?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Placing an unauthorized router with a seemingly legitimate configuration is specifically known as an evil twin. Those can lead to man-in-the-middle attacks,which involve clandestinely placing something (such as a piece of software or a rogue router) between a server and the user, and neither the server’s administrator nor the user is aware of it. The man-in-the-middle intercepts data and then sends the information to the server as if nothing is wrong.
