examQuestions.questionText: Several workstations in your office are running Windows XP Professional. You want to upgrade them to Windows Vista. To which versions of Vista can you upgrade Windows XP Professional? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
Windows XP Professional can be upgraded only to Windows Vista Business or Windows Vista Ultimate. Windows Vista Enterprise is typically installed as a clean install. It can be installed only as an “upgrade” to Windows Vista Business.

examQuestions.questionText: You have just installed a Windows Vista workstation for a user. Company policy is that the user’s TEMP folder should not be located on the system partition. Which administrative tool can you use to change the location of the user’s temporary files folder?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The user’s TEMP directory is a user environment variable and is accessed through Users and Groups (or User Accounts).

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing Windows Vista on an empty mechanical hard drive. When formatting the drive, you want to choose a file system that is lightweight. The user is not concerned about data security. Which file system best meets the user’s needs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
FAT32 is lightweight and relatively fast. It allows for 32-bit cluster addressing, which provides for a maximum partition size of 2 terabytes (2,048GB). It also includes smaller cluster sizes to avoid wasted space. FAT32 support is included in current Windows versions. FAT32 does not have individual file security permissions.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Windows Vista utility provides a single interface for configuring your firewall, getting automatic updates, and setting up malware protection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In Vista, Windows Security Center provides a single interface for firewall settings, automatic updating, malware protection, and other security settings. In Windows 7, other options were added, and it was renamed to Action Center.

examQuestions.questionText: One of the developers in your organization has created a new software package for Windows 8.1 client computers. He wants to custom configure application-specific access permissions. Which administrative tool would he use to do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Component Services is an MMC snap-in in Windows 7 that allows you to administer, as well as deploy, component services and configure behavior such as application-specific security. If you hear the terms DCOM or COM+ mentioned in conjunction with Windows, Component Services is the tool needed for their management.

examQuestions.questionText: Several workstations in your office are running Windows Vista Business. You want to upgrade them to Windows 8.1 Pro. Which of the following statements is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
There is no direct upgrade path from Windows XP or Vista to Windows 8/8.1. You must do a clean installation. You can upgrade from Windows Vista to Windows 7 and then upgrade Windows 7 to Windows 8/8.1.

answers.textAnswer: There is no direct upgrade path from Vista to Windows 8.1. You must perform a clean install.
You can upgrade Windows Vista Business only to Windows 8.1 Enterprise.
You can upgrade Windows Vista Business only to Windows 8.1 Basic.
When you begin the upgrade, choose Custom and then do not format the hard drive.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to format a hard drive with the NFTS file system. It’s the D: drive on a Windows Vista computer. Which command do you use at the command prompt to do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The format command is used to format hard drives. Before you format any drive, be sure that you have it backed up or are prepared to lose whatever is on it. The /fs:[filesystem] switch specifies the file system.

examQuestions.questionText: You are trying to update a Windows Vista workstation. After you make changes to the configuration, the system does not boot properly. Another technician suggests reverting the OS to the previous configuration settings. Which tool can you use to do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
To revert to a previous configuration, you need to apply a restore point. Restore points are created and managed in the System Restore utility. A restore point is a copy of your system configuration at a given point in time. Restore points are useful for when Windows fails to boot but the computer appears to be fine otherwise or when Windows doesn’t seem to be acting right and you think it was because of a recent configuration change.

examQuestions.questionText: A user reports that it seems like her network performance has recently become very slow. While investigating her network card properties, you notice that her network card is set to half duplex. What does this mean?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Duplexing is the means by which communication takes place. With full duplexing, the network card can send and receive at the same time. The main advantage of full-duplex over half-duplex communication is performance. NICs can operate twice as fast in full-duplex mode as they do normally in half-duplex mode.

answers.textAnswer: That is the normal operating setting for a network card.
The switch that she is connected to configured her network card to operate in this mode for backward compatibility.
The card needs to be set to simplex mode for it to run faster.
The card needs to be set to full duplex mode for it to run faster.

examQuestions.questionText: You have recently deployed a custom application to several Windows workstations on your network. The application appears to have a bug, and the developer suggests you edit the Registry to fix it. Which administrative tool would you use to do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Windows configuration information is stored in a special configuration database known as the Registry. This centralized database also contains environmental settings for various Windows programs. To edit the Registry, use the REGEDIT tool. Be careful, though, because an incorrect Registry change can render a system inoperable.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Windows 7 utility allows you to view error messages generated by applications or login failures?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Event Viewer is the Windows tool that allows you to view application error logs, security audit records, and system errors. It’s available in most versions of Windows.

examQuestions.questionText: A user with a Windows 8.1 workstation recently received a second hard drive. Another administrator created a partition on the hard drive, and it’s ready for use. He will store the raw video files he creates on that drive and insists that it be called the R: drive. Which of the following statements is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
In Windows Vista and newer, you can reassign or change a drive letter by using the Disk Management utility.

answers.textAnswer: You can use Disk Management to change the drive letter to R:.
You can use Disk Management to change the drive letter to R:, but only if it’s a dynamic disk.
You can use Disk Management to change the drive letter to R:, but only if it’s in an extended partition.
You will need to use Disk Management to delete the partition and re-create it as R:.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8 workstation with corrupt files in the operating system. It will not boot properly. You need to boot the computer using its network card to connect to an image server to restore Windows. What is this boot process called?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Booting from a network card is referred to as a PXE (Pixie) boot. Netboot is the process of booting the entire OS from a network server, such as from a thin client.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to format a blank SDXC card and transfer files to it. Which file system is ideally suited for this type of media?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Microsoft created ExFAT, and it is a proprietary file system of choice for flash drives where NTFS cannot be used (because of overhead) and FAT32 is not acceptable (because of file system limitations). It is ideal for SD cards that hold a lot of information, and it is supported in all current versions of Windows.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8.1 workstation. You want to connect to a printer located on a Windows 7 workstation. What do you need to do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
To connect to a printer over the network, you map a network printer. If the printer is on your local computer and you want others to use it, you need to share the printer. You do this by right-clicking the printer, choosing Printer Properties, and then going to the Sharing tab. Check the box to share the printer.

answers.textAnswer: Right-click the printer, choose Printer Properties, and share the printer.
Right-click the printer, choose Printer Properties, and map the network printer.
Open the Add a Printer Wizard and share the printer.
Open the Add a Printer Wizard and map the network printer.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing Windows Vista on a computer. When you partition the hard drive, which type of partition is limited to having only one logical drive on it?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows supports both basic and dynamic storage. Basic storage can have a primary and an extended partition, while dynamic storage can be simple, spanned, or striped. In basic storage, Windows drives can be partitioned with primary or extended partitions. The difference is that extended partitions can be divided into one or more logical drives and primary partitions cannot be further subdivided.

examQuestions.questionText: A laptop user has traveled to visit a client and forgot his power adapter. Before going to lunch with the client, he wants to conserve battery power, but he wants to enable the fastest possible startup when he gets back, with his applications already open. Which power mode will conserve battery life but enable the fastest startup?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
While in sleep mode, the computer uses very little power. When you turn it back on, all the applications you left open will still be open. Sleep uses a little more power than hibernate but also boots up faster. Shutting down will save the most battery life but will also take the longest to reboot. There is no resting power mode in Windows, but some configurations will offer a standby power mode.

examQuestions.questionText: You have just installed a second hard drive into a Windows 7 workstation. The drive is properly recognized by the BIOS when the system boots, but you are unable to see it in Windows Explorer. What do you need to do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
New hard drives appear as not initialized in Windows. To use the disk, go into Disk Management and initialize the disk. Then you can create partitions, assign drive letters, and perform other disk management tasks.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Windows user interface was the first one to have translucent windows and provides the ability to create a three-dimensional stack of open windows for users to cycle through?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
An acronym for Authentic, Energetic, Reflective, and Open, Aero differs from previous GUIs in that its windows are translucent and it provides the ability to create a 3D stack of open windows and cycle through them (known as Flip 3D).

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 7 workstation with four hard disks. You want to take advantage of having multiple disks by creating a disk array. What types of arrays can you create in Windows that will combine the disks into one volume? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
There are three types of volumes you can create in Disk Management: simple, spanned, striped, and mirrored. Simple volumes are on one disk. Spanned, striped, and mirrored will be made up of multiple physical disks.

examQuestions.questionText: Which versions of Windows 7 support BitLocker? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
BitLocker is available only for Windows 7 in the Enterprise and Ultimate editions.

examQuestions.questionText: You are working on a Windows 8.1 workstation that you believe has cross-linked files. At a command prompt, you want to check for these files and automatically fix any problems. Which command should you run to do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
You can use the Windows chkdsk command to create and display status reports for the hard disk. chkdsk can also correct file system problems (such as cross-linked files) and scan for and attempt to repair disk errors. The correct switch to automatically fix any issues is /f.

examQuestions.questionText: You are configuring a secondary hard drive using Disk Management in Windows Vista. When setting up basic storage, which two types of partitions can you create? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
Windows supports both basic and dynamic storage. Basic storage can have a primary partition and an extended partition, while dynamic storage can be simple, spanned, or striped.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing Windows 8.1 on a new workstation. Before you format the drive with NTFS, your manager tells you to perform a full format. Which of the following statements best describes what a full format does?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
When formatting a hard drive, you can usually choose between a quick format or a full format. With a quick format, a new file table is created on the hard disk, but files are not fully overwritten or erased from the disk. A full format removes old files, creates a new file allocation table, and scans the hard drive for bad sectors. The scan is what takes so long.

answers.textAnswer: Remove files from the partition, create a new file allocation table, and scan the hard disk for bad sectors.
Remove files from the partition and create a new file allocation table.
Create a new file allocation table and scan the hard disk for bad sectors.
Delete the partition, re-create the partition, create a new file allocation table, and scan the hard disk for bad sectors.

examQuestions.questionText: You are at a Windows 8.1 command prompt. Which command should you use to create and manage partitions?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The diskpart utility shows the partitions and lets you manage them on the computer’s hard drives. Because of the enormous power it holds, membership in the Administrators local group (or equivalent) is required to run diskpart. diskpart replaced the older fdisk.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to install Windows 8.1 on 30 identical workstations. You do not want to manually input information into each of the workstations. What type of installation should you perform?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
An unattended installation, as the name implies, is one in which you don’t need to be sitting in front of the machine to complete the operation. The heart of an unattended installation is utilizing image deployment, which is sort of like copying an ideal image over from one machine to another.

examQuestions.questionText: You are working at a Windows Vista command prompt. Which command should you use to copy directories and subdirectories but not empty directories?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The xcopy command is a more powerful version of copy. It lets you copy directories and also will copy file ownership and NTFS permissions. The /s switch is used to copy directories and subdirectories, except for empty ones. To copy those as well, use /e. The /h switch copies hidden and system files, and the /a switch copies only files with the Archive attribute set.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to configure Internet connections on a Windows 7 workstation. In which tabs of Internet options do you set the home page and enable the pop-up blocker?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Internet options Windows Control Panel utility allows you to configure Internet connections. It has six tabs: general, security, privacy, connections, programs, and advanced. (Some versions of Windows also have a content tab.) The home page is set from the general tab, and the pop-up blocker is enabled on the privacy tab. Proxy settings are configured here as well, in the connections tab.

examQuestions.questionText: You have recently made some configuration changes to a Windows 8.1 workstation, and now it’s behaving erratically. You reboot the computer and enter the Windows Recovery Environment. What should you do to roll back those recent changes?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
When a problem pops up with the Windows 8 operating system, you can boot into the Windows Recovery Environment (Windows RE) and repair it by choosing to refresh, reset, or restore it. Refreshing it keeps personal files and settings along with the default apps and those that you installed from the Windows Store. Resetting reinstalls Windows and deletes all but the default apps (meaning that you lose your personal files and settings). Restoring allows you to just undo recent system changes.

examQuestions.questionText: You are creating a network for a small office with Windows 7 and Windows 8/8.1 workstations. They do not want centralized security, but they want it to be easy to share printers and files, including libraries. What type of network setup should you recommend?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The purpose behind a HomeGroup is to simplify home or small office networking and, more specifically, the sharing of files and printers. Windows 7 Starter can only join a HomeGroup, while all other editions of Windows 7 can both join and create a HomeGroup. The location from which you network must be set to Home. Shared files can include libraries, which is a big feature of Windows 7. All computers participating in the HomeGroup must be running Windows 7 or Windows 8/8.1 (but not Vista), and the network cannot extend outside the small group.

examQuestions.questionText: For which operating system can you get a preconfigured virtual machine (that runs in the Windows Virtual PC emulator) that allows users to run Windows XP–based applications?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The ability to run applications in Windows XP Mode (XPM) is included with Windows 7 Professional, Enterprise, and Ultimate. This is a virtual client (emulating Windows XP Professional with Service Pack 3), and you must download and install Windows Virtual PC to use it. XPM was discontinued in Windows 8/8.1.

chapters.name: Working with Mac OS and Linux

examQuestions.questionText: If the permissions for a file are rwxrw-r--, what permissions apply for a user who is a member of the group to which the owner belongs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The middle set of three permissions applies to the group. In this case, the value is rw-, which means read and write permission only (not execute).

examQuestions.questionText: You are currently in a Linux terminal session and in directory /home/edulaney/documents/mail. Which command will take you to /home/edulaney/documents?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
To change to the parent directory of the one you are in, use two periods (..) with the cd command.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following Linux commands/utilities can be used to edit a wireless connection’s configuration settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
There is a utility called ifconfig that is used to see and edit network configuration files. It has a counterpart, iwconfig, that works with wireless connection configuration files.

examQuestions.questionText: Within a Linux terminal, you want to see all of the files on your system in long format (using the –l option), including any hidden files (which requires the –a option). Which command should you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The command ls –la will show all files (including hidden ones) in long-listing format.

examQuestions.questionText: As part of your training program, you’re trying to convince users to make backups on a regular basis. Which Apple app can be used to make backups of various types on a regular basis?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Time Machine is an application from Apple that can be used to make backups.

examQuestions.questionText: Within a Linux terminal, you want to see all of the files on your system in long format (using the &#8211;l option), including any hidden files (which requires the &#8211;a option). Which command should you use?
examQuestions.explanation: The command ls&#160;&#8211;la will show all files (including hidden ones) in long-listing format.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following allows you to install Windows on a Mac machine and choose between operating systems upon bootup?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Boot Camp can be used to install a 64-bit version of Windows on an Intel-based Mac and then let you choose which operating system to use upon bootup.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a Mac OS X feature for password management?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Keychain app is used for password management.

examQuestions.questionText: The interpreter in Linux between the operating system and the user is known as the ___________________ .
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The shell serves as the interpreter between the OS and the user. A number of different shells are available.

examQuestions.questionText: What type of backups are kept on site at the computer center for immediate recovery purposes?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Working copies are backups kept on site at the computer center for immediate recovery purposes.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following can be used in Linux to download patches for installation on a workstation?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The apt-get utility command can be used in Linux to download files, including patches.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following commands can be used to change the owner of a file to a new owner in Linux?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The chown utility is used to change the owner from one person to another.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Linux utility can be used to check and repair disks?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The fsck utility can be used to check and repair disks in Linux.

examQuestions.questionText: Your iPad has an application that will not stop running. What feature/tool can you use to stop it?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Force Quit exists for the purpose of stopping those runaway applications when they pop up.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the most common shell used with Linux?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Bash shell (borne again shell) is the most popular one included with Linux distributions.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the name of the area at the bottom of a Mac OS X screen where, by default, a bar of crucial icons appears?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The area at the bottom of the screen is known as the Dock.

examQuestions.questionText: What key combination can you use to bring up Spotlight from within an app?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Command+space sequence is used to access Spotlight from within an app.

examQuestions.questionText: Which Linux command can be used to let you run a single command as another user?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The sudo command is used to run a command as another user, and the default user is root.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following Linux commands will show you a list of running processes?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The ps command will show running processes on your system.

examQuestions.questionText: What does the &#8211;p option with mkdir do?
examQuestions.explanation: This option is used to create the folders as well as subfolders, making the parent so to speak.

answers.textAnswer: Prompts the user before creating files
Prompts the user before creating subfolders
Creates subfolders as well as folders

examQuestions.questionText: You have been told to use the /FIXBOOT switch to write a new boot sector on a Windows 7 machine. Which command does this switch work with?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The BOOTREC /FIXBOOT command can be used to write a new boot sector.

examQuestions.questionText: You believe that your system files are corrupted in Windows. You run System File Checker. What do you do to make System File Checker automatically repair your system files if repair is needed?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.

The SFC command will run System File Checker. The /SCANNOW option will scan files, and SFC automatically repairs files that it detects as corrupted.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following utilities is used to update Group Policy settings and replaces some of the functionality that previously existed with SECEDIT?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The GPUPDATE utility is used to update Group Policy settings and replaces some of the functionality that previously existed with SECEDIT.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following Registry hives contains information about the computer’s hardware?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
There are five basic hives in the Windows Registry: HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, HKEY_USERS, and HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG. HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE stores information about the computer’s hardware. HKEY_CURRENT_MACHINE, HKEY_MACHINE, and HKEY_RESOURCES do not exist.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following switches can be used with ROBOCOPY to mirror a complete directory tree?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The /MIR switch can be used with ROBOCOPY to mirror a complete directory tree.

examQuestions.questionText: In Windows, which of the following is the file system of choice for CD media?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
In Windows, CDFS is the file system of choice for CD media.

examQuestions.questionText: Which utility can be used to schedule a remote shutdown?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The SHUTDOWN.EXE utility can be used to schedule a shutdown (complete or a restart) locally or remotely.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following file systems is a proprietary one created by Microsoft for use with large flash drives?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
ExFAT is a proprietary file system created by Microsoft for use with large flash drives.

examQuestions.questionText: Which command lists all running processes at the command line?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The TASKLIST utility will list all running processes at the command line.

examQuestions.questionText: Virtual memory is configured through which system tool?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Virtual memory settings are accessed through the Performance tab or area of the System applet in the Control Panel.

examQuestions.questionText: Within the Services snap-in, services can be in any state except which of the following?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Services can be started automatically or manually or be disabled.

examQuestions.questionText: What can you do if a program is not responding to any commands and appears to be locked up?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
You can use Task Manager to deal with applications that have stopped responding.

answers.textAnswer: Open the System Control Panel applet, and choose Performance to see what process is causing the problem.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Del to reboot the computer.
Open Task Manager, select the appropriate task, and click End Task.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following can be used to configure a remote connection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
MSTSC can be used to configure a remote connection.

examQuestions.questionText: Which type of resource do you configure in Device Manager?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Device Manager is used in Windows to configure all hardware resources about which Windows is aware.

examQuestions.questionText: To back up the files on your disks in Windows 7, which Windows program can you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Backup utility provided with Windows 7 and Windows Vista versions of Windows has different levels of functionality. In Windows 8, this could be done with File History.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following partitions is specifically the partition from which the operating system boots?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The operating system boots from the active partition. Active partitions must be primary partitions, but a primary partition does not have to be active. (There can be up to four primary partitions per hard drive.)

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is replacing the MBR in 64-bit versions of the Windows operating system?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
GPT is replacing the MBR in 64-bit versions of the Windows operating system.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following utilities will rearrange the files on your hard disk to occupy contiguous chunks of space?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows Disk Defragmenter rearranges files on your hard disk so that they occupy contiguous spaces (as much as possible).

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following tools allows you to test DirectX functionality?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The DxDiag utility (DirectX Diagnostics) is used to test DirectX functionality. Telnet is used to establish a remote connection, Msinfo32 shows configuration settings and Ping can let you know if a remote host can be reached.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the name of the file that runs if there are any gadgets placed on the Windows 7 Desktop?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Even though Windows 7 does not have Sidebar (a feature that lived and died with Windows Vista), the file that runs for gadgets is SIDEBAR.EXE.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is used by BitLocker to be able to encrypt a drive?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
BitLocker uses (if it is present) the Trusted Platform Module (TPM).

examQuestions.questionText: Which feature of Windows 7 allows files and folders to be grouped logically and appear as if they are in the same location even when they are not?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Libraries allow files and folders to be grouped logically and appear as if they are in the same location even when they are not.

examQuestions.questionText: As an administrator, you need to get an inventory of computers on your network and plan a rollout of Windows 7. Which tool can be used for this purpose?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Microsoft Assessment and Planning (MAP) Toolkit can be used to get an inventory of computers on your network and plan a rollout of the new operating system.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following editions of Windows Vista can be upgraded to Windows 7 Professional?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Only Windows Vista Business can be upgraded to Windows 7 Professional.

examQuestions.questionText: You need to do an installation of Windows 7 in a PXE environment. Which of the following can be used?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Windows Preinstallation Environment (WinPE), is a stub operating system that creates a Pre-boot Execution Environment (PXE).

examQuestions.questionText: Which editions of Windows 7 include BitLocker? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4},{answer-5}.
Only Windows 7 Enterprise and Windows 7 Ultimate support BitLocker drive encryption

examQuestions.questionText: Where in Windows 7 can you manually create a restore point?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In Windows 7 (and Windows Vista), the ability to do this has been moved to the System Protection tab of System Properties.

answers.textAnswer: System Restore option beneath System Tools
System Protection tab of System Properties
Windows 7 does not allow for the manual creation of restore points

examQuestions.questionText: In Windows 7, what is the default setting for the UAC?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The UAC default in Windows 7 is “Notify me only when programs try to make changes to my computer.”

answers.textAnswer: Notify me only when programs try to make changes to my computer
Notify me only when programs try to make changes to my computer (do not dim my desktop)

examQuestions.questionText: Which feature allows you to use free space on an SD card to speed up a system?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The ReadyBoost feature allows you to use free space on a removable drive (such as an SD card) to speed up a system.

examQuestions.questionText: Remote computers and virtual machines are made available with Windows 7 using which port?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
When remote computers and virtual machine utilities are used in Windows 7 networking, port 3389 is the default port used.

examQuestions.questionText: Which directory on a standard Windows 7 installation holds the boot file configuration?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
On a standard, default installation, the \BOOT directory holds the boot file configuration for Windows 7.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum amount of RAM supported in the 64-bit Enterprise edition of Windows 7?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Professional, Enterprise, and Ultimate editions support 192GB. The maximum amount of RAM supported by Home Premium is 16GB. The Starter edition supports only 2GB.

examQuestions.questionText: Which editions of Windows 7 can create a HomeGroup? (Choose four.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-3},{answer-4},{answer-5}.
While all editions of Windows 7 can join a HomeGroup, only Home Premium, Professional, Enterprise, and Ultimate can create one.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the maximum number of physical CPUs supported by Windows 7 Enterprise edition?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The maximum number of physical CPUs supported by Windows 7 Enterprise edition is two.

examQuestions.questionText: After installing the operating system, what does Windows 7 require in order to curb software piracy?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Windows 7 requires the installation to be followed by a process known as product activation to curb software piracy.

examQuestions.questionText: If a program doesn’t have a shortcut on the Desktop or in the Programs submenu, you can start it by ________________. (Choose the best answer.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
To run any program, select Start > Run and type the name of the program in the Open field. If you don’t know the exact name of the program, you can find the file by clicking the Browse button. Once you have typed in the executable name, click OK to run the program.

answers.textAnswer: Typing CMD in the Start Run box
Using the RUN command and typing in the name of the program
Typing CMD in the Start box followed by the program name

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following can you type at a Start menu in Windows to open a command prompt? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-3}.
To open a command prompt, you can use CMD or COMMAND.

examQuestions.questionText: Which part of the operating system can be described as extremely specific software written for the purpose of instructing the OS on how to access a piece of hardware?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
A driver is extremely specific software written for the purpose of instructing a particular OS on how to access a piece of hardware.

examQuestions.questionText: The Taskbar can be increased in size by ________________.
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
You can increase the Taskbar’s size by moving the mouse pointer to the top of it, pausing until the pointer turns into a double-headed arrow, and then clicking and dragging. Keep in mind that in Windows XP, you have to unlock the Taskbar first by right-clicking on it and deselecting Lock The Taskbar.

answers.textAnswer: Right-clicking the mouse and dragging the Taskbar to make it bigger
Left-clicking the mouse and double-clicking the Taskbar
Moving the mouse pointer to the top of the Taskbar, pausing until the pointer turns into a double-headed arrow, and then clicking and dragging
Highlighting the Taskbar and double-clicking in the center

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following file attributes are available to files on a FAT32 partition?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
FAT32 does not have as many options as NTFS, such as Encryption and Compression, which are attributes are available only on NTFS partitions.

answers.textAnswer: Compression, Hidden, Archive, Encryption, Read Only
Indexing, Read Only, Hidden, System, Compression

examQuestions.questionText: The Windows File Explorer program can be used to do which of the following? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2},{answer-3}.
The Windows File Explorer program can be used to copy and move files and to change file attributes.

examQuestions.questionText: Standard permissions are ________________.
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Standard permissions, unlike special permissions, have been grouped together to make it easier for administrators to assign permissions.

answers.textAnswer: Only the Read, Write, and Execute permissions
Permissions assigned to users but not to groups
Permissions grouped together for easy assignment

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is a program that runs on top of the OS and allows the user to issue commands through a set of menus or some other graphical interface?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The shell is a program that runs on top of the OS and allows the user to issue commands through a set of menus or some other graphical interface.

examQuestions.questionText: What operating system feature offers the ability for a single application to have multiple requests into the processor at one time?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Multithreading offers the ability for a single application to have multiple requests in to the processor at one time.

examQuestions.questionText: In Windows, a deleted file can be retrieved using which of the following?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
All deleted files are placed in the Recycle Bin. Deleted files are held there until the Recycle Bin is emptied. Users can easily recover accidentally deleted files from the Recycle Bin.

examQuestions.questionText: To turn off a Windows 7 machine, you should ________________.
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
To turn off a Windows 7 machine, select Start > Shut Down, and choose Shut Down. This will turn off the computer.

answers.textAnswer: Run the Shut Down (Turn Off) command at a command prompt.
Turn off the switch and unplug the machine
Select Start > Shut Down, and choose Shut Down.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the minimum amount of free hard drive space recommended for the installation of Windows Vista Home Basic?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The minimum amount of free hard drive space recommended for the installation of Windows Vista Home Basic is 15GB.

examQuestions.questionText: In Windows, a quick way to access Help is to press which keyboard key?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
In Windows, a quick way to access Help is to press the F1 key.

answers.textAnswer: The Windows button on the keyboard

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following was installed to the Desktop by default only in Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Sidebar existed only in Windows Vista and provided a quick interface that allowed you to access common utilities such as the headlines.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is located on the rightmost portion of the Taskbar?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The system tray is located on the right side of the Taskbar.

examQuestions.questionText: In addition to right-clicking on the Desktop, how else can you access the Display Properties settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
In addition to right-clicking on the Desktop, you can access the Display Properties settings by using the Display icon under Control Panel (as long as you are not using Category view in some versions).

answers.textAnswer: Using the Display icon under Control Panel
Using the System icon under Control Panel

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the name of the graphical interface included with Windows Vista?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The interface included with Windows Vista is called Aero.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the minimum recommended memory for a 64-bit installation of Windows 7?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The minimum recommended memory for a 64-bit installation of Windows 7 is 2GB.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the minimum recommended memory for a 32-bit installation of Windows 7?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The minimum recommended memory for a 32-bit installation of Windows 7 is 1GB.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following operating systems use the BOOT.INI file during boot?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Only Windows XP uses the BOOT.INI file. Newer versions of Windows use the Boot Configuration Data (BCD) file.

examQuestions.questionText: Which BOOTREC option can be used in Windows to rebuild the boot configuration file?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Windows uses the Windows Boot Configuration Data (BCD) file instead of the BOOT.INI file. This can be rebuilt with the /REBUILDBCD option.

examQuestions.questionText: In Windows, which utility is responsible for finding, downloading, and installing Windows service packs?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Windows Update automatically (by default) finds, downloads, and installs service packs and other Windows updates. None of the other options are real utilities.

examQuestions.questionText: Which boot mode loads only basic drivers?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Safe Mode loads only basic drivers, such as a standard VGA video driver and the keyboard and mouse.

examQuestions.questionText: What is the first step in the troubleshooting process?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The first step is to identify the problem. Once you have done that, you should (in order) establish a theory of probable cause, test the theory, establish a plan of action to resolve the problem, verify full system functionality, and document your findings.

examQuestions.questionText: Which tool do you use to create a restore point in Windows?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The System Restore tool is used to create restore points. Backup creates backups of your hard drive. You can use Backup to create copies of your configuration (like a restore point) along with other data, but to create a restore point specifically, use System Restore. There are no Restore Point or Emergency Repair tools.

examQuestions.questionText: One of the users you support has a Windows 7 laptop that continues to shut down and restart spontaneously. What should you try first?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Check the sleep settings for hibernation, and disable those first to see if that makes a difference. If it does not, then you can begin disabling drivers and making other changes.

answers.textAnswer: Begin disabling drivers one by one until you find the culprit.
Disable the sleep settings for hibernation.

examQuestions.questionText: Windows 7 includes a feature called a _________, which is a copy of your system configuration that can be used to roll back the system to a previous state if a configuration error occurs.
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows can use restore points to roll back the system configuration to a previous state. None of the other options exist.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are used to prevent pop-unders from appearing?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Pop-up blockers are used to prevent both pop-ups and pop-unders from appearing. While older browsers did not incorporate an option to block pop-ups, most new browsers, including the latest versions of Internet Explorer, now have that capability built in.

examQuestions.questionText: In general, how often should you update your antivirus definitions?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
It’s critical to keep your antivirus software up-to-date, so you should update your definitions at least once per week.

answers.textAnswer: Antivirus definitions do not need to be updated.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to ensure that your computer receives automatic updates to Windows and other Microsoft products. Which tool will take care of this for you?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows Update downloads patches for the Windows operating system and other Microsoft products.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following programs could be considered anti-malware?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows Defender is an anti-malware program. It checks for harmful, or unwanted, software installed on the machine.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following allows you to register and unregister modules and controls for troubleshooting purposes?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The REGSVR32 tool (REGSVR32.EXE) allows you to register and unregister modules and controls for troubleshooting purposes.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following can you do to help eliminate security problems? (Select all that apply.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1},{answer-2},{answer-3},{answer-4}.
Establishing security policies and procedures, updating your operating systems, updating your applications, and updating your network devices are all good measures to take to help eliminate potential security problems.

examQuestions.questionText: Which of the following tools automatically verifies system files after a reboot to see if they were changed to unprotected copies?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
SFC automatically verifies system files after a reboot to see if they were changed to unprotected copies.

examQuestions.questionText: To open System Restore, click Start &#10146; All Programs &#10146; Accessories, and then what?
examQuestions.explanation: To open System Restore, click Start &#10146; All Programs &#10146; Accessories &#10146; System Tools &#10146; System Restore.

examQuestions.questionText: One of your users claims that their hard drive seems to be running slowly. What tool can you use to check to see how fragmented the hard drive is?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Disk Defragmenter will analyze the hard drive to determine how fragmented it is, and it will allow you to defragment it. There is no Disk Analyzer tool. Disk Cleanup can help you free up space by deleting unneeded files. Check Disk (CHKDSK) can help you find problems on the hard drive, but it does not look for fragmentation.

examQuestions.questionText: Your network has 24 Windows 8.1 workstations. The office manager is concerned about spyware. What does Windows 8.1 come with, if anything, that will help thwart spyware?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
There are many other forms of malware in addition to viruses. While a true antivirus program will scan for viruses, anti-malware programs are a superset of virus scanners and will look for more than just traditional viruses. One program included with Windows that falls into this category is Windows Defender, which is mainly a spyware detector (and incorporates Microsoft Security Essentials, or MSE, with it as of Windows 8 and later).

answers.textAnswer: Windows 8.1 does not come with spyware protection.

examQuestions.questionText: An iPhone user calls to report that his phone has no wireless connectivity. What is the first thing you should tell him to do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A common cause for lack of wireless connectivity is for a device to be in airplane mode. Make sure the device is not in that mode, and do a hard reboot if necessary.

answers.textAnswer: Turn the phone off and back on.
Perform a reset to the factory default.
Check whether airplane mode is on.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 7 workstation will not boot properly. Instead, there is an error message stating that the operating system is missing. How do you fix this problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If the operating system is missing, it could be due to a bad or corrupt boot sector on the hard drive, or the operating system may indeed be missing. If the hard drive is actually OK, then use the installation DVD (you may have to set the BIOS to use the DVD drive as your primary boot device) or the Windows Repair CD. In Windows 8/8.1, Windows 7, and Windows Vista, go to System Recovery Options and choose Startup Repair.

answers.textAnswer: Boot to the installation DVD, open a command prompt, and type Startup Repair.
Boot to the installation DVD, open SFC, and choose Startup Repair.
Boot to the installation DVD, open System Recovery Options, and choose Startup Repair.
Boot to Safe Mode, open System Recovery Options, and choose Startup Repair.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a user with an iPhone, and the device appears to be locked up. You need to tell him how to perform a hard reset. What do you tell him?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If the system is unresponsive, then a soft reset will not work. A hard reset is the next choice. With Apple’s iPhone, iPad, and iPod Touch, forcing a restart on the device is done by pressing and holding the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons for at least 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo.

answers.textAnswer: Press and hold the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons for at least 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo and then let go.
Press and hold the Sleep/Wake button until the red slider appears and then drag the slider to power off the device.
Use a paperclip or pen point to press and hold the indented reset button on the bottom of the phone until you see the Apple logo and then let go.
Open iTunes or iCloud, log in with his account, and enter recovery mode.

examQuestions.questionText: Your company purchases a custom database software package from an outside vendor. You install the client software on a Windows Vista workstation, and it crashes when you try to open it. You remove the software and reinstall it, but it still crashes when you open it. What should you do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When an application crashes, you want to isolate the cause of the crash—it could be a compatibility issue, hardware, or a host of other problems—and solve it. One step to take early on is to look for updates/patches/fixes to the application released by the vendor.

answers.textAnswer: Run an antivirus remediation on the workstation.
Contact the vendor to see whether an update or patch is available.
Enable Software Compatibility through Control Panel.

examQuestions.questionText: On your MacBook Pro, you use the Safari browser to surf the Internet. Yesterday a friend borrowed your laptop. Today, when you try to browse the Web, no matter what site you type in to the address bar, you are sent to a different website. What is most likely happening to your computer?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
This is a classic symptom of browser redirection. The perpetrator has one goal, which is to direct you to websites that he wants you to visit, regardless of what you actually want to see. Removing the redirector might be as simple as uninstalling an application (by dragging it to the Trash and emptying the Trash), or it might require full-scale virus (malware) mitigation.

answers.textAnswer: A practical joke by your friend.
It has been infected with spam.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 8.1 workstation boots with this error message: Security Center service cannot be started. You try to start the service manually, but it still refuses to start. What should you do to try to fix the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If the service refuses to start, even manually, it is possibly corrupt. (It is also possible that you have malware, but we’ll focus on it being corrupt first.) The system file checker (SFC) utility can fix the key system files needed to run this Windows service. If that doesn’t fix it, then follow the steps needed to mitigate malware, or reinstall Windows.

answers.textAnswer: Use Event Viewer to see whether it produced any error codes.
Use automated system recovery to fix the service.

examQuestions.questionText: A user has an iPhone and has forgotten the passcode. He has entered in the passcode several times, and it will not unlock. He turned the phone off and back on, and the passcode is still invalid. What can he do to unlock the phone?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Unfortunately, the only solution to a locked phone (or system lockout) is to perform a reset to factory specifications. That means that all the data on the phone is gone, unless it was synced with iTunes or iCloud (or the appropriate Android equivalent).

answers.textAnswer: Perform a reset to the factory default.
Crack the phone using a backdoor from Apple.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to display the contents of your iPad on a full-sized computer monitor. The monitor has a DVI connector. What do you need to do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
iPads and iPhones are not large enough to have external DVI or other video ports. If you want to project to an external monitor, you need an adapter or an app that will allow you to broadcast to the monitor over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.

answers.textAnswer: Plug the monitor in to the iPad’s DVI port.
Purchase a USB to DVI adapter.
Purchase a Lightning to DVI adapter.

examQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a Windows Vista workstation that could have malware on it. To follow the best practices for malware removal, what is the first step you should take?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The best practices for malware removal is a seven-step process. Identify malware symptoms, quarantine infected system, disable system restore (in Windows), remediate infected systems (including update anti-malware software and scan and remove the malware), schedule scans and run updates, enable system restore and create a restore point (in Windows), and educate the end user.

answers.textAnswer: Enable system restore and create a restore point.

examQuestions.questionText: Recently, users on your company network have been flooded with unrequested emails trying to sell them goods and services. Which solution will most likely resolve this issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Spam is defined as any unwanted, unsolicited email, and not only can the sheer volume of it be irritating, it can often open the door to larger problems. While spam is not truly a virus or a hoax, it is one of the most annoying things with which an administrator must contend. Installing or enabling a spam filter on the email server is the best solution.

answers.textAnswer: Install anti-malware on all client computers.
Install antivirus on all client computers.
Install a spam filter on the email server.
Renew the invalid certificate on the email server.

examQuestions.questionText: Your network has several dozen mobile device users. Several of them have reported that there are areas within your office where network access is very slow. What can you use to test wireless access?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A Wi-Fi analyzer can be used on your network to see signal strength, channels used, and various other network metrics. Any company with a wireless network should have one for troubleshooting purposes.

examQuestions.questionText: You just installed a new sound card in a Windows 7 workstation. Now, the computer has crashed and given you a blue screen of death. You turn the computer off. What should you try to resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The first rule with BSOD errors is to reboot. If the problem goes away, it could have just been a one-time problem. But since you just installed the sound card, it’s most likely the sound card driver that caused the issue. Reboot into Safe Mode and uninstall the driver. After you reboot again, look on the manufacturer’s site for an updated driver.

answers.textAnswer: Boot to the Windows installation CD and start the Recovery Console.
Boot to Safe Mode and uninstall the sound card driver.
Remove the sound card from the computer and reboot.

examQuestions.questionText: An iPad user reports that when he is in a certain part of the building, his wireless connection intermittently drops. What are the two most likely causes of this? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
There are a number of causes why intermittent wireless connections can occur, but the two most common are lack of a good signal and interference. Increasing the number of repeaters, or being closer to them, can address the lack of a good signal. Interference can be addressed by reducing the number of devices competing for the same channel or by moving away from walls or obstacles.

answers.textAnswer: Poor wireless buffering in the iPad
Weak signal strength from the wireless access point
Retracted Wi-Fi antenna on the iPad

examQuestions.questionText: A network user with an Android tablet wants to back up and synchronize her data with her phone. Which service should she use to perform these tasks?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Because problems tend to happen no matter how careful you may be, it is important to back up devices and be able to restore from those backups after an incident. Google Sync is available for backups and synchronization of data between Android-based devices and PCs.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is troubleshooting a Windows Vista computer that is acting strangely, and she suspects that it’s infected with a virus. She has followed the best practices for malware removal and remediated the computer. What should she do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The best practices for malware removal is a seven-step process. Identify malware symptoms, quarantine infected system, disable system restore (in Windows), remediate infected systems (including update anti-malware software and scan and remove the malware), schedule scans and run updates, enable system restore and create a restore point (in Windows), and educate the end user.

answers.textAnswer: Enable system restore and create a restore point.

examQuestions.questionText: You are training technicians on the shutdown methods of an iPhone. What are two key differences between a soft reset and a hard reset? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
Neither a soft reset nor a hard reset will delete all data on the phone or reset the password. A hard reset will work if the touchscreen is responsive, and a soft reset will keep the data of running applications. Hard resets should be performed only if the system is locked up or unresponsive.

answers.textAnswer: A hard reset will delete all data on the phone, and a soft reset will not.
A hard reset will work if the touchscreen is unresponsive, and a soft reset will not.
A soft reset will keep the data of running applications, and a hard reset will not.
A soft reset will not reset the password, and a hard reset will.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 8 workstation will not load properly. During the Windows 8 boot process, the MBR is responsible for loading which key Windows file?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
During the Windows 8/7/Vista boot process, the master boot record (MBR) determines the file system and loads WINLOAD.EXE, which starts the official Windows boot process. In Windows 8/7/Vista, WINLOAD.EXE replaces NTLDR from the Windows XP days.

examQuestions.questionText: You are training a class on the installation and repair of Windows Vista. What is the purpose of the Windows PE? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
The Windows Preinstallation Environment (PE) is a minimal operating system, designed to prepare a computer for installation or to boot into for launching troubleshooting tools such as the Windows Recovery Environment (RE). It is not intended to be an operating system on a computer but rather as a stepping-stone to get an OS installed or repaired.

answers.textAnswer: Runs as an operating system on thin clients
Collects information during a Windows Vista install
Launches the Windows RE for troubleshooting
Repairs system files if any become corrupted

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is working on a Windows Vista workstation. Which command should she use to scan and fix corrupted system files?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The SFC /SCANNOW command checks all system files and repairs any problems found. SFC /OFFBOOTDIR allows you to set the location of an offline boot directory that can then be used for offline repair. SFC /VERIFYFILE specifies a file to be scanned but not repaired if errors are found. SFC /SCANFIX is not a valid option.

examQuestions.questionText: You believe that someone has been trying to hack into a Windows 7 workstation by guessing passwords. Another administrator suggests you check the log files to be sure. Which utility can you use to see log files?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Log files are created to record significant events. Those events can range from security incidents to system problems to just normal user activity. Windows includes Event Viewer for the purpose of looking at log files and identifying problems.

examQuestions.questionText: You power on your Windows 8.1 client computer, and Windows will not load. When you investigate, you notice that the BOOTMGR file has been renamed to DASBOOTMGR. You were the last one to use this workstation. What is the most likely cause?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Creators of malware have a number of methods by which they can wreak havoc on a system. One of the simplest ways is to delete or rename key system files. Then, the operating system will not work. Just as harmful as deleting or renaming a file is to change the permissions associated with it so that the user can no longer access it or perform those operations.

examQuestions.questionText: You are talking to a friend about purchasing a gift, and he recommends a website to purchase it. When you put the website’s address into your browser, you receive a message stating that there is an invalid certificate. What should you do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
An invalid certificate usually means that the certificate that you have (or the one the website has) has expired. It could mean that the site is fine. But it could also mean someone has set up a Trojan that imitates the site you are seeking. If it’s a site you are not familiar with, the best bet is to avoid it altogether.

answers.textAnswer: Visit the website anyway; it’s probably OK.
Visit the secure version of the website by changing the address to start with <u>HTTPS://</u>.
Visit the unsecure version of the website by changing the address to start with <u>HTTP://</u>.

examQuestions.questionText: A workstation will not load Windows 7 properly after a driver was recently installed. The troubleshooting guide says to boot into Safe Mode. How do you do this in Windows 7?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If when you boot Windows won’t load completely (it hangs or is otherwise corrupted), you can often solve the problem by booting into Safe Mode. To access Safe Mode, you must press F8 when the operating system menu is displayed during the boot process. You’ll then see a menu of Safe Mode choices.

answers.textAnswer: During the boot process, press F1.
During the boot process, press Ctrl+Alt+Del.
During the boot process, press F8.
During the boot process, press F10.

examQuestions.questionText: You are concerned about workstations on your network getting viruses. You configure each machine with antivirus software. How often should the antivirus software update its database?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Antivirus databases should be updated frequently (about once a week, although more often is better) to keep your antivirus program up-to-date with all the possible virus definitions. Most antivirus programs will automatically update themselves (if configured properly) just as Windows Update will update Windows, provided the computer has a live Internet connection. It’s a good idea to let them automatically update.

answers.textAnswer: Only as new threats are discovered

examQuestions.questionText: A user reports that his iPhone will not decrypt email. What is the most likely cause of this problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Mail decryption depends upon certificates, and problems can occur when those certificates expire or you have a configuration problem (which can accompany upgrades). To address the problem, try reimporting S/MIME certificates or deleting/importing them from the source.

answers.textAnswer: There’s a problem with the S/MIME certificate.
The user has a corrupt Mail app.

examQuestions.questionText: A user reports that his mobile phone has been experiencing high resource utilization for about a week. What two things should you immediately suspect could be causing the problem? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
High resource utilization can be a telltale sign that a device is running more than you think it should be—perhaps the drives are being searched or the camera is recording your every move. Or, it could be that the user has too many apps open and the device is struggling with available resources.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 7 workstation will not boot properly. Windows starts to load but never finishes. After troubleshooting, you find that devices are not initializing. Which file is responsible for checking for installed devices and initializing them?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
In Windows 8/7/Vista, WINRESUME checks the system for installed devices and device configurations and initializes the devices it finds. It passes the information to WINLOAD, which collects this information and passes it to the kernel after this file is loaded. WINRESUME.EXE replaces NTDETECT.COM from the Windows XP days.

examQuestions.questionText: You are using an iPhone. When is it generally necessary to close running apps on the iPhone? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
Generally speaking, there is no need to close running apps on mobile devices, unless there is a problem. A common misperception among iPhone users is that all apps in the “background” (when they double-tap the Home button) are still running, when in fact they are not. That is a list of recently used apps, and their preview windows are still visible, but they are not actually using system resources as if they were open. Swiping up on them to “close” them is the same motion you would need to do if an app was locked up and you needed to do a force quit.

answers.textAnswer: When the phone begins to overheat
When you are done using them for the day

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 7 workstation will not boot properly. It shows the Windows logo upon boot and then appears to lock up. No changes have recently been made to the workstation. What is most likely causing the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If Windows 7 (or Windows Vista/8) does not load properly, it could be a problem with the BOOTMGR file. That file starts the loading of the Windows OS. It replaces the NTLDR file, which was used by Windows XP and earlier Windows versions. Numerous dynamic link library (DLL) files are required to boot, but usually the lack of corruption of one of them produces a noncritical error.

answers.textAnswer: A missing or corrupt NTLDR file
A missing or corrupt BOOTMGR file
A missing or corrupt DLL file

examQuestions.questionText: You have 20 Windows 7 workstations on your network. You want to create a bootable CD that will allow you to fix Windows boot issues, in the event that you do not have a Windows installation CD available. Where can you create such a disc?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If you want to recover your computer and bring it back to the point where it was when it was new (minus any files that you added since purchasing the machine), you can use the recovery CD set or DVD. In Windows, you can create a system repair disc from the Backup And Restore interface (beneath the Control Panel options for System And Security). The system repair disc can be used to boot the computer, and it will contain the system recovery tools.

examQuestions.questionText: You are training technicians on the creation and use of restore points. Which of the following is not a way in which restore points get created?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A restore point is a copy, or snapshot, of your system configuration at a given point in time. It’s like a backup of your configuration but not your data. Snapshots are created within Windows from the System Restore program. Restore points are created in one of three ways. One, Windows creates them automatically by default. Two, you can manually create them yourself. Three, during the installation of some programs, a restore point is created before the installation (that way, if the install fails, you can “roll back” the system to a preinstallation configuration).

answers.textAnswer: Windows creates them automatically by default.
Windows creates them before a system crash.
Some installation utilities will create them before installing a new program.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8.1 workstation that is running very slowly. When you look at the hard drive, you notice that very little space is available. Which tool should you run to attempt to free up space?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If the hard drive gets to be under 10 percent free space, its performance can slow down dramatically. The Disk Cleanup utility will show how much disk space is being taken up by temporary files, log files, the Recycle Bin, and other items that can easily be deleted. This could free up some disk space. You will possibly need to delete some files as well.

examQuestions.questionText: A user reports that a Word document he needs will not open. Other documents open as they should. He has not made a backup of this file. Which of the following statements is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows comes with many tools to help protect and repair system files and configuration, such as Last Known Good, the Emergency Repair Disk, SFC, and others. But nonsystem files are not covered. The only way to protect user-generated content is to back it up!

answers.textAnswer: The file is probably corrupt, and its contents are lost.
He can use a restore point to get the file back.
He can reboot into the Last Known Good configuration and then open the file.
He can use the Emergency Repair Disk to repair the file and then open it.

examQuestions.questionText: You have an iPhone that has been charging for an hour. When you unplug it from the charger, the phone feels very hot to the touch. What should your next step be?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Mobile devices will overheat on occasion. Sometimes it happens after it’s been charging, but it can also happen because of excessive ambient temperatures or too much use over an extended period of time. When the device does overheat, it’s best to power it off. And, you can often help it cool down quicker by removing any protective case that may be there—and putting it back on later.

answers.textAnswer: Turn the phone off and let it cool down.

examQuestions.questionText: You receive an email warning you of a new form of ransomware. It contains a link to receive more information on how to protect yourself from this terrible threat. What should you do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The email could be real, but most likely it’s a hoax. Worse yet, it could be malware itself, and by clicking the link you will activate it on your computer. Always check a reputable source, such as www.us-cert.gov, www.cert.org, or an anti-malware vendor (Symantec, McAfee, and so on) for information on the latest threats. At a minimum, delete the email and don’t click the link!

answers.textAnswer: Click the link to receive more information.
Check to ensure that your system has a rogue antivirus installed.
Check <u>www.us-cert.gov</u> for information on the threat.
Forward the email to everyone in your contacts list.

examQuestions.questionText: A user just dropped his Android phone, and the screen now has a large crack in it. The touchscreen is unresponsive. He is in the field and needs contact information from his phone so he can call his client. What is his best option to get the phone working again?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If a touchscreen device is not responsive, the first step is to reboot the device. (If the screen is bad enough, he may need to replace the device, but that will not help in the short term.) A force stop just closes an app. Resetting the phone to the factory default settings will erase the data on the phone, which will not help in this situation.

answers.textAnswer: None, he will need to replace the phone.
Reset the phone to the factory default settings.

examQuestions.questionText: You are visiting a customer’s office in a large city high-rise building. You need to make a call on your mobile phone, but you have only one bar. The call will not complete. What should you do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Weak signals are a common culprit behind dropped signals. Before engaging in communication, signal strength on the device should be evaluated. If the signal is low (for example, no bars), then change location (step outside, drive out of the tunnel, exit the elevator, and so forth) and try for a better signal. A low battery can affect signal strength, so keep the battery charged as much as possible.

answers.textAnswer: Wait a few minutes and try again.
Step outside or near a window to see whether your signal improves.

examQuestions.questionText: An iPhone user brings you her phone, and it’s completely frozen. Neither the touchscreen nor the buttons respond. What should you try first to make the phone work again?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A soft reset will not work, because the buttons do not respond, and neither does the touchscreen, so you can’t swipe to turn it off. You need to do a hard reset; press and hold the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons on an iPhone for at least 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo. If the restart does not work, try plugging in the device and letting it charge (an hour or more is recommended) and try restarting again.

examQuestions.questionText: The GPS app on your mobile phone has stopped responding. What should you do to resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When an app is unresponsive, you can do a force stop to close it. With iOS, press the Home button twice quickly, and small previews of your recently used apps will appear. Swipe left to find the app that you want to close and then swipe up on the app’s preview to close it using a force stop.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 8 user wants to see who has successfully logged in or failed to log in to her workstation. What is the name of the specific log she should look for?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Windows Event Viewer utility provides information about what’s been going on with the whole system to help you troubleshoot problems. Event Viewer shows warnings, error messages, and records of things that have happened successfully. It’s found in all current versions of Windows. The three most commonly referenced logs are Security (which includes information about logins), System, and Application.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is troubleshooting a Windows 7 workstation that has been infected with malware. He has disabled system restore. Following the best practices for removing malware, what should he do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The best practice for malware removal is a seven-step process. Identify malware symptoms, quarantine infected system, disable system restore (in Windows), remediate infected systems (including update anti-malware software and scan and remove the malware), schedule scans and run updates, enable system restore and create a restore point (in Windows), and educate the end user.

answers.textAnswer: Schedule a malware scan and run updates.

examQuestions.questionText: Mobile device users on your network are required to use a VPN app to connect to the corporate network when they are out of the office. A user reports that the app will not open for her. She turned her tablet off and back on again, and the app still will not open. What should she try next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If an app does not load, the first thing to try is rebooting. If that does not work, attempt to remove and reload the app. Be sure to check the vendor’s site for any similar problems (and solutions) encountered by others.

examQuestions.questionText: A user on your network is concerned about spyware. What should be installed to help stop this threat?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
There are many other forms of malware in addition to viruses. While a true antivirus program will scan for viruses, anti-malware programs are a superset of virus scanners and will look for more than just traditional viruses. They can scan for spyware, ransomware, adware, and other malicious programs as well.

examQuestions.questionText: A user with a Linux workstation reported that she received an error that says “kernel panic.” What should she do to resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In the UNIX/Linux world, a kernel panic is when the OS crashes, much like a blue screen of death in Windows. This occurs when the operating system detects an error from which it cannot safely recover—rather than one app crashing, the whole system does. First, reboot. If it comes back, solutions usually include updating hardware, firmware, software, and the OS itself. You can also check drives and RAM for errors that might be causing the crash and correct any problems that you uncover.

answers.textAnswer: Close the program that caused the error and continue working.
Reboot the workstation and see whether the issue persists.
Reboot into Safe Mode and run Linux Diagnostics to determine the cause of the problem.

examQuestions.questionText: Your Windows Vista workstation started running very slowly. Which of the following could cause that to happen?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A computer slowdown could happen because of many things, such as hardware failure, an excessively full hard drive, not enough virtual memory, or malware. Rogue antivirus, hijacked email, and invalid certificates will cause problems but not computer slowdowns.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to broadcast the contents of your iPhone screen to a computer monitor. What are two ways you can accomplish this? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
