iPads and iPhones are not large enough to have external DVI or other video ports. If you want to project to an external monitor, you need an adapter, Apple TV, or an app that will allow you to broadcast to the monitor over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.

answers.textAnswer: Download an app that lets you broadcast wirelessly.
Plug the computer monitor in to the iPhone’s video port.

examQuestions.questionText: You install an updated video card driver, and your Windows Vista workstation crashes with a blue screen of death. What are the quickest two options for getting your system running again? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
It’s most likely the driver that’s causing the problem. One of the quickest (and best) ways to proceed is to boot to Safe Mode, which loads a standard VGA driver. Then you can uninstall the new video card driver. The other way is to boot to the Last Known Good configuration. Last Known Good will roll back the system to the state it was in when the last person logged in. So, if that was before the faulty driver was installed, it might solve the problem.

answers.textAnswer: Boot to the Windows installation CD and start the Recovery Console.
Boot to Safe Mode and uninstall the video card driver.
Boot to the Last Known Good configuration.

examQuestions.questionText: Your Windows 7 workstation is having problems at startup. Too many applications are loading, and it is slowing the system down considerably. Which tool should you use to disable programs from loading automatically at startup?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The MSCONFIG utility helps troubleshoot startup problems by allowing you to selectively disable individual items that are normally executed at startup. There is no menu command for this utility; you must run it with the Run command (on the Start menu). Choose Start -> Run, and type MSCONFIG. It works in most versions of Windows, although the interface window is slightly different among versions.

examQuestions.questionText: A user just tried to boot his Windows 7 workstation, and Windows will not load. When you investigate, you notice that several key boot files for Windows have been deleted. What is this a sign of?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Creators of malware have a number of methods by which they can wreak havoc on a system. One of the simplest ways is to delete key system files. Then, the operating system will not work.

examQuestions.questionText: You have one Linux workstation on your network. Another administrator gives you advice on how to enable an antivirus program, and she tells you that you need to type in the commands. What is the name of the interface where you do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The Linux terminal is where commands are typed into. (It’s the equivalent of a Windows command prompt.) Then, the commands are processed by the shell. The most common shell in Linux systems is bash, which stands for Bourne Again Shell.

examQuestions.questionText: You arrive at work in the morning to see that your inbox is full of automated replies and out-of-office messages. The subject line is for something you did not send. What is this a sign of?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Hijacked email is when an attacker sends out an email from your address to your contacts or as spam to others. One of the easiest ways to spread malware is to capture the email contacts of a user and send it as an attachment to all of those in their circle. The recipient is more likely to open the attachment because it seemingly comes from a trusted source.

examQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a Windows 8.1 workstation that has contracted a virus. According to the best practices for malware removal, which two steps are part of remediating the infected system? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
The best practice for malware removal is a seven-step process. Identify malware symptoms, quarantine infected system, disable system restore (in Windows), remediate infected systems (including update anti-malware software and scan and remove the malware), schedule scans and run updates, enable system restore and create a restore point (in Windows), and educate the end user.

answers.textAnswer: Scan for and remove the virus.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8 workstation that is not booting properly. You need to boot to the installation DVD to repair the installation. Where do you make the change to the boot settings?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The BIOS or UEFI will contain the boot order, which is what you need to change. You can set the system to boot to a hard drive, optical drive, network card, or other options.

examQuestions.questionText: You are visiting a website using Internet Explorer, and without you clicking anything, a new Internet Explorer window opens in front of it with an advertisement. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Pop-ups are annoying but not necessarily an indication that your computer is infected with anything. Adware pop-ups usually spam your desktop with multiple (if not dozens of) windows at the same time. Spyware generally doesn’t announce its presence, and viruses generally do more damage than a simple pop-up ad does.

answers.textAnswer: Your computer has been infected with adware.
Your computer has been infected with spyware.
Your computer has been infected with a virus.
The website is programmed to show a pop-up advertisement.

examQuestions.questionText: In the afternoon, you start receiving email responses from co-workers and friends. They want to know why you are trying to directly sell them electronics through a suspicious-sounding website. What is most likely the cause of this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Hijacked email is when an attacker sends out an email from your address to your contacts or as spam to others. One of the easiest ways to spread malware is to capture the email contacts of a user and send it as an attachment to all of those in their circle. The recipient is more likely to open the attachment because it seemingly comes from a trusted source.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is describing a situation he had yesterday where the workstation gave him a kernel panic error and locked up. What operating system was the technician most likely dealing with?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
In the UNIX/Linux world, a kernel panic is when the OS crashes, much like a blue screen of death in Windows. This occurs when the operating system detects an error from which it cannot safely recover—rather than one app crashing, the whole system does. The first step in troubleshooting a kernel panic is to reboot and see whether the error persists.

examQuestions.questionText: The touchscreen on a user’s iPhone is not responding, and the phone is powered on. What should you recommend she do as a next step to get the phone working again?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If a touchscreen device is not responsive, the first step is to reboot the device. In the case of an iPhone, a soft reset won’t likely work (because the touchscreen is not responsive), so try a hard reset. Press and hold down the Home and Sleep/Wake buttons for about 10 seconds, and then the Apple logo will appear. The phone will shut off. Then use the Sleep/Wake button to power it back on.

answers.textAnswer: Remove the battery to power it off. Reinsert the battery and turn it back on.

examQuestions.questionText: On a Windows 7 workstation, you receive an error message that says Security Center service cannot be started, but Windows still loads. What is the first step you should try in troubleshooting the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
First, make sure that the service is configured to start properly. You can do this in the Services MMC app. An easy way to open Services is to click Start and type services in the search box. Then find Security Center and see what it’s set to. It should be set to a Startup type of Automatic (Delayed Start).

answers.textAnswer: Check to see whether the service is set to be started automatically in Services.
Check to see whether the service is set to be started automatically using REGEDIT.

examQuestions.questionText: An Android phone user just received a new Bluetooth headset for phone calls. She reports that it does not work with her phone. Both devices are powered on and appear to be operational. What is most likely the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If the Bluetooth devices have not been used together previously, they need to be paired to work. Pairing is usually a simple process where one device locates the other, a PIN is entered for security, and connectivity is tested. Then the two will work together. Otherwise, lack of Bluetooth connectivity is often caused when a device is not turned on and/or has an improper setting for discoverabilty.

answers.textAnswer: Bluetooth is turned off on the Android device.
Bluetooth is turned off on the mobile headset.
The devices need to be paired.

examQuestions.questionText: Your Windows Vista workstation performance has been slowing down, particularly when it comes to disk reads and writes. Which of the following tools is designed to help improve your hard disk performance?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Defragmenting a disk involves analyzing the disk and then consolidating fragmented files and folders so that they occupy a contiguous space, thus increasing performance during file retrieval. In Windows, there are a few different ways that you can get to the Disk Defragmenter, but the command prompt version is DEFRAG.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8.1 workstation that will not boot properly. After the POST, the screen displays a message saying “Operating System Not Found.” What is most likely causing the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Windows 8/7/Vista use Boot Configuration Data (BCD), which holds information about which OSs are installed on the computer. If BCD isn’t able to find the OS bootstrap files (BOOTMGR in this case), then Windows won’t load. BCD, which is edited with BCDEDIT.EXE, replaces the BOOT.INI file, which was used in Windows XP and other older versions of Windows.

examQuestions.questionText: While driving through the remote countryside, you notice that your mobile phone battery has been quickly drained of power. What is the most likely cause of this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
While apps, usage, and so on, can contribute to power drain, one of the biggest offenders is the search for a cellular signal.

answers.textAnswer: The battery needs to be replaced.
The phone has been searching for a signal.
You need to perform a soft reset.
The phone needs to be replaced.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a workstation that dual-boots between Windows XP and Windows 8.1. When choosing to boot Windows XP, you receive an error message saying that NTLDR is missing. Which utilities will let you repair or replace this file? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
The NTLDR loader file is a key component of the Windows XP boot process, and the system will not boot without it. The file can be retrieved from the Recovery Console, from SFC, or from bootable media (recovery DVD, repair disk, and so on).

examQuestions.questionText: An iPhone user is concerned about her privacy. She wants to ensure that others can’t hack into her phone and track her location without her knowing about it. Which of the following actions will provide her with the least amount of protection to help prevent this from happening?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
iPhones are susceptible to malware, just like any other computer device. Some malware can be configured to perform unauthorized location tracking. To help prevent this, always patch and update iOS as soon as updates are available and install anti-malware software. She can also disable Location Services in Settings -> Privacy -> Location Services.

answers.textAnswer: Update iOS as soon as updates or patches are available.

examQuestions.questionText: A user reports that the battery life on his iPhone is very short. It works for only about three hours before it needs to be recharged. What can you recommend he do to extend the battery life? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-3}.
Tips for increasing battery life include keeping OS updates applied (they may include energy-saving patches), avoiding ambient temperatures that are too high or too low, letting the screen automatically dim, and turning off location-based services. You should also disconnect peripherals and quit applications not in use (Bluetooth, for example, uses power when enabled, even if you are not using it to connect to anything).

answers.textAnswer: Perform a reset to the factory defaults.
Set the screen to automatically dim.

examQuestions.questionText: You have just purchased an Android mobile phone and are concerned about security threats. Which of the following statements is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Viruses do exist for Android; some industry estimates say that 90 percent of mobile-based viruses are targeted at Android OSs. Install an antivirus app and make sure it’s kept up-to-date, just like you would on a PC.

answers.textAnswer: There are no viruses for Android-based mobile phones.
Android-based phones come with an automatically enabled antivirus app.
You should download and install an antivirus app.
As long as you automatically install OS patches, you will not get an Android virus.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows Vista workstation has started exhibiting slow system performance. Where can you go in Windows to find tools to help you troubleshoot this problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Windows Vista and Windows 7 have a Performance Information and Tools applet in the Control Panel. Once in there, click Advanced Tools to see a list of different tools that can help you monitor system performance. A lot of these tools are also located elsewhere, such as Event Viewer, Task Manager, Performance Monitor, Defrag, and others.

answers.textAnswer: Control Panel -> Performance Information and Tools

examQuestions.questionText: You have an Android mobile phone. When you go outside, the screen of your phone is dim, and you can’t see anything. What should you do to resolve the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Check the settings on the device to see whether it is possible to brighten the screen. You can also change how quickly the phone dims with inactivity, as perhaps it’s automatically dimming too quickly.

answers.textAnswer: Power the device off and back on again.

examQuestions.questionText: Before you install a new antivirus program, a technician recommends that you manually create a restore point. What will the restore point do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
A restore point is a copy, or snapshot, of your system configuration at a given point in time. It’s like a backup of your configuration but not your data. Snapshots are created within Windows from the System Restore program. If Windows will not load, Safe Mode can be used to run rstrui.exe, which will open a version of System Restore so you can use a snapshot.

answers.textAnswer: It will create a copy of the entire hard drive.
It will create a copy of system configuration data.
It will create a copy of the Users folder and system configuration data.
It will create a bootable disk with copies of key system files.

examQuestions.questionText: An employee with an iPhone quit, and you are giving his iPhone to a new employee. What should you do to the phone before giving it to the new user?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
When you need to get to a safe state—such as when you are disposing of a device or assigning it to a new user—you can reset it to the factory default settings. To do this, tap Settings and then General. Scroll down until you see the Reset option and choose it. Tap Erase All Content And Settings. At this point, the iPhone or iPad will ask you to confirm the reset, and when you tap OK, it will start the process.

examQuestions.questionText: Your iPad is experiencing slow performance. What are the best two options to increase performance speed? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-4}.
Slow performance is often related to RAM. Look for any apps that are running and can be closed, or perform a soft reset to try to free up memory. Resetting to the factory default will delete all data on the device. You can’t upgrade the RAM in an iPad.

answers.textAnswer: Perform a reset to the factory default.

examQuestions.questionText: You are working on a Windows workstation. When it boots up, it produces an error message that says Missing BOOT.INI and does not boot any further. What is the purpose of the BOOT.INI file?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Different versions of Windows use different files to identify what operating systems are installed and where their boot files can be found. With Windows XP and earlier versions (something you need to know only because NTLDR is an objective), the text file BOOT.INI is used to identify the operating systems installed, their locations, and the boot options to use. Windows 8, Windows 7, and Windows Vista use the Windows Boot Configuration Data (BCD) file instead.

answers.textAnswer: In Windows XP and older, it identifies where the boot files are for the operating system.
In Windows Vista and newer, it identifies where the boot files are for the operating system.
In Windows XP and older, it starts the bootstrapping of the operating system.
In Windows Vista and newer, it starts the bootstrapping of the operating system.

examQuestions.questionText: A user with an iPhone reports that almost immediately after she touches her touchscreen, the screen becomes dark and hard to read. What should she do to fix this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Light can quickly drain a battery on a mobile device, and thus most of them include the ability to dim the display both manually and automatically after a period of inactivity. While you normally want these actions, if the settings are incorrect, the screen can be too dim to work with. Check the settings on the device to see whether it possible to brighten the screen and/or keep it from automatically dimming within a short period of time.

answers.textAnswer: Adjust the settings to keep it from dimming so quickly.
Power the device off and back on again.

examQuestions.questionText: You have an Android tablet. The screen does not seem to accurately sense where you are touching on the touchpad. You reboot and the problem is still there, what should you do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
One option for an inaccurate touchscreen is to clean the screen, but that doesn’t often solve the problem. A better solution is to calibrate the screen. Each mobile OS handles it differently, so check the manufacturer’s website for help.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows Vista workstation will not load Windows. Which file in the boot process is responsible for switching the system from real mode to protected mode?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
In Windows 8/7/Vista, WINLOAD.EXE is responsible for switching the system from real mode (which lacks multitasking, memory protection, and those things that make Windows so great) to protected mode (which offers memory protection, multitasking, and so on) and enables paging. In Windows 8/7/Vista, WINLOAD.EXE replaces NTLDR from the Windows XP days.

examQuestions.questionText: You are working on a Windows 8.1 workstation that has dual monitors. For some reason, everything on the secondary monitor is upside down. What is the easiest solution to this problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The easiest thing to try is to change the monitor orientation. This can be done through Control Panel, but an easy way to get to the setting is to right-click the desktop, choose Screen Resolution, and then change the orientation.

answers.textAnswer: Right-click the desktop, choose Screen Resolution, and change the monitor orientation.
Right-click the desktop, choose Video, and change the monitor orientation.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 7 workstation will boot only into Safe Mode. Even after multiple reboots, Windows will not load properly. Which tool should you use to scan for problems?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
At times, a system will become corrupted to the point where it will only boot into Safe Mode and not allow a normal boot. While a hardware issue can cause this, it can often be associated with a damaged/missing driver. To address the problem, boot into the Recovery Console and scan for problems. You can also choose to boot to the Last Known Good configuration or resort to the recovery DVD.

examQuestions.questionText: A user with an Android phone reports that she is running out of memory on her phone. Which of the following will help resolve that issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Apps that are not used should be removed from a device to free up resources, namely, memory. To be fair, when users run out of storage space on their mobile devices, it’s usually more because of videos, music, or pictures than apps. But apps do take up space and should be deleted if they are not being used.

examQuestions.questionText: On your mobile phone, you notice that you are connected to a Wi-Fi network that you don’t recognize, instead of your normal home network. What is a possible consequence of this unintended Wi-Fi connection?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
When autoconnect is enabled on mobile devices, it is possible for them to seek out open Wi-Fi networks and try to connect to them automatically. This setting should be disabled for all devices because an untrusted connection is a possible place for a DNS or man-in-the-middle attack to occur.

examQuestions.questionText: You are training new users on proper mobile device usage. In the class, you suggest that they disable their Bluetooth connection unless they need it. What is the biggest risk caused by an unintended Bluetooth pairing?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
It’s true that enabling Bluetooth will cause more of a drain on the battery, but that’s not the biggest risk here. When anonymous devices are allowed to connect to Bluetooth-enabled devices, this is known as unintended Bluetooth pairing, and it represents a security threat. Mobile security policies should be created and enforced to prevent this from occurring.

examQuestions.questionText: Your MacBook Pro appears to be unresponsive, and the cursor has changed to a rotating pinwheel. What should you do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
When a Mac cursor turns into a pinwheel and stays there, the system will not respond. Opening Apple Diagnostics won’t work. You need to force a reboot of the system. There is no need to boot into Safe Mode yet; see whether the problem goes away first.

answers.textAnswer: Force a reboot of the system.
Wait for the problem to clear and then resume working.
Open Apple Diagnostics to see what the problem is.
Reboot the Mac into Safe Mode.

examQuestions.questionText: A network user with an iPad wants to back up her data. Which of the following are options for her to use? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
Because problems tend to happen no matter how careful you may be, it is important to back up devices and be able to restore from those backups after an incident. In the Apple world, there is iTunes and iCloud. iTunes is installed on a desktop or laptop PC, and iCloud is cloud-based storage, as its name implies. Be sure that your computer meets the necessary hardware and software requirements to install iTunes or other mobile synchronization software.

examQuestions.questionText: You are training new company employees on the proper use of Windows 8.1 workstations. What are two problems that could likely arise from improperly shutting down a workstation? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-4}.
Not shutting down properly can result in lost data from open applications or corrupted operating system files. Neither option is good. Train all users on how to shut down properly.

examQuestions.questionText: You use the most recent version of Internet Explorer to browse the Internet on your Windows 8.1 workstation. Today when you try to visit any website, you receive an error message that there is an invalid certificate. It happens regardless of the site you visit. What should you do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If your computer is set to an incorrect time and date (we’re talking years off, not just a few minutes), then it can cause invalid certificate errors for the websites you want to visit. It’s never recommended to lower your security settings for the Internet zones.

answers.textAnswer: Check your computer’s time and date.
Refresh your certificate through Control Panel -> Security.
Refresh your certificate through Control Panel -> Internet Options.
In Internet Explorer, set the security level for the Internet zone to Low.

examQuestions.questionText: You are educating network users about software security challenges. A user asks what the best way to avoid spam is. What should you recommend to the group?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
While spam is not truly a virus or a hoax, it is one of the most annoying things with which an administrator must contend. Spam is defined as any unwanted, unsolicited email, and not only can the sheer volume of it be irritating, it can often open the door to larger problems. Administrators can help stop spam with spam filters on email servers. In addition, users can help themselves by not giving out their email addresses to websites that ask for them. Some companies will sell their lists of email addresses to other firms for “marketing” purposes, and then you start to get piles of spam.

answers.textAnswer: Install an antivirus program on your computer.
Only visit websites that have a secure site (that start with <u>HTTPS://</u>).
Don’t give your email address to websites.

examQuestions.questionText: Mobile device users on your network report that the network has very slow data speeds. Which of the following are likely contributors to this problem? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-4}.
Slow data speeds can be caused by too much interference or by a weak signal. If there is too much interference, try changing the channel on Wi-Fi routers to less-used channels; performance should increase. Solve weak signals by installing more access points or by moving closer to an existing access point.

examQuestions.questionText: A client has a Windows 8 computer with a virus on it. She has quarantined the system from the rest of her network. To follow malware removal best practices, what is the next step she should take?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The best practice for malware removal is a seven-step process. Identify malware symptoms, quarantine infected system, disable system restore (in Windows), remediate infected systems (including update anti-malware software and scan and remove the malware), schedule scans and run updates, enable system restore and create a restore point (in Windows), and educate the end user.

examQuestions.questionText: The GUI fails to load on a Windows 8.1 workstation. The Windows logo appears during boot and then disappears, and the workstation appears to hang. What should you do to resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Fixing this issue is just like fixing a missing operating system or missing system files. Using the installation DVD (you may have to set the BIOS to use the DVD drive as your primary boot device) or the Windows Repair CD, go to System Recovery Options and choose Startup Repair.

answers.textAnswer: Boot to the installation DVD, open System Recovery Options, and choose Startup Repair.
Boot to Safe Mode, open System Recovery Options, and choose Startup Repair.
Boot to the installation DVD, open a command prompt, and type Startup Repair.
Boot to the installation DVD, open SFC, and choose Startup Repair.

examQuestions.questionText: An iPad user reports that when he eats lunch in the garden next to the office building, he has intermittent wireless connectivity. What is the most likely cause of this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
There are a number of causes why intermittent wireless connections can occur, but the two most common are lack of a good signal and interference. Increasing the number of repeaters, or being closer to them, can address the lack of a good signal.

answers.textAnswer: The iPad’s signal receptivity is set to low.

examQuestions.questionText: On your network, you are concerned about mobile users accidentally granting unauthorized account access or root access. What step should you take to help prevent these security problems?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Security holes in mobile device operating systems can leave backdoors into which users can get unauthorized account or root access. The majority of these holes are closed by patches and upgrades as soon as they are discovered, so be sure to keep operating systems current.

answers.textAnswer: Apply patches and upgrades as soon as they are available.
Monitor resource utilization and remediate high usage.
Install mobile firewalls on all devices.
Disable location tracking, the camera, and the microphone.

examQuestions.questionText: A user with a new iPhone wants to know how she can change her wallpaper, notifications, and battery configurations. Where should she do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Configurations and settings need to be personalized to the user using the device. Except for apps, choosing Settings on the device usually does this, followed by finding the areas that you want to modify and then making the desired changes and saving them.

answers.textAnswer: Using the Configuration app on the iPhone
Using the Desktop, Messages, and Power apps on the iPhone
Using the Settings app on the iPhone

examQuestions.questionText: Client computers on your network connect to the Internet through a proxy server. Recently, a Windows 8.1 client was infected with adware and a browser redirector. You have removed the malware, and now the computer will not connect to the Internet. What should you do to resolve the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Malware can change more settings than you might be aware of on a computer. For example, adware might be obvious because of the pop-ups and browser redirects, but it can also change the client-side IP settings that point to a DNS or proxy server. Check the IP configuration on the client and be sure it’s set properly.

answers.textAnswer: Disable the network card. Reboot and enable the network card.
Check the IP configuration to ensure it’s pointing to the correct proxy server address.
Disable the proxy server configuration to connect directly to the Internet.

examQuestions.questionText: You use an iPad and an iPhone at work. Which of the following represents the greatest threats to leaking personal files or data? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-2}.
When authorized users access devices through unintended connections or unauthorized users access absconded devices (such as with root access), they can access the data on the device. Every firm should have a policy for protecting data (encryption) and dealing with leaks when they occur.

examQuestions.questionText: You receive a notice from your wireless provider that you are about to exceed your data transmission limit for the month. What type of risk does this present?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Going over the limit on your phone’s data plan is generally not a major risk, other than to your finances. Data overage charges can be high, depending on your provider and service plan.

answers.textAnswer: You may incur a security breach.
You may have to pay high fees.

examQuestions.questionText: Your favorite restaurant locator app on your iPhone won’t load. You closed it and tried to reopen it a few times and it still doesn’t work. What should you try next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If an app does not load, try rebooting (forcing the device to restart, if necessary). If that does not work, attempt to remove and reload the app. Be sure to check the vendor’s site for any similar problems (and solutions) encountered by others.

answers.textAnswer: Reboot the phone and try the app again.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 7 user’s antivirus software has crashed. He reboots the computer and tries to open it again, and it crashes again. What should he do to solve the problem? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-4}.
When an application crashes, you want to isolate the cause of the crash—it could be a compatibility issue, hardware, or a host of other problems—and solve it. One step to take early on is to look for updates/patches/fixes to the application released by the vendor. You can also try to repair the installation through Control Panel. If needed, you can remove and reinstall the software.

answers.textAnswer: Look for a patch or update on the manufacturer’s website.
Repair the antivirus installation through Programs in Control Panel.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 8 workstation that is spontaneously shutting down and restarting. What should you do to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Occasionally, a rogue system will begin automatically shutting down and/or restarting while in use. While it could be indicative of a hardware problem (malfunctioning motherboard, for example), it can also indicate a setting misconfiguration or driver problem. The most likely setting problem is with sleep settings, such as hibernation mode. If that’s not it, then it could be a driver. To begin ruling out possibilities, boot the system into Safe Mode and see whether the problem continues. If the problem does not occur while in Safe Mode, then boot normally and begin testing what occurs as you eliminate drivers/devices one by one (sound, video, and so forth) until you find the culprit.

answers.textAnswer: Check the system BIOS to ensure that the boot order is set properly.
Boot to the Windows installation CD and start the Recovery Console.
Boot to Safe Mode and see whether the problem persists.

examQuestions.questionText: You want to register some .dll files as command components in the Windows 8.1 registry. Which command should you use?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
REGSVR32.EXE, known as the REGSVR32 tool, allows you to register and unregister modules and controls for troubleshooting purposes. It is often associated with Internet Explorer, but it can be used with any control or module. The command-line syntax is REGSVR32 DLLNAME.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 7 workstation that was infected with adware. You’ve removed the adware, but now the computer is unable to connect to the Internet. It is still able to print to a local printer. What is the most likely cause of the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Malware can change more settings than you might be aware of on a computer. For example, adware might be obvious because of the pop-ups and browser redirects, but it can also change the client-side IP settings that point to a DNS or proxy server. Check the IP configuration on the client and be sure it’s set properly.

answers.textAnswer: The DNS server has been poisoned.
The malware changed the computer’s TCP/IP configuration to point to a fake DNS server.
The malware is still on the computer and has infected the boot sector.
The computer has a rogue antivirus.

examQuestions.questionText: You are dual-booting a workstation with Linux and Windows 8.1. One day when you boot up, you get a GRUB error message. What is the most likely cause of the problem?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
In Linux, there are two common boot loaders used. LILO (LInux LOader) is the older one but has been replaced by GRUB (GRand Unified Bootloader) in most instances. The most likely cause of a GRUB/LILO error is a missing or corrupt master boot record (MBR). The method to fix it depends on the version of Linux you are running, but generally speaking, you need to boot to the Linux installation CD/DVD, go into Linux rescue mode, and re-create the MBR.

answers.textAnswer: The Windows boot loader is missing.
The Linux boot loader is missing.
The MBR is missing or corrupted.
The BIOS/UEFI is missing or corrupted.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a user with an iPhone 6, and the user needs to restart the phone. He asks you how to perform a soft reset. What do you tell him?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
A soft reset is the gentlest of the resets. In fact, it will retain data for running applications. Many iPhone users will know the soft reset as the way they turn their phone off and on normally. Press and hold the Sleep/Wake button until the red slider appears and then drag the slider to turn the device off. To turn the phone back on, press and hold the Sleep/Wake button again until you see the Apple logo.

answers.textAnswer: Use a paperclip or pen point to press and hold the indented reset button on the bottom of the phone until you see the Apple logo and then let go.
Press and hold the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons for at least 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo and then let go.
Press and hold the Sleep/Wake button until the red slider appears and then drag the slider to power the device off.
Press the Home button two times, and the Home screen will appear. Swipe up to initiate a soft reset.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician just updated the network card driver for a Windows 7 workstation. Now, the network card does not appear to work. She reboots the computer and logs back in, and it still does not work. What should she do next to resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If you have just updated a driver and the device isn’t functioning, rolling back the driver installation can sometimes solve the problem. To roll back a driver, right-click the device name in Device Manager and choose Properties. On the Drivers tab, click the Roll Back Driver button. The Last Known Good configuration will not work because she logged in again. It will therefore be configured with the new (presumably bad) driver.

answers.textAnswer: Reboot into Safe Mode and uninstall the network card driver.
Reboot using the Last Known Good configuration.
Open Device Manager, find the network card, and roll back the driver.

examQuestions.questionText: On a Windows 8.1 workstation, the user has received a full-screen message saying that his computer has been locked because of illegal activity. The message also states that he can unlock his computer by paying a $300 fine to the government. He reboots and logs into Windows, and the message immediately reappears. What should he do to remove this message?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
He won’t be able to open his anti-malware software because the computer is locked. Paying the fine is not a good option, because this is a ransomware attack. Deleting and reinstalling Windows will work, but it’s overkill. Simply boot into Safe Mode and use system restore to roll back the system. It’s not guaranteed to work, but it’s the best choice here. He could also boot to a recovery disk from his anti-malware provider (if he has one) and try a remediation.

answers.textAnswer: Open his anti-malware software and perform a remediation.
Boot into Safe Mode and use System Restore to roll the system back to an older restore point.

examQuestions.questionText: You have recently installed new software on a Windows 7 workstation. When you try to open it, you receive an error message that the application is not compatible with Windows. What should you try first to resolve the issue?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Sometimes a driver or application will give you compatibility errors in Windows. Microsoft has provided a Program Compatibility Assistant to help you troubleshoot errors and also fix them. To use Compatibility Assistant, right-click the program and choose Troubleshoot Compatibility.

answers.textAnswer: Right-click the application and choose Troubleshoot Compatibility.
Run SFC /scannow to check for compatibility issues.
Run MSCONFIG to see whether there are system configuration settings causing the issue.

examQuestions.questionText: You are educating mobile users on best security practices. Which of the following are the biggest threats to network and data security? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}, {answer-4}.
Unintended connections of any type are not good. When your device is connected to an anonymous device on the other end, who knows what could happen. Disable autoconnect on your mobile devices so this does not happen.

examQuestions.questionText: You have been experiencing power drains on your mobile phone recently. Which of the following is not a common cause of power drains?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
All else being equal, airplane mode will actually conserve a bit of battery life because all the wireless signals are disabled. Apps, usage, and searching for a cellular signal will all drain the battery.

examQuestions.questionText: You just installed a new driver on a Windows Vista workstation, and now the operating system will not load. The manufacturer’s troubleshooting suggestion is to reboot and use the Last Known Good configuration. Where do you choose this from?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
If when you boot Windows it won’t load completely (it hangs or is otherwise corrupted), you can often solve the problem by booting into Safe Mode. To access Safe Mode, you must press F8 when the operating system menu is displayed during the boot process. You’ll then see a menu of Safe Mode choices, one of which is Last Known Good Configuration.

examQuestions.questionText: You have a Windows 7 workstation that will not boot properly. You suspect that the boot sector on the hard drive is corrupt. Which command in the Windows RE will allow you to create a new boot sector?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The BOOTREC /FIXBOOT command will rebuild the boot sector to one that is compatible with Windows 7 (or Windows Vista/8/8.1). BOOTREC /FIXMBR will fix the Master Boot Record, and BOOTREC /REBUILDBCD will rebuild the BCD file.

examQuestions.questionText: You have an Android mobile phone, and the resource usage has been unusually high lately. What can you do to see whether your phone has acquired malware?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Many mobile security software suites have multiple security features. For example, Avast Mobile Security & Antivirus has multiple antivirus and anti-malware capabilities built in. One of the features is an app scanner, which will scan all apps for issues or potential malware.

answers.textAnswer: There is no malware for Android-based phones.
Download security software and use an app scanner.
Download security software and use a Wi-Fi analyzer.
Install the latest Android patches and perform a soft reset. If there was a virus, this will remove it.

examQuestions.questionText: You use Internet Explorer to browse the Web. Starting yesterday, whenever you try to search for anything on your favorite search engine, you are always sent to the same specific website trying to sell you stuff. This happens regardless of what you are searching for. Which two things are most likely to cause this to happen? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-3}.
Browser redirection happens any time you try to visit a site and your browser instead sends you to an alternate site. One of two things is causing this. First, and most likely, you have some sort of malware that is redirecting your browser. Removing it can be as simple as uninstalling a program by using Programs in Control Panel, or it might require virus (malware) mitigation. The second possibility is that the DNS server you use (likely your ISP’s) has been poisoned. If this happened, your ISP would be attempting to fix it as soon as possible.

answers.textAnswer: Your computer has an invalid certificate.
Your computer has malware that is causing browser redirection.
The DNS server has been poisoned.
The search engines you use have been compromised.

examQuestions.questionText: A Windows 7 workstation on your network is exhibiting slow performance. Which of the following tools should be used to check for a potential problem causing the slowdown?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A computer slowdown could happen because of many things, such as hardware failure, an excessively full hard drive, not enough virtual memory, or malware. Run a scan from anti-malware software to see whether there are any issues. Event Viewer, MSCONFIG, and REGSRV32 are useful troubleshooting tools but not typically used for system slowdowns.

examQuestions.questionText: You are consulting for a high school that is deploying iPads to its students for in-school use. The iPads all need to have identical configurations. Which service should you use to configure these devices?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Apple Configurator simplifies mass configuration and deployment on iPhone, iPad, and iPod Touch devices. It is intended for use by schools, businesses, and institutions that need to deploy specific configurations to multiple devices.

examQuestions.questionText: You have installed a new network card driver, and it’s not working properly. According to the manufacturer’s website, you need to edit a setting in the Windows configuration database. Which tool should you use to do that?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Registry Editor (REGEDIT) is used to change values and variables stored in a configuration database known as the Registry. This centralized database contains environmental settings for various Windows programs along with registration information, which details the types of filename extensions associated with applications. Be careful when editing the Registry. There is no undo feature, and one incorrect change could cause Windows to malfunction.

examQuestions.questionText: You are trying to apply Windows Updates to a Windows 8.1 client computer. The update fails with this message: Failure configuring Windows updates. Reverting changes. What should you do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
If an OS update fails, it could be a configuration issue or simply a one-time glitch in the process. Wait until Windows Update reverts the changes and then reboot and try the update again. If that does not work, you can unplug removable media from your computer and try again, or you can try the Windows Update Troubleshooter.

answers.textAnswer: Wait until changes are reverted. Reboot the computer and try the update again.
Immediately turn off the computer. Reboot and try the update again.

examQuestions.questionText: You installed a new anti-malware software package on a Windows 8.1 workstation. Now the system does not seem to run normally. It’s very slow and seems to hang often, and the anti-malware program will not open. You want to roll the system back to a previous configuration to see whether that removes the problem. Where do you do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A restore point is a copy, or snapshot, of your system configuration at a given point in time. It’s like a backup of your configuration but not your data. Snapshots are created within Windows from the System Restore program. If Windows will not load, Safe Mode can be used to run rstrui.exe, which will open a version of System Restore so you can use a snapshot.

examQuestions.questionText: A network user with a Microsoft Phone wants to back up her device. Which service should she use to do this?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
OneDrive is Microsoft’s cloud implementation for end users. It will allow the user to sync her phone and back it up to the cloud. She can also access the data from other devices.

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is fixing a Windows 7 workstation that has contracted a virus. He is following the best practices for malware removal and has enabled system restore and created a restore point. What is the next step he should take?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The best practice for malware removal is a seven-step process. Identify malware symptoms, quarantine infected system, disable system restore (in Windows), remediate infected systems (including update anti-malware software and scan and remove the malware), schedule scans and run updates, enable system restore and create a restore point (in Windows), and educate the end user.

examQuestions.questionText: You are installing a new piece of software on your computer, and you do not agree with terms in the EULA. Which of the following statements is true?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When you buy an application, you aren’t actually buying the application. Instead, you’re buying the right to use the application in a limited way as prescribed by the licensing agreement that comes with it. Don’t like the terms? Too bad. No negotiation is allowed. If you don’t accept the end-user license agreement (EULA), your only recourse is to return the software for a refund.

answers.textAnswer: You can skip the EULA and continue the installation.
You will not be able to install the software unless you agree to the terms in the EULA.
You can click that you agree with the EULA and then provide notes to the parts you disagree with and will not be bound to those terms.
You can install the software but will be provided with limited functionality.

examQuestions.questionText: Your company has a policy prohibiting illegal content on work computers. You have seized a workstation from an employee after finding illegal content. How do you ensure that the illegal material is managed in the correct way and that it is delivered to the proper authorities?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
After the device or data has been preserved, someone needs to keep track of it before it’s handed over to the proper authorities. The specific next step depends on your documented chain of custody. Depending on the situation, materials may be held in a safe, locked location at the office, or they may need to be turned over to local authorities. Have a documented procedure in place to follow, given a situation. Always document the findings and who has custody of the illegal materials.

answers.textAnswer: Drive the computer to the proper law enforcement agency.
Remove the hard drive and preserve it in a locked safe.

examQuestions.questionText: You are troubleshooting a Windows Vista desktop computer that appears to be having driver issues. According to troubleshooting theory, when is the appropriate time to perform backups of the system?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
According to troubleshooting theory, backups should be made before making changes. This is part of the first step, which is identifying the problem. In reality, it does make a lot of sense to perform backups before making major changes to a system. Just in case.

answers.textAnswer: After verifying full system functionality and implementing preventive measures
After documenting findings, actions and outcomes

examQuestions.questionText: You just got off a repair job at a customer’s site, and it was difficult. To make matters worse, the customer was argumentative and difficult to work with. Which of the following should you not do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
One of the golden rules of customer service is, don’t vent about customers on social media. You never know who will read it, and regardless, it’s unprofessional to air dirty laundry. Depending on the situation, it may be advisable to discuss it with your manager or simply document it and move on with your day.

answers.textAnswer: Document the situation in your work log.
Try to put the experience out of your mind and focus on your next call.
Call your manager and explain the situation.
Post the experience on social media.

examQuestions.questionText: You recently purchased software that you installed on your laptop. It worked for 30 days and now tells you that you must activate the product. What will be required to activate the software?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
If you buy commercial software, you will receive a product key, which you will need to enter during installation or the first time the application is opened. (Some products may let you use them on a trial basis but will then deactivate until you purchase the software and enter the key.) The product key might be emailed to you, or it could be located on the physical media if you got an installation CD-ROM or DVD.

examQuestions.questionText: You are fixing a broken printer on the second floor of your office building. When you get the printer running again, you notice that it’s printing off employee paychecks. What should you do?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
IT professionals often deal with confidential, private, or restricted information. Other users trust that IT professionals will treat the sensitive material as such and not spread information. Ignore the paychecks and focus on doing the job professionally.

answers.textAnswer: Take pictures of the paychecks and post it on social media.
Look to see how much everyone gets paid compared to what you get paid.
Ignore the information and focus on making sure the printer is fixed.
Text your friends and tell them that you make more than they do.

examQuestions.questionText: When you are working at a client’s site, which of the following is the most appropriate behavior you should exhibit?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Avoid distraction and/or interruptions when talking with customers. You need to make them feel that their problem is important and that it has your full attention. Distractions can include personal calls, texting or social media, talking to co-workers, and other personal interruptions. Taking notes and asking appropriate questions is part of good customer service.

examQuestions.questionText: You are in the field replacing a defective PCI network card in a desktop computer. You realize that you forgot your ESD strap. The computer needs to be fixed quickly. What is the best way to proceed?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Self-grounding is not as effective as using proper anti-ESD gear, but it makes up for that with its simplicity. To self-ground, make sure the computer is turned off but plugged in. Then touch an exposed (but not hot or sharp!) metal part of the case. That will drain electrical charge from you. Better yet is if you can maintain constant contact with that metal part. That should keep you at the same bias as the case.

answers.textAnswer: Practice self-grounding by bending down to touch the ground before working on the PC
Practice self-grounding by touching the plastic front of the case while working on the PC
Practice self-grounding by staying in contact with the computer’s desk while working on the PC
Practice self-grounding by staying in contact with the metal part of the case while working on the PC

examQuestions.questionText: A technician is troubleshooting a Windows 7 laptop that won’t boot properly. She has established a theory of probable cause. According to troubleshooting theory, what should she do next?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Troubleshooting theory for the A+ exam consists of six steps: identify the problem; establish a theory of probable cause; test the theory to determine cause; establish a plan of action to resolve the problem and implement the solution; verify full system functionality and, if applicable, implement preventive measures; and document findings, actions, and outcomes.

answers.textAnswer: Test the theory to determine cause.
Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem and implement the solution.

examQuestions.questionText: When working with a customer, which of the following demonstrates proper communication technique and professionalism?
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Be culturally sensitive. Some people may have a language barrier that makes it difficult to explain their problem. (Think about how much computer language you learned in your high-school language courses!) Others may have different habits or practices in their workplace. Be respectful of their world. In some cases, using the appropriate professional titles is a sign of respect, and not using them is an insult.

answers.textAnswer: Staring at religious artifacts hanging on the wall
Imitating the client’s accent when speaking to them
Using the client’s title when speaking to them
Laughing at the client’s choice of clothing

examQuestions.questionText: You are practicing appropriate safety procedures as you fix computers. Which of the following are times you should wear an ESD strap? (Choose two.)
examQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}, {answer-4}.
To use the ESD strap, you attach one end to an earth ground (typically, the computer case) and wrap the other end around your wrist. This strap grounds your body and keeps it at a zero charge. Never wear an ESD strap if you’re working inside a monitor or inside a power supply. If you wear one while working on the inside of these components, you increase the chance of getting a lethal shock.

answers.textAnswer: When working inside a desktop case
When working inside a power supply
When working inside a CRT monitor
When working inside a laptop case

unsortedQuestions.questionText: When you begin synchronization of an iPhone to a desktop computer, what type of authentication occurs?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
When synchronizing with a desktop, both the iOS and the desktop authenticate each other. This two-way authentication is called mutual authentication, and it lets multiple services on the iOS device communicate with the appropriate services on the desktop.

answers.textAnswer: There is no authentication required for synchronization.
The iPhone authenticates the desktop computer.
The desktop computer authenticates the iPhone.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Vendor-specific is also known by what other term?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Vendor-specific means closed source. The other options mean the opposite.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which form of social engineering is nothing more than looking over someone’s shoulder while they enter or view sensitive information?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Shoulder surfing involves looking over someone’s shoulder as they enter information.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: From which government agency can MSDS sheets be obtained?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
These are traditionally created by the manufacturer, and you can obtain them from the manufacturer or from the Environmental Protection Agency at[code] www.epa.gov[code].

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following cannot be used to retrieve mail on a mobile device from a mail server?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
SMTP is for sending mail, not retrieving it.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which [code]SFC[code] option reports any issues but makes no changes?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The [code]/VERIFYONLY[code] option tells [code]SFC[code] to report any issues but make no changes.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which switch is used with CHKDSK to tell it to fix errors that it finds?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}
The[code] /R ([code]or[code] /F)[code] switch is used with [code]CHKDSK [code]to tell it to fix errors that it finds.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: The command[code] IPCONFIG /RENEW[code] will renew an IP address for the host from what type of server?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The [code]/RENEW[code] switch with the [code]IPCONFIG[code] command renews an IP address for the host from a DHCP server.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following traits affecting IT support is also governed by law?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.

Law governs privacy at several levels.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a built-in account in Windows 8.1 with HomeGroup enabled?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The four built-in accounts are Administrator, Guest, the initial user, and the HomeGroup user.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the result of pressing Ctrl+Shift+Esc in Windows 7?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
To get to the Task Manager directly in any of the Windows versions, you can press Ctrl+Shift+Esc.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following volume types combines space from a number of disks (up to 32) to appear as a single logical volume to the user but provides no fault tolerance?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Spanned means that you want space from a number of disks (up to 32) to appear as a single logical volume to the user(s). A minimum of two disks must be used, and no fault tolerance is provided by this option.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which option is used with SFC to scan one file and repair any problems that are found?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The /SCANFILE option is used with SFC to scan a file and repair problems if found.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following parameters is used with the CHKDSK utility to locate bad sectors and recover readable information? (Choose the best answer.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The /R parameter is used to perform this operation.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In the call center in which you are an administrator, operators handle a great deal of personal data. What can be used to prevent those in the aisles from reading the information on an operator’s screen?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
Privacy filters are either film or glass add-ons that are placed over a monitor that prevent the data on the screen from being readable when viewed from the sides.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: A user complains that their speakers are not producing any sound. What should you try first?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Always keep it simple when troubleshooting hardware and software. If you can stay seated and check the system tray for muted speakers, don’t bother reaching over or getting up to check buttons on the speaker or to move furniture to verify that everything is plugged in. There’s no guarantee that you will not wind up performing manual labor to get the problem solved, but why start with that?

answers.textAnswer: Make sure the sound is not muted in the operating system.
Make sure the speakers are plugged in to power.
Make sure the speakers are powered on and turned up.
Make sure the speakers are plugged in to the sound card.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Serial ATA (SATA) drives typically include which utility for erasing the hard drive’s contents?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
SATA drives typically include the Hdderase utility for erasing hard drives.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: On which tab of MSConfig can you choose the startup type?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
On the General tab, you can choose the startup type. There are three sets of options: Normal, Diagnostic, and Selective.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the software that allows the virtual machines to exist?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The hypervisor is the software that allows the virtual machines to exist.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the term used for when an attacker attempts to acquire information about your network and system by talking to people in the organization?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Social engineering is a process in which an attacker attempts to acquire information about your network and system by social means, such as talking to people in the organization.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Upon arriving at a customer’s site, you are told by the office manager that you are not welcome there. They are used to dealing with another technician—one who is currently unavailable—and they only want to deal with him. What should you do?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
You should never disrespect the customer or your fellow technician. The best response is to seek guidance from your manager and let him determine how to handle the situation.

answers.textAnswer: Push past the office manager and continue toward the equipment you have been summoned to fix.
Tell the customer that the other technician isn’t as qualified as you are.
Call your manager and inform him of the situation.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: As a weak form of security for your wireless SOHO network, which of the following can you attempt?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
One method of “protecting” the network that is often recommended is to turn off the SSID broadcast. The access point is still there and can still be accessed by those who know of it, but it prevents those who are just scanning from finding it.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Kayla needs to delete a number of files from the command line. Unfortunately, they are marked as Read Only. What switch can be used with DEL to remove these files?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The /f option forces the deletion of read-only files.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: If Automatic Private IP Addressing is being used, what range will a host’s IP address fill within?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The loopback address that is used for troubleshooting and diagnostic is 127.0.0.1.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following options is used with FORMAT to specify which file system to use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The /FS switch is used to specify the file system for FORMAT to use.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What command is used to establish a connection to a shared resource?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The [code]NET USE[code] command is used to establish network connections via a command prompt. For example, to connect to a shared network drive and make it your M drive, you would use the syntax [code]net use m: \\server\share.[code]

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Into which tool was the Security Center rolled in Windows 7?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
With Windows 7, the Security Center was rolled into the Action Center. You can access it by choosing Action Center in the Control Panel or by typing Security Center in the Start button’s search box.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the ideal humidity level to strive for to protect equipment?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Care should be taken to maintain the relative humidity at around 50 percent. If it is too high, moisture starts to condense on the equipment. If it is too low, ESD can result.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a share permission?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The three share permissions are Read, Change, and Full Control.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which command can be used to add and delete computer accounts?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The [code]NET COMPUTER [code]command can be used to add and delete computer accounts. [code]NET CONFIG[code] is used to see network-related configuration. [code]NET ACCOUNTS [code]is used to set account options (password age, length, and so on). [code]NET FILES [code]can be used to close open files.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which wireless technology is most often used to connect peripherals to a mobile device?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology that is used to create a wireless connection between digital devices. One of its applications is to create connections between mobile devices and items such as speakers, headphones, external GPS units, and keyboards.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following commands can be used to find the MAC address of a Linux client connected to your Windows network?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
If you don’t know a workstation’s MAC address, use[code] ipconfig /all [code]to find it in the Windows-based world and[code] ifconfig i[code]n Unix/Linux.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following settings are optional?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}, {answer-4}.
While usually configured, the DNS server address and the default gateway are optional. You cannot configure an IP address without a subnet mask, however.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: On which tab of Internet Options can you set Parental Controls options?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The Content tab contains Parental Controls and Content Advisor, both of which can be helpful for troubleshooting purposes.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is not a recommended security best practice to secure a workstation?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.

Low-level formatting is used to initialize media, and this practice is not a part of the best practices to secure a workstation.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What command is used in Windows 8 to remove all data from a volume?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The [code]Diskpart> clean[code] command will remove all data from the volume.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Carl is using a utility to overwrite the hard drive on his computer and make it “safe” to toss it away. When overwriting, the data that was there is replaced with what?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
A common practice is to replace the data with 0s.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following switches is used with XCOPY to require you to press any key to begin the copy process?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The /W switch is used to require you to press a key to begin the copy process.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What Windows utility is used to prepare a computer to be imaged?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The Sysprep utility makes an exact image or replica of the reference computer (also known as the master computer) to be installed on other computers. Sysprep removes the master computer’s security ID. When the device reboots with the new image, it will generate a new ID.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which switch is used with[code] IPCONFIG[code] to show all the information related to the network cards and not just the summary information?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The [code]/ALL[code] switch with [code]IPCONFIG [code]shows all the information related to the network cards and not just the summary information.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is important when planning for solving a customer’s problems?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Punctuality is important and should be part of your planning process before you ever arrive at the site. If you tell the customer you’ll be there at a certain time, you need to make every attempt to be there at that time.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which utility is used to terminate processes?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The[code] TASKKILL[code] command can be used to terminate a process that has become problematic.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following parameters is used with the TASKLIST utility to see as much information as possible?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The /V parameter is used for verbose displays.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What should be the first solution attempted after a blue screen of death (BSOD)?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
In the majority of cases, a reboot solves a blue screen of death.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which class of fire extinguisher is meant for flammable liquids?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Three major classes of fire extinguishers are available, one for each type of flammable substance: A for wood and paper fires, B for flammable liquids, and C for electrical fires.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which principle should be used with assigning permissions?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The principle of least privilege is that when assigning permissions, it gives users only the permissions they need to do their work and no more.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which installation method overwrites the operating system that existed on a machine and places a new one there?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
With a clean installation, you overwrite the operating system that existed on a machine and place a new one there. An example of a clean installation would be changing the operating system on a laptop from Windows Vista to Windows 7. The user accounts and other settings that existed with Windows Vista would be removed in the process and need to be re-created under Windows 7.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Any software that is built into a hardware device is called:
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
Any software that is built into a hardware device is called firmware. Firmware is typically in flash ROM and can be updated as newer versions become available.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Chuck’s Windows laptop has such a small amount of memory that it runs sluggishly. Walter tells him that he can significantly lessen the problem by letting Windows use a flash drive for memory. Which feature allows this to happen?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
The ReadyBoost feature uses space on the removable drive as virtual memory.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You have been asked to configure client-side virtualization on a friend’s workstation. She is concerned that her computer will not be able to run Windows, Linux, and Mac OS X at the same time. What is your response?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
As long as the computer has sufficient resources to support the host OS and guest OSs, it can run as many as the user would like. Only one hypervisor is needed, and it can manage multiple virtual OSs.

answers.textAnswer: It can’t run all three OSs at once.
It can run all three, provided it has sufficient resources to support all three.
It can run all three, but it requires the installation of multiple hypervisors.
It can run all three, but it requires the use of a Type 1 hypervisor.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Retinal scanners and fingerprint scanners fall into the category of which type of devices?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
Biometric devices are those that authenticate an individual based on a physical characteristic.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the term for electrical tripping that should not be happening but routinely does?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Nuisance tripping is the phrase used if tripping occurs often and isn’t a result of a serious condition.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In Windows Vista, which System Recovery Options menu choice is used to fix problems with startup, such as missing operating system files?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The Startup Repair choice is used to fix problems with startup, such as missing operating system files.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which type of virus changes form in order to avoid detection?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Polymorphic viruses change form in order to avoid detection.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: When you begin to collect evidence, you must keep track of that evidence at all times and show who has it, who has seen it, and where it has been. What is this known as?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
It is known as chain of custody.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What type of formatting is done by manufacturers of IDE drives and must be done before a drive can be partitioned?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
IDE hard drives are low-level formatted by the manufacturer. Low-level formatting must be performed even before a drive can be partitioned.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: You do a full backup every Sunday and an incremental backup at 6 a.m. all the other days. Your system crashes at 9 a.m. on Thursday. How many restore operations will you need to do?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
You will need to restore the full backup first. After that, you will need to restore the incremental from Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What is the final step in the CompTIA troubleshooting model?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
You should always document findings, actions, and outcomes after resolution.

answers.textAnswer: Test the theory to determine cause.
Verify full system functionality and, if applicable, implement preventive measures.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: In the Windows Registry, which of the following is a subset of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
It is HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: To share the [code]C:\SPENCER[code] directory as [code]MKTING[code], which command would you use?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
To share the [code]C:\SPENCER[code] directory as [code]MKTING[code], the command to use is NET SHARE MKTING=C:\SPENCER.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: With which mobile file system are files with .ipa filename extensions typically associated?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
The .ipa filename extension is for iOS app store package files, and it is therefore associated with iOS.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which technology is used to transmit electrical power over twisted-pair cabling?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-4}.
The purpose of Power over Ethernet (PoE) is pretty much described in its name: electrical power is transmitted over twisted-pair Ethernet cable (along with data).

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following are software programs that have the ability to hide certain things from the operating system?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-2}.
Rootkits are software programs that have the ability to hide certain things from the operating system.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which command is like COPY but also duplicates any subfolders?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
[code]XCOPY[code] is like [code]COPY[code], but it also duplicates any subfolders.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: What type of backup stores only the information that has been changed since the last full or incremental backup?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-3}.
An incremental backup is a partial backup that stores only the information that has been changed since the last full or incremental backup. If a full backup were performed on a Sunday night, an incremental backup done on Monday night would contain only the information that changed since Sunday night.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: When answering telephones and providing remote support, what is the most important skill you can have?
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
The most important skill you can have is the ability to listen.

unsortedQuestions.questionText: Which of the following parameters is used with the SHUTDOWN utility to abort a shutdown? (Choose the best answer.)
unsortedQuestions.explanation:
{answer-1}.
